The Hourglass glowed, reversing the Time Flow to normal again and,
"SCREEEEEEEECH!"
The Eternal Warden screeched again, his glowing eyes staring at Nux, prepared to tear him apart—or, well… turn him into a child before disintegrating him out of existence.
The smoke moved, trying to surround Nux again.
Wanting to confirm that the smoke only had the power to reverse time and nothing else, Nux allowed the smoke to surround him, and once again, his body started regressing.
Nux was now sure.
Flicker
He disappeared once again and,
Slash
He attacked, splitting the Warden into two.
Once again, the Warden 'died' only for the Hourglass to reverse the Flow of Time and revive him again.
"SCREEEEEEEECH!"
"Huh…"
Nux noticed something.
The soldiers… something was different.
The soldiers weren't in the position they were in the first time the Eternal Warden was formed.
Something had changed, and very quickly, Nux realized what it was.
The first time the Eternal Warden was formed, Nux took nine seconds to kill it before he was curious about what it could do.
The second time, he took 8 seconds, and that difference in the second made the difference in the soldiers' positions.
A difference that disappeared in a second.
But…
Slash
Nux killed the Eternal Warden again, this time in 3 seconds, and once it reformed, the difference became larger, and Nux finally understood what was happening.
The Eternal Warden needs about 10 seconds of time reversal to come back to life.
So if Nux kills him in 3 seconds, time, as usual, would reverse to 10 seconds to revive him, which would push back the timeline by 7 seconds.
And if…
Slash
Slash
Slash
Slash
As Nux continued to kill the Warden again and again, this time in less than a second, time continued to push back.
"Wait…
So the way to completely kill this guy is to continue till the smoke it is created from disappears?"
Nux wonders out loud.
He looked around and saw a few places that were burned to the ground and constantly releasing the smoke.
"So I need to get rid of them."
He realized.
First, he tried to devour those places and then kill the Eternal Warden, but that only brought them back after the Eternal Warden was revived.

He even tried devouring the places, waiting for 10 seconds, and then killing the Eternal Warden to avoid reversing that much time, but this time, time was reversed to the point where those burnt places existed.
There was indeed no way out.
Nux had to continue pushing the time back till the source of this smoke disappeared on its own.

chapters.title: Chapter 2009 [Trial Fo#!#@ @#$$#]
paragraphs: "Is it done yet…?"
Nux, who woke up from a little power nap, stretched his body and walked towards his golem, who had been attacking the Eternal Warden the moment it revived.

The Eternal Warden was as weak as Nux expected. The only reason he even used the Bloodedge the first few times was because he was bored. Nux, however, could very much deal with this thing even with a normal sword.
He didn't have to use any of his Laws; he just needed to put a bit of his energy and get rid of this thing.
Since it was such a thankless task, he decided to use the Power of Genesis to create a golem who would attack this thing every time it was formed while he went to sleep.

The golem continued to push the time back by 10 seconds with each attack. Nux, who had woken up after a sleep, looked around and noticed that quite a lot of dead soldiers had returned to life. The battlefield that was littered with corpses looked somewhat clean now.
Nux could tell that at least eight hours had passed. However, he could also tell all of this would still take a long time, so this time, he gathered the Energy of Genesis and created another golem.
"Wake me up when it's done."
Yes, he went back to sleep again.
He couldn't even tell how many centuries had passed inside this place now. Without any rest and while his mind wasn't exactly affected, he still wasn't prepared to do something so thankless.
So he decided to sleep instead.
With his eyes closed, he thought about his wives and entered the dreamlands.
Time passed, days after days, weeks after weeks, months after months, and soon, decades had passed, yet Nux's golem still hadn't awakened him.
Nux, who was in a deep sleep, didn't notice, but there was only so long one could sleep for. Soon, Nux's eyelids fluttered, and he woke up from his sleep on his own.
"Who is th—"
He heard a voice as a woman got close to him, confused, but before she could complete her sentence,
Bzzzzzz
The Time Flow reversed, and the woman moved back.
"Huh…?"
Nux frowned.
Bzzzzzz
Once again, the Time Flow returned to normal, but before anything big could happen,
Bzzzzzz
It reversed again, sending the woman even further away.
"What the hell…"
Nux frowned.
He looked around and realized the battlefield had long disappeared. The desolate, dull ground had turned into a lush, healthy ground, and there was no sign of the Eternal Warden around.
"Where am I…?"
Nux questioned. He expanded his senses and quickly found the answer.
He was still on the same desolate battlefield, just that so much time had passed that everything around had changed.
He also saw his golem still killing the Eternal Warden, just that this time, they were about a few thousand kilometres away from this place.
"Huh…"
Nux let out a strange huff.
Then, he turned towards the golem who still stood next to him, prepared to wake him the moment the Eternal Warden died for good.
Nux placed his hand on the golem and started reading its memories, and soon, he got the answer.
During the battlefield, the Eternal Warden was here. However, when his golem got rid of the smoke source using the Time Reversion, the Warden simply latched itself to another source of smoke.
This continued for decades, with the Warden continuously attaching itself to different sources of smoke time and time again.

Nux didn't know whether it was a coincidence or not, but the world they were in seemed to have a constant supply of smoke—be it a wildfire, or some factory producing weapons or other artifacts, even a simple gas stove could be used as a source.
"So you are telling me…
I need to reverse time, by 10 seconds, till I reach the time before the fire wasn't even discovered?"
Nux blinked at the absurdity of all this. Soon, however, he realized something else,

"No, even before the discovery of fire, natural fires are a thing, and considering how absurdly large this world is, it is very possible to have at least one natural fire somewhere, all the time, all the way to… the very end of the world."
Nux couldn't believe it.
"Fuck."
He cursed.
So… he now needed to rewind time until he reached the point before this world was formed?
That could be millions of years!
Honestly, even if that was the case, it wasn't much of a problem for him since this wouldn't be the first time he would witness the lifespan of a world.
Just that… he would be looking at things from a very… different perspective this time.
"Nope, not doing that."
Nux shook his head.
He teleported in front of the Warden again and deactivated his golem, facing the Warden himself.
The Temple had given him his powers for this Trial, they must have some use. There was no need to kill the Warden using simple slashes or a golem; he could try some other things.
After all, he had quite a few ways to kill something and make sure it was actually dead.
The first thing that came to his mind was the Law of Absolute Death.
Very quickly, Black Mist surrounded the Eternal Warden and within seconds, all life was sucked out of him and he crumbled into pieces.
But…
It didn't work.
Bzzzzzz𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶
The Hourglass glowed, Time was reversed, and the Warden revived.
Nux frowned, but he didn't give up. He used everything in his arsenal, starting with the Law of Absolute Devour, then the Law of Absolute Sword, or any other Absolute Law, but nothing worked.
Every time he got rid of the Eternal Warden, the Time reversed and he simply reformed again.
In frustration, Nux also tried to attack the Hourglass itself, but all his attacks simply passed through it, making Nux realize that it was only a projection and couldn't actually be attacked.
Even when he used his broken Complete Law of Absolute Space to create a Black Hole to erase the Eternal Warden's very existence, the Hourglass glowed, and the Warden came back.
In frustration, Nux also tried to attack the Hourglass itself, but all his attacks simply passed through it, making Nux realize that it was only a projection and couldn't actually be attacked.
"What in the hell is wrong with this Trial…"
He sighed.

Racking his brain to come up with a way—from everything that happened in previous trials, he did know there was always a very specific way to clear the trial and brute force was not the way to go—but right now, Nux couldn't come up with anything.
Yes, he was supposed to form a Law here that would help him clear the Trial, but no matter how much he thought about it, he didn't know what sort of Law he was supposed to form.
Usually, the answer was hidden in the very Trial itself, the surroundings, something of significance.
He looked around, and honestly, the only noteworthy thing he could think of was the huge Hourglass hovering in the air.
The darn thing didn't actually exist, it was only a projection that was just… there.
There had to be some meaning behind it, just that…
Nux didn't know what it was.
What Law could possibly be related to an Hourglass?
Was he supposed to learn how to reverse time?

He already knew that. He had complete control over the Time Flow after the First Trial. Let alone reverse, he could slow, hasten—he could do almost anything he wanted with the Time Flow and he highly doubted it could get any better.
'Do I… go against the Hourglass?'
Nux had a thought.
If both he and the Hourglass had the ability to reverse time, did the Trial want him to resist the Hourglass's ability with his own?
Honestly, Nux highly doubted it—there were no records of a Trial like this in the book Tenzin had given him—but…
He couldn't think of any other way either.
'Well, it wouldn't hurt to try.'
Nux shrugged, then, with a wave of his hand, he cut the Eternal Warden in two, killing him in an instant.
Bzzzzzz
The Hourglass glowed and reversed the Flow of Time, Nux, however, used his own Law to Flow once again.
As if it was offended,
Bzzzzzz
The Hourglass glowed again, reversing the Time Flow again.
"Oh? You are going for it, huh? Let's go at it then."
Nux cracked his fingers and reversed the Time Flow again.
Bzzzzzz
The Hourglass did it again, so did Nux, then the Hourglass, then Nux, Hourglass, Nux, Hourglass, Nux,
The cycle continued almost endlessly.
BZZZZZZZZ
The Hourglass glowed much brighter than before, almost as if it was roaring in anger.
"Bring it on!"
Nux didn't back down either.
Yes, he was now fighting a literal projection.
Things long years without your wives do to you~

Of course, no one else was here to sigh at Nux's behaviour. The battle between Nux and the Hourglass continued, Nux used as much energy as it took, using his absurdly high energy reserves. The Hourglass's energy reserves seemed quite high as well.
No one knew how long this continued for, but for Nux, it was getting more and more difficult, until finally,
He lost it and,
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM
He unleashed his Aura.
Yes, the Aura of a Universe was unleashed and suddenly,
The Temple Screen faltered.

chapters.title: Chapter 2010 The Shattering Multiverse
paragraphs: "Alright, fuck it!"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM
Nux finally lost his mind and released his Aura.

The weight of the Universe fell on the world he was in, and everything around him trembled. The air turned so heavy that it became visible, blurring the vision. Cracks started appearing all over the place,
Yes, all over the place.
The Ground, the Sky, the Air…
It wasn't just the world that was collapsing under the weight of Nux's Aura, the very reality seemed to be in danger.
The Temple was alerted.
A strange, red screen appeared in front of Nux, making him frown. Then suddenly, as if one was not enough.
Tens of similar screens appeared right in front of his face as if telling him to stop, and he did.
Nux was here to learn, not to destroy everything. There were still three more Trials he had to clear. He still wanted to learn more about Time and the Temple of Time itself,
But…
The damage was already done.
Even when he was no longer releasing his Aura or even opposing the Hourglass of Undoing, the Eternity Warden wasn't back yet.
Which was strange, considering the Hourglass of Undoing was glowing and buzzing nonstop, meaning that it was working. Nux could also sense that it was releasing the Time Flow energy, just that…
The energy had gotten… much more… unstable.
Crack
Then it happened.
The cracks that had appeared all over the world started widening. Nux was able to sense an external force that was trying to close them, but it was becoming more and more difficult.
There were just too many cracks, and it seemed like they all had their own distinctive energies. It was a sight that made Nux curious, so he didn't extend a helping hand either.
Yes, he wanted to learn more but…
Doesn't this situation scream of something new? Something he could… learn from?
Nux watched everything with interest.
Yes, he was bored.
But he would never say that out loud.
Crack Crack Crack
The things continued to turn to shit. The Temple tried to forcefully close those cracks, but they continued to widen.
Nux was continuously spammed by those messages, until finally, something changed.
[Trial Four: Updated]
[Trial Four: The Shattering Multiverse]
[Make Time meaningful again.]
"What the…"
Nux blinked.
He also noticed that the force that was continuously trying to stop these cracks from opening completely had disappeared. It was almost as if the Temple had bumped all the responsibility on him.
And in return,
It had decided to be a little more helpful.
[You have stepped into a realm that should not exist.
This is the Shattering Multiverse—a place where time itself has been broken beyond recognition. Here, the past, present, and future of countless universes do not flow—they collide.
Battles from long-forgotten wars rage in the distance. Cities that have yet to be built crumble into dust. The sky flickers between infinite sunsets and endless midnights.
Time has lost its meaning, reality is falling apart.
Repair the Time Fractures or you will be trapped in Eternal Paradox.]
Another screen explaining everything that was happening appeared in front of Nux.
"Wait wait wait…"
Nux narrowed his eyes as he read those last words.
"What do you mean by Eternal Paradox?"
He questioned out loud, but there was no other answer.
CRACK
The largest crack around him widened, and from it came down massive landmasses. Floating islands carrying huge castles and other unfamiliar structures…
The sight seemed to be defying gravity or…
Well, any other Law of Physics for that matter.
These huge landmasses settled on the ground, as if merging into the new lands and Nux, who saw this, widened his eyes in shock as he realized something.
The Time Flow in these landmasses…
It was different.
And it wasn't just about the speed or the direction of the Time Flow either, it was… something entirely different.
Something… otherworldly.
No, that was incorrect.
It wasn't just a different world. It doesn't matter how many Worlds there were in this Vast Universe, 'Time' was always constant.
But since the very Time in this place was different than what Nux knew or was familiar with…
He understood what these lands were…
Other Universes.
A different reality.
Two Realities were mixing with each other.
CRACK
However, this was just the beginning.
Another crack that was now large enough started spewing out floating islands of its own. The islands collided with the ground and settled in.
And just as Nux expected, 'Time' there was different as well…
It was the Third Reality.
CRACK CRACK CRACK
Then came the fourth, fifth, sixth…
The number of realities mixed together, forming something that couldn't even be explained. Nux, who was watching everything, couldn't be more shocked.
He was frozen.
Unable to believe what was happening.

Every Law he had comprehended, he could sense another version of the same Law somewhere in the place. Yes, all these realities had their own way of forming a Law, and all those Laws were just as strong.
It was…
Something unbelievable.
[Make Time meaningful again.]
The Trial showed the message, making him remember what he was supposed to do here, and at those words, Nux just laughed out loud.
Meaningful?

Tens of different realities had mixed in here and ridiculously more were forming right in front of him. Time was NOT meaningful here; even causality failed since so many different versions of Time existed here.
How was he supposed to make this… meaningful?
Which 'Time' was he supposed to make meaningful?

The once simple red sky had become a mosaic of colors and patterns, each representing a different universe. The ground beneath him shifted, blending elements from various worlds—crystalline formations sprouted beside ancient trees, and rivers flowed with luminescent liquids.
BOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOM
Nux heard a few loud explosions. Boundaries between different realities were collapsing and converging into a singular, chaotic existence—an existence that should not exist by any means.
What's worse?
CRACK CRACK CRACK
This all hadn't ended.

The cracks were still widening, spitting out more and more realities. Because the fabric of existence had weakened so much, more of these cracks were forming and widening. It was as if all the Universes had found a common converging point and were rushing towards it.
Nux, who stood at the very center of it, gulped.
For the first time in a long while, he…
He was nervous.
This… was not good.
'Repair the Time Fractures or you will be trapped in Eternal Paradox.'
At first, he didn't understand the meaning behind these words. Heck, even now, he didn't know the exact meaning of Eternal Paradox. He, however, was able to sense danger.
The place he was standing at—the Shattering Multiverse or whatever this was called—had become a point that, for some reason, had become very attractive to different realities.
More and more of these realities were rushing towards it, weakening its fabric of existence and overpowering it.
If the Temple's words were correct, and the number of these realities was… countless,
Then this… 'process' would never stop.
Rather, it would only become easier and easier, and it would eventually reach a point where more and more realities would merge with this one within seconds.
Of course, normally, Nux wouldn't have cared about it.
Sure?
From his understanding, things would be more chaotic,
Funnnn~
But…
No fun.
Nux was standing right here.
He could feel how these realities were merging. The 'product' of these realities was dangerous.
The 'Time' had already become something he could no longer mess with—Life, Death, Creation, Destruction…
All the Primordial Laws, or any other Laws—they were very quickly starting to lose meaning.
The weaker Laws he had had long lost their meaning. They were absolutely useless in this place.
Even his Complete Law of Absolute Space, his strongest Law—while it was still strong, Nux could see that it was also… losing its meaning.
Yes,
This reality was nowhere near strong enough to become a focal point between so many Universes.
No reality was.
The reality was collapsing.
If Nux didn't do anything, his Laws, his Powers—they would all become meaningless and… together with him, the Temple would fall as well.
And if that happened,
He wouldn't be able to return.
He would be trapped here forever, until reality collapsed completely for good, creating a black hole so strong that nothing would escape,
Not even him.
And this time, the chances of him reviving would be… quite low.
[Make Time meaningful again.]
Once again, the Temple showed him the message, and Nux paused, stopping himself from falling any lower in this downward spiral.
"So you think I can still fix this, huh…"
He muttered out loud.
"That's optimistic."
Nux chuckled.
He again looked around. This time, his focus fell on the mixed reality in front of him.
And there…
He saw it.
Someone familiar.
'Ah, Father-in-law…'
He grinned.

Something he could… learn from?
Nux watched everything with interest.
Yes, he was bored.
But he would never say that out loud.
Crack Crack Crack
The things continued to turn to shit.
The Temple tried to forcefully close those cracks, but they continued to widen.
Nux was continuously spammed by those messages, until finally, something changed.
[Trial Four: Updated]
[Trial Four: The Shattering Multiverse]
[Make Time meaningful again.]
"What the…"
Nux blinked.
He also noticed that the force that was continuously trying to stop these cracks from opening completely had disappeared.
It was almost as if the Temple had bumped all the responsibility on him.
And in return,
It had decided to be a little more helpful.
[You have stepped into a realm that should not exist.
This is the Shattering Multiverse—a place where time itself has been broken beyond recognition.
Here, the past, present, and future of countless universes do not flow—they collide.
Battles from long-forgotten wars rage in the distance.
Cities that have yet to be built crumble into dust.
The sky flickers between infinite sunsets and endless midnights.
Time has lost its meaning, reality is falling apart.
Repair the Time Fractures or you will be trapped in Eternal Paradox.]
Another screen explaining everything that was happening appeared in front of Nux.
"Wait wait wait…"
Nux narrowed his eyes as he read those last words.
"What do you mean by Eternal Paradox?"
He questioned out loud, but there was no other answer.
CRACK
The largest crack around him widened, and from it came down massive landmasses.
Floating islands carrying huge castles and other unfamiliar structures…
The sight seemed to be defying gravity or…
Well, any other Law of Physics for that matter.
These huge landmasses settled on the ground, as if merging into the new lands and Nux, who saw this, widened his eyes in shock as he realized something.
The Time Flow in these landmasses…
It was different.
And it wasn't just about the speed or the direction of the Time Flow either, it was… something entirely different.
Something… otherworldly.
No, that was incorrect.
It wasn't just a different world.
It doesn't matter how many Worlds there were in this Vast Universe, 'Time' was always constant.
But since the very Time in this place was different than what Nux knew or was familiar with…
He understood what these lands were…
Other Universes.
A different reality.
Two Realities were mixing with each other.
CRACK
However, this was just the beginning.
Another crack that was now large enough started spewing out floating islands of its own.
The islands collided with the ground and settled in.
And just as Nux expected, 'Time' there was different as well…
It was the Third Reality.
CRACK CRACK CRACK
Then came the fourth, fifth, sixth…
The number of realities mixed together, forming something that couldn't even be explained.
Nux, who was watching everything, couldn't be more shocked.
He was frozen.
Unable to believe what was happening.
Every Law he had comprehended, he could sense another version of the same Law somewhere in the place.
Yes, all these realities had their own way of forming a Law, and all those Laws were just as strong.
It was…
Something unbelievable.
[Make Time meaningful again.]
The Trial showed the message, making him remember what he was supposed to do here, and at those words, Nux just laughed out loud.
Meaningful?
Tens of different realities had mixed in here and ridiculously more were forming right in front of him.
Time was NOT meaningful here; even causality failed since so many different versions of Time existed here.
How was he supposed to make this… meaningful?
Which 'Time' was he supposed to make meaningful?
The once simple red sky had become a mosaic of colors and patterns, each representing a different universe.
The ground beneath him shifted, blending elements from various worlds—crystalline formations sprouted beside ancient trees, and rivers flowed with luminescent liquids.
BOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOM
Nux heard a few loud explosions.
Boundaries between different realities were collapsing and converging into a singular, chaotic existence—an existence that should not exist by any means.
What's worse?
CRACK CRACK CRACK
This all hadn't ended.
The cracks were still widening, spitting out more and more realities.
Because the fabric of existence had weakened so much, more of these cracks were forming and widening.
It was as if all the Universes had found a common converging point and were rushing towards it.
Nux, who stood at the very center of it, gulped.
For the first time in a long while, he…
He was nervous.
This… was not good.
'Repair the Time Fractures or you will be trapped in Eternal Paradox.'
At first, he didn't understand the meaning behind these words.
Heck, even now, he didn't know the exact meaning of Eternal Paradox.
He, however, was able to sense danger.
The place he was standing at—the Shattering Multiverse or whatever this was called—had become a point that, for some reason, had become very attractive to different realities.
More and more of these realities were rushing towards it, weakening its fabric of existence and overpowering it.
If the Temple's words were correct, and the number of these realities was… countless,
Then this… 'process' would never stop.
Rather, it would only become easier and easier, and it would eventually reach a point where more and more realities would merge with this one within seconds.
Of course, normally, Nux wouldn't have cared about it.
Sure?
From his understanding, things would be more chaotic,
Funnnn~
But…
No fun.
Nux was standing right here.
He could feel how these realities were merging.
The 'product' of these realities was dangerous.
The 'Time' had already become something he could no longer mess with—Life, Death, Creation, Destruction…
All the Primordial Laws, or any other Laws—they were very quickly starting to lose meaning.
The weaker Laws he had had long lost their meaning.
They were absolutely useless in this place.
Even his Complete Law of Absolute Space, his strongest Law—while it was still strong, Nux could see that it was also… losing its meaning.
Yes,
This reality was nowhere near strong enough to become a focal point between so many Universes.
No reality was.
The reality was collapsing.
If Nux didn't do anything, his Laws, his Powers—they would all become meaningless and… together with him, the Temple would fall as well.
And if that happened,
He wouldn't be able to return.
He would be trapped here forever, until reality collapsed completely for good, creating a black hole so strong that nothing would escape,
Not even him.
And this time, the chances of him reviving would be… quite low.
[Make Time meaningful again.]
Once again, the Temple showed him the message, and Nux paused, stopping himself from falling any lower in this downward spiral.
"So you think I can still fix this, huh…"
He muttered out loud.
"That's optimistic."
Nux chuckled.
He again looked around.
This time, his focus fell on the mixed reality in front of him.
And there…
He saw it.
Someone familiar.
'Ah, Father-in-law…'
He grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 2011 Another Universes.
paragraphs: Nux paused as he saw a familiar man passing orders to his subordinates in a hurried tone.
'Ah, Father-in-law…'
He grinned and unconsciously teleported next to the man.
A wrong move.
"Who are you?"
Azriel questioned as he and everyone around him took defensive positions, instantly pointing their weapons at Nux.
'Fuck…'
Nux realized his mistake as well.
Soon, however, he realized something else.
This version of his Father-in-law…
He was weak.
Rather, that beautiful woman standing next to him and looking at him with a wary look on her face was much stronger than him. Compared to Nux, however, even the woman was quite weak.
She was only a Saint.
'Wait, is she…'
Nux suddenly frowned.
That woman…
Long black hair, crimson eyes, ancient, gothic clothing…
"Lady Luminia…"
He realized.
Another mistake.
The moment Nux said Luminia's name, Azriel narrowed his eyes dangerously. He was prepared to attack, even though he was merely an Emperor.
It was somewhat adorable in a way.
'Oh, how the tables have turned.'
"You shouldn't be…"
Nux grinned inwardly.
Of course, he wasn't here to fight, so he decided to calm the situation.
"Are you… Lady Luminia…?"
He questioned in a confused tone.
"You shouldn't be…"
"What are you talking about?"
Luminia frowned.
"If you are Lady Luminia, then where is Lord Azriel? Shouldn't you two be next to each other?"
Nux tilted his head in confusion, and this time,
"…huh?"
Azriel blinked in confusion as well.
"Have you lost your sight?"
He called out directly.
"How do you even know about the two of us? I have never seen you in my life."
Azriel questioned. He even glanced at Luminia, and the woman shook her head, signaling she didn't know whoever this man was.
"Wait…"
But suddenly, Nux's expression changed.
"You are… Lord Azriel?"
"Why are you calling me a Lord? I do not know you."
"You are Lord Azriel!"
Nux raised his voice, surprised. But then, he tilted his head and frowned,
"But why are you so weak? Have I somehow come to the past?"
"Past? Are you saying you are from the future?"
Azriel questioned.
"It… looks like it."
Nux nodded.
"And you want me to believe that?"
Azriel raised his head, clearly suspicious.
"Shouldn't you, out of all people, believe me the most?
You have a 40,000-year-old monster's memories in your head. You are a relic of the past and your present at the same time."
"…how do you know that?"
Azriel narrowed his eyes.

Nux smiled inwardly, realizing that he was right. As he looked around and sensed their power levels, it didn't take long for Nux to realize what 'Timeline' he was in. It was the time when Azriel Ruinous had just begun his journey and had started gathering Vampires to recreate the Blood Empire together with his wives, Luminia and Ithania.
"As I said, I am from the future. I know everything about you. Lady Luminia, Lady Ithania, your subordina—"
"Ithania?"
"Yes, your second wife. I know her as well."
"What the hell are you talking about, boy?"
Suddenly, Luminia raised her voice. Her expression seemed quite menacing.
"What second wife?"
She questioned, and Nux could swear he saw a tinge of Amaya in this woman; heck, even Azriel looked scared.
"I do not know what this man is talking about. You know I will never choose someone over you. He is trying to form a wedge between us."
The Vampire Progenitor defended himself as he stared at Nux threateningly, and it was only then that Nux finally realized it.
In the story he was told, Azriel met Luminia and Ithania at almost the same time, before he even became a Master Stage Cultivator.
So the fact that Azriel here was an Emperor and still didn't know about Ithania only meant one thing,
Ithania Sky doesn't exist.
This Azriel wasn't the Azriel he knew. He wasn't dealing with the Azriel of the past. This Azriel…
He was an Azriel of a different Universe.
'But why is there an Azriel in another Universe?'
Nux tilted his head in confusion.
'Wait,
What is another Universe?'
Nux questioned inwardly.
To him, there were only two Universes: his own, and the Main Universe.
But now, as he stood in front of the possibility of there being other Universes, he couldn't help but question everything.
"You, state why you are her—"
While Nux was still thinking things through, Azriel called him out.
"Nope, I don't have time for this."

Nux, who had now realized he wasn't actually meeting his Father-in-law or the past version of his Father-in-law for that matter, decided that there was no need to be respectful and teleported away without saying anything.
Azriel and the others, who let an unknown man appear amidst them and then disappear without a care in this world, were frozen stiff.
"He… He disappeared…
And he did it without a portal…"

One of the subordinates who had pointed his weapon at Nux called out. Honestly, more than once, he wanted to attack that man, but something deep in his body was stopping him every single time. He didn't know what it was, but he got a feeling that his end wouldn't be good if he made a move here, so he decided to listen to that feeling and stayed put.
It wasn't just him. The rest of the subordinates, even Azriel and Luminia, the strongest in the group, felt the same. This was also the reason they didn't lash out at him.
"Was he… really from the future?"
Luminia questioned.
"I… do not know…"
Azriel shook his head.
"Azriel Ruinous."
Suddenly, the woman called out, her crimson eyes shining dangerously as she stared at the man who was supposed to be only HERS.
"I do not know who this Ithania that man speaks of is. I only know one thing: if in the future, I see an Ithania,
I will kill her."
Hearing those words, Azriel grinned. He grabbed Luminia's hand and walked close to her,
"If any Ithania does appear,
I will kill her before you, Teacher."
He whispered lightly.
"No other shall ever come between us."
He declared, and Luminia smiled dangerously. She was about to get close and bite Azriel's neck, but Azriel backed down,
"But for now, we need to understand where we are.
I cannot connect to Yrniel. Something isn't right."
He spoke up, and Luminia nodded solemnly as well.
Once again, the two started passing down orders and resumed what they were doing, choosing to completely ignore the man who had suddenly popped in and disappeared.
Nux, who was observing them from afar, remained expressionless.
He had expanded his senses and realized that this wasn't the only version of Azriel in this place.
There were more.
Quite a few, actually.
There was an Azriel who was friendly towards humans.
An Evil Azriel who was hell-bent on killing all races of Yrniel, even the Vampires.
A weak Azriel who was enslaved even after he received Origin's Blood.
And a few more.

Not just Azriel, Nux also saw a few versions of some other people he knew. The Vampire King Alden Sky, Orpheus Bloodheart, Ambrosia Sky, Rislith Lust, Maline Lust, Oberon Feline, Ariana Frostwillow, Faelara Dawnshade, Vulpiana Dawnshade, Ricardus Skyfall, and even… Arvina Skyfall.
He saw them all.
Different versions of all these beings, and he finally realized what a different Universe is.
'Another Timeline.'
Yes, that was what a different Universe was, another Timeline.
A Timeline different from the Main Universe, continuing to grow further and further away from the Main Universe, ultimately forming another, entirely different Universe.
The more of these Timelines existed, the more Universes there are.
This is also the reason the 'Time' in these Universes is different.
'Time' alone was so powerful that it was able to create an entirely different Universe. This was also the reason it is the most difficult Law to comprehend.
But then…
'How are these new Timelines created?'
Nux frowned.
He thought about it for a while, but his mind wasn't able to come up with an answer.
He looked around, wanting to find more answers in the collapsing reality in front of him. He expanded his senses.
If there were so many different versions of the people he knew, doesn't this mean there should also be other versions of him?
A smile appeared on his face as he thought about the possibility of meeting another him. Soon, however, his expanded senses found something,
Not another version of him, but something more…
Home…
Yes, he sensed Earth, or at least a part of it.
Without waiting for a single moment, he teleported there.
It was… chaotic.
Siren Siren Siren
[Please move to your nearby emergency bunker. This is not a drill.]
Loud sirens echoing throughout the city, constant announcements telling people to leave, army tanks moving in the city.
The situation couldn't be less panicky, and how could it not be?
A large chunk of the city was suddenly teleported to this random place, the blue sky had turned colorful, and communications with the rest of the world had disappeared.
Everyone was panicking, except for Nux, of course.
He was standing silently, feeling a strong sense of nostalgia, but then suddenly, he was hit by a man running towards the emergency bunker, and the man shouted,
"Oi! If you wish to die, die! Don't block my path!"
Hearing his voice, Nux finally came out of his reverie. Not wanting to miss this chance, he turned towards the man and desperately grabbed his shoulders,
"Your phone…
How many animes have you downloaded in it? Are the new ones any good!?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2012 Who are you?
paragraphs: "Your phone…
How many animes have you downloaded in it? Are the new ones any good!?"
Nux questioned, jumping on the first chance he got.

Yes, he was happy. Ever since he transmigrated to this world, he met the wives he loves so much, he had a body and a system with potential far greater than anyone else. Compared to the nobody he was in his previous life, in this life, he felt like he had a purpose, a goal.
He felt like he was… something.
But be that as it may, in this life, he did one thing.
Culture.
Just thinking about how many animes, mangas, and novels he must have missed in these thousands of years, his heart bled.
He wanted to catch up with everything and embrace the new, evolved culture, but then,
"Have you lost your fucking mind!? Do you not see what is happening!?"
The man he had blocked snapped.
The world was about to end and anime was what this bastard was talking about!?
It made him remember another man, a much more hateful, carefree, and lifeless bastard who was now gone for good.
"Oi! Jason! The fuck are you doing talking to a cosplayer!? Come!"
Suddenly, the man heard a shout. He looked behind and saw his boss, who seemed to be waiting for him.

A gesture that any naïve man might believe grand, thinking that the bastard cared about his subordinates, but Jason knew that wasn't the case. Jason knew that stingy bastard only wanted him by his side so he could protect him in case something happened.
'Like hell I will protect him.'
Jason snorted in his head, then just to spite his boss, he shouted back,
"He doesn't look like a cosplayer! He is too fit for that! Most of them are NEETs with no lives! Most of those cosplaying events have become dating sites for these weirdos!"

"Have you lost your fucking mind!? Who cares if a cosplayer is fit or not!? He must go to the gym or something, no-lifers have too much time on their hands for things like that anyway! If you do not return, I'll tell them I am the last person and close the bunker!"
'Tsk, bastard.'
Jason snorted at those words and,
"I am coming!"
He rushed back, slapping Nux's arms away from his shoulders.
Just as Jason and his boss were about to get away, suddenly, their bodies started floating in the air.𝘧𝓇ℯ𝑒𝓌𝑒𝑏𝓃𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘭.𝒸ℴ𝓂
"H-Huh…? W-W-What the hell is happening!?"
The boss questioned, panicking.
"Jason! What the fuck is happening!?"
He raised his voice, but this time, Jason snapped.
"How the fuck am I supposed to know, you dumbass!?"
"Y-You! How dare you talk to me like that!? I will take away your ince—"
"Take your incentives and shove it in your ass! I quit! I fucking quit!"
"NO! You don't quit! I am firing you! I AM firing you!"
"Yo—"
The two just continued cursing each other, however, as their bodies dragged back towards Nux, they both froze.
"You…"
Nux called out.
"A-Are you the one doing t-this?"
The boss questioned.
Jason, however, was a step ahead.

"B-Bro, I am sorry if I was rude to you before, you wanted to watch animes, didn't you? I-I don't have it on my phone, but I am sure my son has downloaded a few on my laptop. I don't have it with me right now, b-but I am sure I can find it after I retu—"
Yes, he had started bribing Nux with animes, but then,
"Jason Spector…"
Nux said a name.
Jason's eyes widened.
"H-How do you know my full n-name?"
He questioned, but Nux didn't answer. He had more questions of his own.
"What year is it?"
"Y-Year?"
"Answer the question."
Jason answered and suddenly, Nux's expression changed.
It was the year he died as James and transmigrated into Nux's body and this man…

He was Jason Spector, a colleague who constantly looked down on him, made fun of him, and made jokes at his expense to be more likeable in the office. He was also quite good at licking his boss's ass.
Yes, the same boss he was currently fighting with.
These two people…

He had already disappeared to god knows where.

chapters.title: Chapter ﻿2013 A thousand more.
paragraphs: "I really do not exist here..."
Nux muttered out loud as he went to his apartment.

Yes, since the entire city had been transported here, his previous home was here as well. Nux thought that maybe, in this timeline, 'he' was working somewhere else, so Jason and his boss didn't know him.
But even when he returned to his apartment, he realized it didn't belong to him—it never belonged to him. He even checked the city records and searched for his name, but...
Nothing.
He didn't find anything.
He didn't exist in this world.
Nux's expression turned heavy.
He expanded his senses even further, trying to find more versions of himself, but again, no matter how much he tried, he couldn't find anything.
He found people he had interacted with—more than once, actually. All different from each other—but he didn't find 'him'.
And not just him.
He didn't find his wives either.
He and his wives did not exist in any of these realities.
'Wait...'
Suddenly, Nux's expression changed as he realized something. He closed his eyes and expanded his senses. This time, he searched for Yrniel—a Yrniel where Progenitors roamed free.
And he found one such version.

A Yrniel that had just come into existence, where the Progenitors were still growing and facing the Magic Beasts. He teleported to the world, and very quickly, his eyes fell on Azriel Origin, the Vampire Progenitor.
However, as he glanced at the Dragon Progenitor standing next to him, he frowned.
Wanting to confirm what he was thinking, he grabbed the being and started reading his memories. Azriel tried to protect his friend, but Nux grabbed him and started reading his memories as well.
And very quickly, he realized it...
The Dragon Progenitor...
His name was Valtharion Origin.
Yes, Dagahra or Saphira Origin didn't exist in this world—neither did Faustina or Caesar. None of Yrniel's Progenitors except for Azriel existed.
Not just in this reality, but in any of the realities Nux was seeing.
"All the beings connected to me... no longer live in any other realities."
Nux finally realized it.
When he devours a being from a universe, he isn't just devouring them from one universe—he is erasing their existence from every single universe.
The reason he couldn't find any other Nux was because...
No other Nux existed.
The universe inside his body—since it wasn't formed like how the rest of the universes were formed—was not connected to any of them.
In this vast, endless multiverse...
Nux was a sole existence that is... an outsider.
An anomaly.
A multiverse anomaly.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞
"Holy..."

Nux gulped audibly. The revelation opened up a whole new perception of things. It was as if he was exploring an entirely different world, getting answers to the questions he was never able to find answers to.
Questions like...
Why was he never able to form a Law related to Time?
Aeliana had the Law of Absolute Control—a Law that did allow him to control Time. It could very much be used to derive a Law related to time—yes, a weaker Law, but a Law nonetheless.

Not just her—Rune's Law was related to Time as well. Amaya's Law could devour Time. Lyriana's Law could freeze Time. Heck, Vulpiana's Law was directly related to time and allowed him to create Time Rifts. Some of the other beings he had devoured had Laws related to Time as well—again, very weak, but they still existed.
Yet...
Nux's Universe never accepted those Laws.
At first, Nux believed it was because the Laws he had were too weak—just like how Thyra's Law's connection with Death was too weak to be accepted by the Universe—but deep down, he knew he was wrong.

His explanation didn't make sense. This was nowhere similar to Thyra's case. Unlike with Thyra's case, he had multiple Laws related to Time. In theory, he should have been able to form a stronger Time Law that should be accepted by his Universe if he combined all those Laws, but...
He couldn't.
Something didn't make sense here.
And finally, after thinking about this for centuries, Nux finally got an answer.
He was never able to form a Law related to time because his Universe never had a Time.
Time wasn't just one of the Primordial Energies—it was something... much more.
It was the only force capable of forming multiple universes.
A universe forms when a 'Time' from another universe 'branches' and extends further and further away from the main universe.
So in theory, every single universe ever formed already had its own 'Time'—a branched version of another universe's Time.
Every universe but Nux's.
His Universe wasn't a 'branched' universe like others.
It was a universe independent of the rest of the universes. The very concept of Time didn't exist in his Universe.

Yes, his Universe didn't have any of the other required concepts either, but that was not as big of a problem. Nux could always comprehend the rest of the concepts and add those to his Universe, but Time...
Time was different.
Each universe had its own unique Time.
Time was like an identity to a universe. If Nux 'copied' another universe's Time, the two universes could clash—it would never work.
So in order to add a force of Time to his Universe, instead of comprehending Time...
He needed to... create it.

Yes, Nux was never capable of forming a Time Law to begin with. Even if he read Tenzin's memory and comprehended his Law, his own Universe would never be able to accept it. Even the Laws he had comprehended in the Temple of Time—although they might work inside the Temple—the moment he returned, his Universe would reject them, and they would become useless again, simply because his Universe had no Time for him to manipulate in any way.
'Fuck...'
Nux cursed in his head.
"How is one supposed to create time?"
He questioned out loud.
But then,
[Make Time meaningful again.]
The Temple's screen appeared in front of him again.
'Right...'
Nux realized it.
He was still in a zone that was about to be ruined. More and more realities were opening and merging with this one every second.
He needed to somehow save it.
How was he supposed to do that?
Nux had no clue. He, however, did know one thing.

He needed to create time, and for that, he needed to understand Time—not just 'one' Time. He needed to understand 'different' types of Time. He needed to understand what differentiates one type of time from another and somehow... create a time unique to his own Universe.
Nux felt his head aching just as he thought about it, but at the same time, he also realized that he was incredibly lucky.
Everything that happened here was purely coincidental.

He had only come here to form a Law. If all had gone according to plan, he would have cleared all six Trials, formed a strong Time Law, only to realize everything he had done so far was absolutely useless.

But instead, he had released his aura, weakened the existential boundary of whatever place he was in to the point all the universes started overlapping here, shattering the Balance of the Multiverse in the process—until finally, he fell into this situation.

Where he was supposed to differentiate different 'Times' that had overlapped with each other, 'solve' the overlapping problem, set the timelines back in their original form again, and close the cracks in order to prevent this place from complete destruction.
It was honestly scary, considering how this was exactly what he needed right now before he even attempted to create his own Time.
'Alright, let's begin...'
Nux muttered as he stared at one of the cracks that was still expanding without stopping, and he teleported next to it.
Again, he had no idea what he was supposed to do. He just... had to do something.
'Haaahh...'
Nux sighed as he stared at the crack again. It was one of the smaller ones—just a thin little line in the large sky, glowing faintly, buzzing with unstable energy.
Normally, Nux wouldn't have cared, but now, he could feel the pressure behind it.

The crack was carrying the weight of another universe trying to push its way in. If it widened further, the universe on the other side would bleed into this one, forcing itself where it didn't belong.
Something that had already happened more than once and could not be allowed to happen again.
This place could not become any more chaotic, or else...
It would shatter.
Nux hovered closer and raised his hand, touching the edge of the crack. The moment his fingers brushed its surface, his vision blurred.
"Father..."
He heard a voice.
He turned around and saw a barely meter-tall being with three eyes and yellow skin holding his hand with a big smile on his face.
He looked around and realized he was walking on a golden bridge under two suns. People dressed in red armor bowed to him.
"Father, don't worry! We will win the War!"
The child he was walking with exclaimed excitedly.
"Huh? What War...?"
Soon, however, Nux's expression changed. He couldn't lose himself.
None of this was real.
None of this was his.
It was the other universe—the other side of the crack—something he was trying to keep away.
"Haaaahhh!!"
Nux forcefully pulled back, gasping.
'I need to separate it.'
But how?
Nux had one idea. He already understood the 'Time' of the place he was in. Now he just needed to understand the Time of this timeline and differentiate the two.
With that thought in his mind, Nux took a deep breath, extended his hand back to the crack, returned to the universe he was in, and then...
He watched.
Years passed.
Nux saw how time flowed in that foreign universe—how people lived, how events unfolded, how their history moved. He started comprehending their Time.
And slowly, he began to see how this foreign Time was connecting onto the one he was in.
It wasn't random—it was looking for similar points, shared moments it could connect to. That's how they began merging.
So Nux started forcefully pulling them apart.
He isolated events that didn't belong together. Played with causalities and shifted moments that were trying to overlap.
He used his own understanding of Time to build a boundary between what was and what... wasn't.

It was like separating two different songs playing at once. At first, they clashed, but as he removed the similar tones and shifted them to different times where they did not overlap with each other, the noise began to clear.
Decades passed, and during this time, thousands of more cracks had appeared. Hundreds had grown completely, and different universes coming from them had merged with where Nux was.
But the crack Nux was working on remained the same.
And finally, on a fateful day, when Nux 'removed' the final connecting point...
The crack trembled as it began to shrink.
The light dimmed.
The pressure it was radiating faded.
And finally, the crack closed.
Yep, one was done.
"Time for a thousand more...
Easy peasy!"
Nux smiled brightly.
Yes, he was already losing his mind.

Even if he read Tenzin's memory and comprehended his Law, his own Universe would never be able to accept it.

Even the Laws he had comprehended in the Temple of Time—although they might work inside the Temple—the moment he returned, his Universe would reject them, and they would become useless again, simply because his Universe had no Time for him to manipulate in any way.
'Fuck...'
Nux cursed in his head.
"How is one supposed to create time?"
He questioned out loud.
But then,
[Make Time meaningful again.]
The Temple's screen appeared in front of him again.
'Right...'
Nux realized it.
He was still in a zone that was about to be ruined.
More and more realities were opening and merging with this one every second.
He needed to somehow save it.
How was he supposed to do that?
Nux had no clue.
He, however, did know one thing.
He needed to create time, and for that, he needed to understand Time—not just 'one' Time.
He needed to understand 'different' types of Time.
He needed to understand what differentiates one type of time from another and somehow... create a time unique to his own Universe.
Nux felt his head aching just as he thought about it, but at the same time, he also realized that he was incredibly lucky.
Everything that happened here was purely coincidental.
He had only come here to form a Law.
If all had gone according to plan, he would have cleared all six Trials, formed a strong Time Law, only to realize everything he had done so far was absolutely useless.

But instead, he had released his aura, weakened the existential boundary of whatever place he was in to the point all the universes started overlapping here, shattering the Balance of the Multiverse in the process—until finally, he fell into this situation.

Where he was supposed to differentiate different 'Times' that had overlapped with each other, 'solve' the overlapping problem, set the timelines back in their original form again, and close the cracks in order to prevent this place from complete destruction.
It was honestly scary, considering how this was exactly what he needed right now before he even attempted to create his own Time.
'Alright, let's begin...'
Nux muttered as he stared at one of the cracks that was still expanding without stopping, and he teleported next to it.
Again, he had no idea what he was supposed to do.
He just... had to do something.
'Haaahh...'
Nux sighed as he stared at the crack again.
It was one of the smaller ones—just a thin little line in the large sky, glowing faintly, buzzing with unstable energy.
Normally, Nux wouldn't have cared, but now, he could feel the pressure behind it.
The crack was carrying the weight of another universe trying to push its way in.
If it widened further, the universe on the other side would bleed into this one, forcing itself where it didn't belong.
Something that had already happened more than once and could not be allowed to happen again.
This place could not become any more chaotic, or else...
It would shatter.
Nux hovered closer and raised his hand, touching the edge of the crack.
The moment his fingers brushed its surface, his vision blurred.
"Father..."
He heard a voice.
He turned around and saw a barely meter-tall being with three eyes and yellow skin holding his hand with a big smile on his face.
He looked around and realized he was walking on a golden bridge under two suns.
People dressed in red armor bowed to him.
"Father, don't worry!
We will win the War!"
The child he was walking with exclaimed excitedly.
"Huh?
What War...?"
Soon, however, Nux's expression changed.
He couldn't lose himself.
None of this was real.
None of this was his.
It was the other universe—the other side of the crack—something he was trying to keep away.
"Haaaahhh!!"
Nux forcefully pulled back, gasping.
'I need to separate it.'
But how?
Nux had one idea.
He already understood the 'Time' of the place he was in.
Now he just needed to understand the Time of this timeline and differentiate the two.
With that thought in his mind, Nux took a deep breath, extended his hand back to the crack, returned to the universe he was in, and then...
He watched.
Years passed.
Nux saw how time flowed in that foreign universe—how people lived, how events unfolded, how their history moved.
He started comprehending their Time.
And slowly, he began to see how this foreign Time was connecting onto the one he was in.
It wasn't random—it was looking for similar points, shared moments it could connect to.
That's how they began merging.
So Nux started forcefully pulling them apart.
He isolated events that didn't belong together.
Played with causalities and shifted moments that were trying to overlap.
He used his own understanding of Time to build a boundary between what was and what... wasn't.
It was like separating two different songs playing at once.
At first, they clashed, but as he removed the similar tones and shifted them to different times where they did not overlap with each other, the noise began to clear.
Decades passed, and during this time, thousands of more cracks had appeared.
Hundreds had grown completely, and different universes coming from them had merged with where Nux was.
But the crack Nux was working on remained the same.
And finally, on a fateful day, when Nux 'removed' the final connecting point...
The crack trembled as it began to shrink.
The light dimmed.
The pressure it was radiating faded.
And finally, the crack closed.
Yep, one was done.
"Time for a thousand more...
Easy peasy!"
Nux smiled brightly.
Yes, he was already losing his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 2014 Hello? Mr. Temple? Is anyone there?
paragraphs: "Alright, this one was faster than before."
Nux muttered as he stretched his body after closing the tenth crack.
But…
Even though he had been working without any breaks from the beginning, the number of cracks hadn't gone down but had increased instead.
The rate at which he was closing them was far lower than the rate at which they were being formed, it couldn't even be compared.
Even when Nux had started closing larger cracks first, it still wasn't helping.
More and more Realities were merging with the current one, the fabric of existence had been getting weaker and weaker, and reality was close to collapsing altogether.
Yes, things were bad.

But on the bright side, the speed at which Nux was closing the portals was increasing. By now, he had already gotten used to sensing two different 'times' and it only took him a few years to find the 'joining' points.
Points that he needed to forcefully pull apart.
The process was getting quicker and quicker, and as more time passed, Nux's speed increased even further.
In just a hundred more years, the speed at which Nux was closing these cracks had become similar to the speed at which these things were opening.
Also, since every time he closed an already opened crack, the reality that came from that crack returned to its original timeline—

What's more? Since Nux was only dealing with already opened cracks and it took a lot of time for the new cracks to be wide enough for the reality from the other side to come and merge with the main reality, the number of realities mixed with the main reality was reducing, reinforcing the fabric of existence, making it difficult for the new cracks to form.
Yes, Nux had finally begun making progress.

One by one, he continued dealing with mixed realities, protecting millions in the process. He didn't even know how many versions of Azriel he had saved from being killed by their own alternative versions.
Heck, some of the evil Azriels had banded together to 'take over the new world', a ridiculous notion, but it seemed like not every Azriel was a good Azriel.

Other people he knew had joined the mixed reality war as well, even some versions of Arvina were participating actively, just that most of Arvina's versions were quite weak, so they weren't able to survive for long.

Actually, the one who was making the most progress after versions of Azriel was Faelara. The Fox's versions seemed as talented as her. Some of her evil versions were even stronger than Azriel herself and with their mastery over space, she had turned the battlefield into a nightmare.
The only ones who were actually able to stop evil Faelaras were the good Faelaras who seemed to be fighting to protect the world and their people.
They were… quite charming.
If Nux wasn't desperate to end things quickly and return to his wives, he might have made his move and taken them with him.
All in all, it was very interesting to watch different versions of people he knew battle each other.
What's intriguing was that he wasn't seeing anyone too strong.
Yes, while the realities on the other side of the cracks were indeed complete Universes, there were no signs of Supreme Entities like Infinities making an appearance from any of the Universes.
Let alone an Infinity, Nux hadn't even seen a Primordial. The strongest being in here was a Divine and even that too had only appeared after a long, long time.

It seemed like there was some force that was resisting the complete collision between two realities, and while the other Universes were still able to bleed into this one, only a weaker part of it—the one somehow connected to Nux—could be sent here.
Another thing to note, however, was that whatever it was that was resisting the complete reality collapse, it was getting weaker.
At first, the strongest being here was only an Early Saint, but now, Nux had seen Peak Divines.
Heck, he had also seen a Peak Level Divine Stage Azriel with his ridiculous Law of Absolute, and that being was a complete monster.
So much so that if Nux was actually a Divine, he might have used that chance to spar with him, and even with all the advantage he had, it wouldn't have been an easy fight.
'I still would have won though.'
Nux muttered in his head.

Yes, even when the entire reality was collapsing, he was still being competitive. Heck, he was even considering purposefully weakening the fabric of reality and letting a Primordial Level Azriel appear, just to fight him.
Of course, as soon as that thought appeared, he quickly threw it out. He still needed to return to his wives. It had been such a long time that even someone like him was getting sick of it.
Therefore, Nux continued to close the cracks.
Another century passed and by now, the speed at which Nux was closing the cracks had become ridiculous.
All of the merged realities were gone, only three unopened cracks were left, and the fabric of existence had become so strong that it required more than 10 years just for a crack to form.
Yes, it was all over.
Nux appeared next to the third-last crack, placed his hand over it, entered the other side, comprehended their 'Time' in a day, found the 'shared moments' or what he now liked to call 'knots'.

The more knots there were between the two realities, the larger the crack. And since these were all unopened cracks, the number of knots wasn't much, barely a few hundred. With Nux's speed now, he needed about a day to untie a knot, so within a year, a small, unopened crack could be closed.
And two years later, Nux closed the final knot and then,
[Trial Four: Complete]
He saw a familiar screen and,
"Haaaahhh…"
He sighed in relief.
For a moment, he closed his eyes, exhausted. He sensed the world around him and realized that he was now able to sense the very fabric of existence that he didn't even know existed before.
Not just that, his grasp over Time itself had become so strong that it was almost ridiculous. How could it not?

He had understood the concept of Time of so many different Universes that all other Laws in his mind felt vague now. Even he, someone with such a highly functional mind, needed some time to slow down his thought process and return to his normal state.
Yes, that was what this trial had done to him.
It was… overwhelming.
Nux kept his eyes closed for the next few days, then, once he felt that he was ready, he opened his eyes and,
"So? What's next?"
He questioned, feeling confident.
He, however, was only met with silence.
"Hello? Mr. Temple? Is anyone there?
I was told there were Six Trials here. I have only cleared Four. Where are the rest of them?"
He questioned out loud.
Of course, he still hadn't forgotten the fact that he cannot form any Time-related Law anyway if he doesn't create Time on his own, but he was still curious about the next Trials.
And honestly…
Nux was pretty confident the next two Trials would be a breeze, especially after what he had been through.
So…
Since he was already here,
Might as well continue and break the Universal record, no?
Nux didn't mind any extra attention.
Suddenly,

Nux felt a force trying to teleport his body away. Since he had gotten his powers back, meaning he now once again had Absolute Power over Space, he could resist this. But thinking he was being taken to the next Trial Ground, he allowed it.
Flicker
Nux's body flickered out of existence, and he was teleported away.

He looked around, curious as to what the next Trial was about. The only thing his mind could think about was the ways he could clear these next two trials as soon as possible before returning to his wives, but then,
'NUX!!'
He heard a loud scream as suddenly, his shadow under his foot trembled and engulfed him in an instant.
'W-What?'
Nux stuttered, somewhat confused.
For a moment, he wondered if this was part of the Trial. Soon, however, he was quickly attacked by 18 figures and he… he was completely helpless against them.
The women shouted, pretty much fighting each other to get close to him.
And Nux, who was once again surrounded by his heaven, finally realized that the Temple had thrown him out.
But honestly,
He didn't care.
Not when the welcome he received was… this overwhelming.
With a wide grin on his face, he glanced at his beautiful wives around him and,
"I am backkk~
Did you miss me?"
He sang, waiting for wholesome replies, but then,
"WHAT WERE YOU DOING!?"
"WHERE HAVE YOU BEEN!?"
"WHAT WERE YOU THINKING!?"
"HOW DID IT TAKE YOU FIVE THOUSAND YEARS TO CLEAR THE TRIALS!?"
"DO YOU KNOW HOW WORRIED WE WERE!?"
The women shouted, ready to actually tear him apart,
That was how angry they were.
And Nux…
He couldn't believe what he was hearing,

chapters.title: Chapter 2015: From here on out, you are not allowed to leave.
paragraphs: Nux’s eyes widened in surprise.
"Wait, wait, wait, wait,
Are you telling me that I spent five thousand years inside the Temple?"
"Exactly! What were you doing!? You told us people usually return in a few decades, how did it take you so long!?"
Nux frowned.
According to the reports, a thousand years inside was a decade outside. Yes, while it did differ with each Trial, the average was about the same.
This was also the reason Nux thought he only spent about a few centuries inside the Temple...
But...
Five thousand years...?
This is the longest he had been away from all his wives, they...
They must be losing their minds...
As Nux realized that, he once again looked at his wives and finally saw it—those desperate, trembling bodies, those messy emotions, those beating hearts—he sensed it all.
"W-We couldn’t sense your existence, even Shadow couldn’t. The Universe was acting independently. Shadow’s control over it became absolute, almost as if she had inherited it.
We... we were so scared."
Felberta explained in a weak voice. Shadow, who was hearing those words, trembled even further.
The thought of inheriting all that power, the thought of inheriting an entire Universe and an army of Transcendents together with it to do whatever she pleased,
She hated it.
She hated every second of it because of how horrified she was.
After all, her inheriting that power meant that the one who once had this power no longer existed. Just the mere thought of that possibility was enough for her to fall on her knees and tremble.
And Nux could sense all these emotions, therefore, he hugged all of them as tightly as he could and,
"I am sorry."
He apologized.
"I do not know what happened, but I should have hurried back. I made you all worry."

He spoke in a voice as calming as possible. Just imagining the possibility of his wives dying in a place he couldn’t reach was enough for him to shudder in despair. To live through that feeling for 5,000 years...
He was pretty sure he would have lost his mind.
"If you dare do something like this again, I will break you into pieces."
Vyriana threatened. Even when she was overwhelmed by her emotions, she didn’t wish to appear weak.
What’s worse?
Her words weren’t an empty threat.
The current her was very much capable of harming Nux.
Yes, the Dragon had broken through.
She was now a Transcendent Level Being, and she wasn’t like those weak Transcendents like the subordinates Nux, Eisheth, and Skyla had gathered. She was different.
She alone could take all of them on, and it wouldn’t even be a fair battle.
Yes, the difference was that high.
At the Transcendent Stage, the battle between cultivators shifts from a simple, barbaric clash to a higher form of battle.
It becomes a battle between domains.
Usually, once a Domain is activated, the Law of the being who has formed the Domain becomes an Absolute. The being can then use his powers to fight and overpower his opponent.
But...
What if the opponent is a Transcendent as well?
What if both cultivators activate their domains at the same time? Would both of them now have Absolute Laws?
No.
Two Domains cannot coexist in the same space, and because of this rule, the battle of Transcendents is also called the Battle of Domains.

When the two Domains clash, one overpowers the other, and the winning cultivator gets to deal the final blow. The cultivator whose domain was crushed would be weakened and would be forced to face a being with an Absolute Law, making it pretty much impossible for him to win.
Now, how is the winner between the Battle of Domains decided?
A Domain has two properties: its Stability and its Length.
It depends on the stability of the Domains, which in turn depends on the Law the Domain is created from. The stronger the Law, the more stable the Domain formed, making it difficult to ’crush’ it.
As for beings with Absolute Laws?

Since their Law is the strongest there is, the same is true for their Domains. Their Domains are so strong in their battle against normal cultivators, all they have to do is form their Domain, crush the opponents’ Domain through the sheer weight of their own, weaken them, and then overpower them.
Yes, it was that easy.
This was also the reason that despite Nux having tens of Transcendent Level subordinates, against Vyriana, they were all...
Useless.

Of course, that had always been the case against beings with Absolute Laws and normal Laws. Beings with Absolute Laws were always capable of fighting and overpowering multiple cultivators with simpler, normal Laws.
The true battle between Domains is played between beings with equal strength—a battle where two beings cannot simply crush the opponent’s Laws.
What happens then?

As both Laws try to dominate the same space, what results is a Domain Collision—a metaphysical battlefield where Laws are locked in a contest of will and structure. The battlefield itself becomes unstable and constantly shifts between the two Laws.
The very reality flickers—fire becomes ice, gravity flips, time distorts, mountains collapse and reform as thoughts change.
In such battles, the tactics used are far more complicated than the tactics used in normal battles. It was an entirely different battle.
One that relies on Domain Stability—some Laws form a more stable Domain compared to others of similar strength. One’s comprehension of their Law can also strengthen one’s Domain.

The Size of a Domain also plays a vital role—larger Domains obviously have more influence, but at the same time, are harder to control. Smaller Domains, on the other hand, have a smaller reach, but are easier to control.

A cultivator’s willpower influences a Domain. When Domains clash, it becomes a battle between belief, obsessions, and dreams. If a being is prepared to give it his all, there is a chance to overpower the enemy’s Domain. This is also the reason broken beings usually have weaker Domains. There are even cases where Peak Transcendents have lost against new Transcendents simply because their willpower was too weak.
Another, much more difficult way to win a Battle of Domains is to Adapt.

A cultivator has absolute control over their Domain. They can be changed mid-battles. Of course, since their own understandings cannot be strengthened during the battle, this usually depends on the opponent’s Law.

A being can try and understand the enemy’s Law and while understanding the complete Law is impossible, if they understand even a little of it, they can adjust their Domain to weaken their enemy and eventually win the battle.

Of course, this is usually impossible, especially mid-battle. Usually, this only happens when one of the cultivators has encountered an enemy with a similar Law as their current enemy. The prior knowledge can be used to gain an advantage.

To weaponize this, there are many beings who explore the large universe, meeting other beings with different Laws, familiarizing themselves with those Laws, and expanding their scope of knowledge so they can use it to win future battles.
Most of the Transcendent Level Mercenaries are beings who have already exhausted their potential and are relying on this method to stay relevant and keep getting stronger.
Of course, there are countless other tactics that can be used in a Battle of Domains as well. Nux, who had absorbed knowledge of literal worlds, was familiar with most, but right now, he didn’t care.
He just stared at his wife and smiled,
"This will never happen again, I promise."
"Yes, it won’t. I know."
Amaya nodded as well, her eyes shining possessively as she stared at Nux. Nux, who looked into those eyes, gulped audibly.
He...
He was scared...?
Nux frowned at the emotion that now seemed foreign to him.
Step Step Step
Amaya, however, started walking towards him, her black eyes darkening to a degree that Nux didn’t even know was possible.
"It will never happen again because from now on, you are not allowed to leave."
The Devourer announced.
Nux narrowed his eyes. Amaya, however, wrapped her arms around his neck, chains formed out of dark mist bound Nux’s limbs, signaling him to not move, as the Devourer then continued,
"We already have our Universe. No one can threaten us here. No one can even find us here. Was that not our goal to begin with?"
The woman spoke as more and more chains started binding Nux,
"A life where no one bothers us. A life where we can stay with each other without any interference from outside. A life where only you and I exist.
We have reached it,
We have achieved our goal,
There is no need to continue any longer."
Finally, when Nux’s entire body was covered by Amaya’s chains, binding him to the ground with no escape, Amaya’s black eyes shined,
"Nux Leander, from here on out, you will keep your promise.
From here on out, you are not allowed to leave.
You will stay with me for Eternity.
And that is final."
The woman spoke as suddenly,
BOOOOOOM
Her Domain expanded.
Yes, Amaya had become a Transcendent as well.𝕗𝕣𝐞𝐞𝘄𝐞𝚋𝚗𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗹.𝚌𝕠𝚖
And not just her,
BOOOOM BOOOM BOOOM
Felberta, Aeliana, Astaria, they had all become Transcedents and had unleashed their Auras.
It seemed that...
Nux wasn’t leaving his Universe anytime soon.
