What were you doing!?
You told us people usually return in a few decades, how did it take you so long!?"
Nux frowned.
According to the reports, a thousand years inside was a decade outside.
Yes, while it did differ with each Trial, the average was about the same.
This was also the reason Nux thought he only spent about a few centuries inside the Temple...
But...
Five thousand years...?
This is the longest he had been away from all his wives, they...
They must be losing their minds...
As Nux realized that, he once again looked at his wives and finally saw it—those desperate, trembling bodies, those messy emotions, those beating hearts—he sensed it all.
"W-We couldn’t sense your existence, even Shadow couldn’t.
The Universe was acting independently.
Shadow’s control over it became absolute, almost as if she had inherited it.
We... we were so scared."
Felberta explained in a weak voice.
Shadow, who was hearing those words, trembled even further.
The thought of inheriting all that power, the thought of inheriting an entire Universe and an army of Transcendents together with it to do whatever she pleased,
She hated it.
She hated every second of it because of how horrified she was.
After all, her inheriting that power meant that the one who once had this power no longer existed.
Just the mere thought of that possibility was enough for her to fall on her knees and tremble.
And Nux could sense all these emotions, therefore, he hugged all of them as tightly as he could and,
"I am sorry."
He apologized.
"I do not know what happened, but I should have hurried back.
I made you all worry."
He spoke in a voice as calming as possible.
Just imagining the possibility of his wives dying in a place he couldn’t reach was enough for him to shudder in despair.
To live through that feeling for 5,000 years...
He was pretty sure he would have lost his mind.
"If you dare do something like this again, I will break you into pieces."
Vyriana threatened.
Even when she was overwhelmed by her emotions, she didn’t wish to appear weak.
What’s worse?
Her words weren’t an empty threat.
The current her was very much capable of harming Nux.
Yes, the Dragon had broken through.
She was now a Transcendent Level Being, and she wasn’t like those weak Transcendents like the subordinates Nux, Eisheth, and Skyla had gathered.
She was different.
She alone could take all of them on, and it wouldn’t even be a fair battle.
Yes, the difference was that high.
At the Transcendent Stage, the battle between cultivators shifts from a simple, barbaric clash to a higher form of battle.
It becomes a battle between domains.
Usually, once a Domain is activated, the Law of the being who has formed the Domain becomes an Absolute.
The being can then use his powers to fight and overpower his opponent.
But...
What if the opponent is a Transcendent as well?
What if both cultivators activate their domains at the same time?
Would both of them now have Absolute Laws?
No.
Two Domains cannot coexist in the same space, and because of this rule, the battle of Transcendents is also called the Battle of Domains.
When the two Domains clash, one overpowers the other, and the winning cultivator gets to deal the final blow.
The cultivator whose domain was crushed would be weakened and would be forced to face a being with an Absolute Law, making it pretty much impossible for him to win.
Now, how is the winner between the Battle of Domains decided?
A Domain has two properties: its Stability and its Length.
It depends on the stability of the Domains, which in turn depends on the Law the Domain is created from.
The stronger the Law, the more stable the Domain formed, making it difficult to ’crush’ it.
As for beings with Absolute Laws?
Since their Law is the strongest there is, the same is true for their Domains.

Their Domains are so strong in their battle against normal cultivators, all they have to do is form their Domain, crush the opponents’ Domain through the sheer weight of their own, weaken them, and then overpower them.
Yes, it was that easy.
This was also the reason that despite Nux having tens of Transcendent Level subordinates, against Vyriana, they were all...
Useless.
Of course, that had always been the case against beings with Absolute Laws and normal Laws.
Beings with Absolute Laws were always capable of fighting and overpowering multiple cultivators with simpler, normal Laws.
The true battle between Domains is played between beings with equal strength—a battle where two beings cannot simply crush the opponent’s Laws.
What happens then?
As both Laws try to dominate the same space, what results is a Domain Collision—a metaphysical battlefield where Laws are locked in a contest of will and structure.
The battlefield itself becomes unstable and constantly shifts between the two Laws.
The very reality flickers—fire becomes ice, gravity flips, time distorts, mountains collapse and reform as thoughts change.
In such battles, the tactics used are far more complicated than the tactics used in normal battles.
It was an entirely different battle.
One that relies on Domain Stability—some Laws form a more stable Domain compared to others of similar strength.
One’s comprehension of their Law can also strengthen one’s Domain.
The Size of a Domain also plays a vital role—larger Domains obviously have more influence, but at the same time, are harder to control.
Smaller Domains, on the other hand, have a smaller reach, but are easier to control.
A cultivator’s willpower influences a Domain.
When Domains clash, it becomes a battle between belief, obsessions, and dreams.
If a being is prepared to give it his all, there is a chance to overpower the enemy’s Domain.
This is also the reason broken beings usually have weaker Domains.
There are even cases where Peak Transcendents have lost against new Transcendents simply because their willpower was too weak.
Another, much more difficult way to win a Battle of Domains is to Adapt.
A cultivator has absolute control over their Domain.
They can be changed mid-battles.
Of course, since their own understandings cannot be strengthened during the battle, this usually depends on the opponent’s Law.

A being can try and understand the enemy’s Law and while understanding the complete Law is impossible, if they understand even a little of it, they can adjust their Domain to weaken their enemy and eventually win the battle.
Of course, this is usually impossible, especially mid-battle.
Usually, this only happens when one of the cultivators has encountered an enemy with a similar Law as their current enemy.
The prior knowledge can be used to gain an advantage.

To weaponize this, there are many beings who explore the large universe, meeting other beings with different Laws, familiarizing themselves with those Laws, and expanding their scope of knowledge so they can use it to win future battles.
Most of the Transcendent Level Mercenaries are beings who have already exhausted their potential and are relying on this method to stay relevant and keep getting stronger.
Of course, there are countless other tactics that can be used in a Battle of Domains as well.
Nux, who had absorbed knowledge of literal worlds, was familiar with most, but right now, he didn’t care.
He just stared at his wife and smiled,
"This will never happen again, I promise."
"Yes, it won’t.
I know."
Amaya nodded as well, her eyes shining possessively as she stared at Nux.
Nux, who looked into those eyes, gulped audibly.
He...
He was scared...?
Nux frowned at the emotion that now seemed foreign to him.
Step Step Step
Amaya, however, started walking towards him, her black eyes darkening to a degree that Nux didn’t even know was possible.
"It will never happen again because from now on, you are not allowed to leave."
The Devourer announced.
Nux narrowed his eyes.
Amaya, however, wrapped her arms around his neck, chains formed out of dark mist bound Nux’s limbs, signaling him to not move, as the Devourer then continued,
"We already have our Universe.
No one can threaten us here.
No one can even find us here.
Was that not our goal to begin with?"
The woman spoke as more and more chains started binding Nux,
"A life where no one bothers us.
A life where we can stay with each other without any interference from outside.
A life where only you and I exist.
We have reached it,
We have achieved our goal,
There is no need to continue any longer."
Finally, when Nux’s entire body was covered by Amaya’s chains, binding him to the ground with no escape, Amaya’s black eyes shined,
"Nux Leander, from here on out, you will keep your promise.
From here on out, you are not allowed to leave.
You will stay with me for Eternity.
And that is final."
The woman spoke as suddenly,
BOOOOOOM
Her Domain expanded.
Yes, Amaya had become a Transcendent as well.𝕗𝕣𝐞𝐞𝘄𝐞𝚋𝚗𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗹.𝚌𝕠𝚖
And not just her,
BOOOOM BOOOM BOOOM
Felberta, Aeliana, Astaria, they had all become Transcedents and had unleashed their Auras.
It seemed that...
Nux wasn’t leaving his Universe anytime soon.

chapters.title: Chapter 2016: Just say you aren’t going to create Time in the first place and will find something else to replace it.
paragraphs: "My lovely, most beautiful, most amazing wives."
Nux called out, staring at the beautiful women walking towards him with a nervous look on his face.

The chains restricting him got tighter and tighter, making it impossible for him to move. Now, could he break these chains and free himself? Of course he could. He was in his Universe, where he was at his strongest. Transcendents or not, his physical might was more than enough to forcefully break through these chains.
But...
Would he survive the consequences?
Heh.
Nux was a smart man.
He knew where he had to back down.
Happy wife, happy life. This is even truer when you have more wives.
The only thing Nux could do right now was to profusely beg and get out of this situation as sleekly as possible.
And there he was, trying to do just that.
"Why not listen to what I have to say first?"
He suggested intelligently.
"And what is it?"
Felberta took the bait.
"You know how much I love you, right?"
"Do we?"
Aeliana questioned back.
"You left us."
Even Evane complained.
"It wasn’t m—"
"For five thousand years."
The instant the elf completed that sentence, Nux turned silent.
Evane’s breathing became heavy and,
"I was... scared.
We all were."
"So you will stay with us.
For Eternity."
The elf declared, repeating Amaya’s words, and since even the most reasonable one had deviated from his side, there was no way out.
It was Nux’s defeat.
He simply closed his eyes as his wives surrounded him.
Amaya’s domain expanded even further, surrounding every single woman, instantly pausing Time around them, something that Nux narrowed his eyes at as he noticed something strange.
His focus, however, was instantly attracted by the woman who smiled at him and,
"It is only you and I now."
"That has a nice ring to it."
Nux commented intelligently.
"I agree."
Amaya nodded with a light smile.
"Would sound even better once we deal with all our enemies for goo—"
"Don’t push your luck, boy."
Amaya interrupted, putting her finger on Nux’s lips.
"You are only a few years older than me."
Nux retorted as he started sucking her finger, something that Amaya didn’t mind one bit.
"You are still a boy."

She spoke, putting the second finger in. The smile on her face widened slowly, her dark eyes became darker and darker as suddenly, the chains wrapped around Nux loosened and grabbed Amaya as well, pulling her in.
"This is not safe, you know?"
Nux, who could now feel Amaya’s body all over him as the chains tightened around them, commented with a smile on his face, still sucking on her fingers.
"Are you scared of little chains?"
Amaya questioned in a playful tone.
"I am not."
Nux shook his head.
"But you should be."
He spoke with a demonic grin on his face. His canines elongated as he bit Amaya’s neck, leaving no way for the woman to resist as she was now bound by her own chains.
"Aaannhh~"
The woman moaned, her body squirmed as she sensed Nux’s body over hers after such a long, long time.
Soon, the chains continued to wrap around them, covering their entire body, forming a strange dome where they couldn’t move apart for more than a second.
Yes, their bodies were now glued, something that Amaya had been fantasizing all this while and...
And it felt much, much better than what she had in her mind.
Very quickly, clothes were ripped apart, their naked bodies rolled over each other and then,
"Annnh~"
The devourer moaned as she slowly got devoured.
Time passed. Since Amaya was now a Transcendent, she could last much longer than before, something she took full advantage of.
She didn’t even bother regenerating the broken chains after a few years. With Nux right next to her, her messy mind had finally become clearer.
A heaven.
That was what Nux’s embrace was for her.

And it wasn’t just her. The rest of the women, who Nux went to after Amaya, were all the same. They were scared, nervous, and were in constant pain for the past five thousand years. Nux felt his heart ache every time he saw them in this state.
He spent as much time as they wanted with them. He stayed with them even when they were asleep simply because these women refused to let his hand go, even in their sleep.
For the next few centuries, he didn’t give two shits about the Supreme Worlds, that Soul Father of his, or even Azriel, the Universe, and the Time Laws.
The only thing he cared about was his wives and how to calm them down.
Time passed just like that, and only after about 800 years had passed did Nux finally let go of his wives, and the first question was asked,
"What did you learn inside the Temple of Time?"
Felberta questioned, curious.
Nux laughed. He then told them everything that happened and how he had to ’create’ his own unique Time, and as he continued, the women frowned.
"So the five thousand years you spent...
They were all useless?"
Astaria raised her eyebrow.
"Well...
Yeah."
Nux nodded.

The Power of Time was complicated. Even if he formed his own Time, its rules would not apply to the Main Universe. He wouldn’t be able to use any of the Time-related powers against beings of the main Universe because the two of them would exist in different Times.
All the women turned silent.
What could they even say? It wasn’t like Nux knew this was going to happen. Blaming him for this is foolish.
"So... are you going to create Time?"
"I will, yes.
For the Universe to be functional, all Primordial Energies are needed, especially the Energy of Time."
Suddenly, a frown appeared on Amaya’s face.
"But doesn’t Time already exist in our Universe?"
She questioned as she glanced at all the women around her and,
"We all spent five thousand years in here, we cultivated and even broke through. If the concept of Time doesn’t exist here, then everything shouldn’t be this smooth, should it?
How did only five thousand years pass?
Why did the Time Flow?
If Time didn’t exist, why weren’t we trapped here for Eternity?
And...
What do I devour if I devour the Time around us to freeze time?"
The woman shot a bunch of questions, questions Nux already had the answers to.
"It is a borrowed framework."
"What?"
"Borrowed Framework,"
Nux repeated as he then started explaining,
"There are a few forces no Universe can survive without:
Time, Space, Cause and Effect.

When our Universe was formed, it was Empty, but it wasn’t truly ’Empty’. Even the weakest, simplest of dimensions need the above-mentioned forces, let alone a Universe. That is how essential these forces are.
But because of how essential these forces are, every being understands their simplest of concepts.
Any human, even a mortal, is able to perceive time. I was no different, so the Universe used my perception of Time and made it its own."
"So if it used your perception..."
"Yes, it copied Time from the Main Universe."
Nux nodded.
"But again, it was just a borrowed framework, like an echo. It was not an established Time set by me, the Universe.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
It was only a temporary measure, something that can never be used as one of the Primordial Energies. After all, if two Universes have the same ’Time’, they will collide."
"So... how are you going to form your own Unique Time?"
Felberta questioned with a curious look on her face.
Since it was about creation, she was extremely interested. She was also waiting to see if she could be of any help in any way, something that Nux could see with how her eyes were shining brightly.
He chuckled at how adorable his wife was as he then shrugged,
"Well, I have differentiated between thousands of ’Times’ when I cleared the final Trial."
"But there aren’t just thousands of Universes, you said it yourself."
Melia pointed.
"There aren’t."
Nux nodded.

"There are many, more than what any of us could think of. If I follow their pattern and create something similar, but different from the Times I comprehended, I am sure that our Universe will then clash with another, making it impossible for me to continue.
I need something...
Entirely Unique.
Something that doesn’t exist, even once, in trillions and trillions of Universes."
The moment she heard those words, Edda laughed out loud,
"Trillions? Just say you aren’t going to create Time in the first place and will find something else to replace it.
That sounds more plausible."
The perverted maid grinned. The rest of the women stared at her, narrowing their eyes at her, not liking her pessimistic attitude, but suddenly,
"That is correct."
Nux nodded.
The women frowned, Nux on the other hand, grinned.
"I am not going to form Time. It is impossible to form a uniquely structured Time considering the absurd number of Universes there are...
So,
I am going to create something different.
Instead of trying to form a structured Time, I am going to form an unstructured Time,
A Sentient Time.
A Time that feels, responds, and empathizes with every being of the Universe.
A Time anchored, not to the Universe, but to its residents’ emotions."
"What...?"
The women blinked, and Nux’s grin just widened as he closed his eyes and got to work.

chapters.title: Chapter 2017: Emotions are what give Time meaning.
paragraphs: "He... He is really creating it...
He is creating Time..."
Felberta, who saw her own powers being used in a way she could never imagine, muttered with a ridiculous look on her face.
"...Just when I thought I would never be surprised again."

Astaria commented. As one of the oldest wives, she had been constantly shocked by Nux’s feats and had promised herself not to react to her husband’s absurdities—a promise she had been breaking again and again and again... and again.
And again.
The rest of the women were awestruck as well, unable to say anything.
They just stared at Nux hovering in the vast Universe with his eyes closed. In front of him, an extremely beautiful stream of energy floated constantly, attracting all their attention.
It was like a river, a river that flowed through the middle of Nux’s Universe. It had no path, no fixed direction, it just... flowed.
It was wide, endless, and full of soft light and deep shadows. Its colors kept changing—sometimes golden-pink like a sunrise, other times dark red, blue, or even almost invisible.
It wasn’t just the colors; the speed at which the river flowed seemed to constantly change as well. Sometimes, it even stayed still, not moving at all.
The women didn’t know what this river was, but they did know one thing—
It was beautiful.
*Picture*
"River of Time."
Suddenly, Shadow blurted out some words. Even she seemed taken aback by the sudden information entering her mind.
The rest of the women turned towards her and tilted their heads in confusion.
The river still wasn’t completed yet, but as the Soul of the Universe, Shadow had begun to understand what it was.𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
She stared at it with a lost look on her face. With all the information entering her mind, the entire thing became even more beautiful in her eyes.
"This is the River of Time."
She started sharing the information with her sisters.
"A representation of Time in our Universe."
"This is Time...?"
Lyriana frowned.
This looked nothing like Time.
The rest of the women seemed confused as well. None of them had comprehended a Law related to Time, but they still understood how Time generally worked.
Even if Nux was creating something unique, he couldn’t exactly ’change’ the very meaning of Time itself.
Time needed to flow.
Time needed to have a direction.
It needed to be constant.
It needed past, present, and future.
That is what gave Time meaning.
But...
A color-changing river that flowed in an unknown direction, at a constantly changing speed—it was hardly a representation of Time.
Shadow, knowing exactly what her sisters were thinking, shook her head and clarified.
"The River doesn’t reflect Time. It reflects Emotions.
Emotions that our Universe’s Time will be affected by."
"He... really meant it when he said he will create a Time anchored to every being’s emotions...?"
Felberta blinked, unable to believe what she was hearing.
"That makes no sense."
Eisheth shook her head, and the rest agreed.
"Emotions and Time are not related in any way."

paragraphs: "And what are thesepurefetishes?"
Edda questioned playfully.
"I love t—mmhppgghhhh!!"
Before Shadow could continue any longer, Lane appeared by her side and grabbed her mouth, not allowing her to speak any longer.
She glared at Edda, Aisha, and Eisheth and,
"I know what you are trying to do."
She spoke up.
"Come on, it’s all fun and games."
Edda answered.
"Share your own fetishes for that."
"Sure.
Which one would you like to hear first?
Or better, how about you participate in one? I assure you, it will be unlike anything you have ever experienced."
"S-Shut up!"
Lane silenced the woman before she released Shadow and,
"Don’t let them distract you, continue what you were telling. This is an important moment, we need to focus."
"Yes, I wish to know more about the River."
Felberta nodded as well.
As a being who specialized in creation, witnessing the creation of Time itself felt like her very existence was being given a new meaning.
The rest of the women were curious too, even Eisheth, Aisha, and Edda, so they turned silent, allowing Shadow to continue.
During their little interaction, more information filled her mind, information that gave her a slight glimpse into Nux’s mind.
"As I was saying,
Time is a blank canvas. We—the living—are the ones that paint it, that give it a meaning.
However, Nux had turned this blank canvas into something different, into something... special.
Something Superior."
"Something... Superior?"
Melia muttered, awed.
"Superior to Time?"
Felberta frowned.
How could something be... superior to a Primordial Energy? That too, a Primordial Energy that gave a Universe an identity.
That made no sense.
Shadow, however, nodded at her question and continued.
"The Time in our Universe is much more special than the Time you are familiar with.
It does not move like the ticking of a cold, unfeeling clock.
It breathes.
It listens to the heartbeat of the Universe.
It stretches and contracts with sorrow and joy,
It quickens with rage and slows with despair.
Our Time is not bound to seconds or minutes—it is bound to emotions.
Our Time will not be measured by how long something lasts—
It will be measured by how deeply it is felt.
A single kiss shared between two lovers can stretch for eternity.
A moment of heartbreak can feel heavier than a thousand years.
Time will depend on one’s will. Time they consider to be precious will slow down. Time they consider to be a drag will move fast.
In our Universe, Timewillwait for its people.
The Time of our Universe, just like Nux said, will be sentient—an entity that will sense all there is.
Our Time will be ours alone.
It will be personal, subjective, and...
True.
No two beings of ours will experience Time the same way, not because our Universe is broken, but because our Universe isbetter."
Shadow explained, and just the thought of living in times where the moment you want to last for eternitywilllast for an eternity felt like a dream come true.

Just imagining how kissing Nux and spending time with him would continue on for thousands of years, and waiting for him for thousands of years would only feel like a few seconds, made them shiver in joy.
It was a dream world.
A world where things happened exactly how they wanted them to happen.
The women stared at the River of Time with a newfound shine in their eyes.
Felberta, however, was confused.
"If every being perceives Time differently, won’t everything fall into... chaos?"
Aeliana nodded at those words.
"Indeed, even in freedom, there needs to be a structure, or else society cannot function."
The rest of the women frowned. They had just started dwelling in their fantasies—to think they would be crushed before they could even lose themselves for a few seconds.
"It won’t."
Suddenly, the women heard a voice.
A voice that instantly attracted their attention. They turned around and saw Nux standing behind them with a smile on his face.
"Nux!"
Very quickly, they surrounded him. Even after centuries of spending time with him, the women still couldn’t get enough of him—a feeling Nux wholeheartedly shared.
He then glanced at Felberta and Aeliana and answered their question.
"Yes, our Time will be bound to one’s emotions and everyone will perceive it differently, but it doesn’t mean they will be able to abuse it.
When it is said every being perceives time differently, it doesn’t mean that Time will have no structure.
Understand it in this way:
Assume that the Universe has two coexisting layers of Time: a Universal Time, a time shared by all the worlds and the beings living in them,
And a Personal Time, time perceived by individuals.
Personal Time can be altered; however, no change in personal time will affect the Universal Time.
Say, if a couple expands their personal time and changes 12 hours of their Personal Time into 12 days, the rest of the Universe and the Universal Time will only perceive it as 12 hours.
Also, events that happen when the Personal Time is expanded cannot defy the limitations of Universal Time.
If a Cultivator needs to gather 100 years of energy to break through, he needs to spend 100 years of Universal Time. Expanding a day of his Personal Time into 100 years will not work.
Of course, there are a few other restrictions as well, but in conclusion, even when Time in our Universe will be subjective, structure and order will still exist in a most unstructured way."
"That sounds... overly complicated."
Felberta muttered with a lost look on her face, to which Nux just laughed out loud.
"Well, I did spend countless years comprehending and coming up with it."
The women laughed as well.
"Anyways, should we continue?
I still need to create Anchors and Compasses around Umbrasol to stabilize Time."
"Is it still not done yet?"
Felberta questioned with a frown as she stared at the River flowing in the Universe. From her perspective, it seemed to be completed already.
"It is still unstable, very unstable."
Shadow shook her head and Nux, who heard those words, chuckled and then nodded.
"Indeed. It still needs work."

chapters.title: Chapter 2019: The Cost of Free Will.
paragraphs: "What is this?"
Felberta questioned with a curious look on her face as she stared at the 1000-meter-tall crystalline tower. It shined with soft light that changed colors.
Inside the tower, there was a glowing hourglass. The sand inside it sparkled like stars, but it never ran out. The hourglass turned on its own, always slow and steady, like the heartbeat of time.
Its surface was smooth, but if someone looked closely, they would see thousands of complex tiny Runes and Glowing Geometries that seemed almost impossible to even comprehend, let alone replicate.
*Picture*

Yes, Felberta, using her Power of Genesis, tried more than once, but every single time, she missed the mark by more than a few strokes. Even when she tried to picture the entire thing in her mind, she couldn’t get the entire thing correct.
To make things worse?
These complex Runes shifted every heartbeat.

Yes, a heartbeat. In Nux’s Universe, Shadow’s heartbeat had replaced the unit of time. This was done to strengthen the concept of linkage between Time and Emotions. While every being in the Universe has their own Personal Time, the Universal Time needed a structure as well.
A structure that Shadow, as the Soul of the Universe, decided to become.

Yes, for Shadow, the Universal Time was her Personal Time. She could manipulate it just like others could manipulate their Personal Time, just that in her case, once she manipulates the Time, the entire Universe will be affected by it—even Nux and his wives.

If Shadow so wanted, thousands of years in Nux’s Universe could pass within seconds, just that no one in the Universe would realize it since they would be living through that time like they normally would.
Why was Shadow chosen for this?
There were several factors:
She was the First Goddess of the Universe, the Soul of the Universe, plus, her powers depended on Nux, so she didn’t have to cultivate.
Her ’Time’ was the most stable.
Anyways, as mentioned, the Runes and Geometries changed with every heartbeat, and every change was completely different than before, making it impossible for one to copy them.
"It is a Time Anchor."
Nux answered with a light smile.
"What are those Runes?"
Felberta asked another question. Nux, however, shook his head.
"You will not understand.
These Runes are what allow the Time Anchors to function. You need to understand the concept of the Universe’s Time to get the answer to your question."
"Is that why I cannot replicate it?"
"Mhm."
Nux nodded, and Felberta just sighed.
"What does it do? This Time Anchor?"
Rune questioned, curious.
"Emotions are unstable.
Linking Time with Emotions may be a novel concept, but it comes with its own share of troubles.
The biggest one being losing oneself.
A Time Anchor prevents that."
Nux answered, and the women just stared at him with deadpan looks on their faces—clearly, they had no clue what this man was talking about.
Nux knew that, so he chuckled and then continued,

"There are times when people’s emotions are too strong for them to have any control over—a mother grieving her lost child, lovers kissing each other for the first time, a Hero being betrayed by the very people he protected all his life.
It is easy to lose one’s sense of Personal Time during these moments. There might even be a case where beings might stretch their Personal Time for eternity and lose themselves entirely.
The Time Anchor constantly emits a stream of Universal Time, which gives it the power to forcefully level one’s Personal Time to the Universal Time.
When a being is lost in his own Personal Time, he can be brought near the influence of a Time Anchor, and the lost being can be recovered."
The women nodded at the explanation.

"Of course, it has other important roles too. It will act like the Universal Time Beacon. Negotiations where every being needs to be on the same ’Time’ and no being is allowed to use their Personal Time for whatever reasons can be held under the influence of Time Anchors."
"Wait...
Anchors?
You will make more than one?"
"Of course.
I have limited its sphere of influence; else there will be no point in having different Times.
One Anchor would have about a 10-kilometre-long influence."
"That’s quite small."
Astaria muttered.
"There will be a Time Anchor every 1,000,000 square kilometres."
"Still, don’t you think the sphere of influence is too small?"
"I made it that way. I do not want the people to be too heavily reliant on the Time Anchors."
"And who will have the authority over the Time Anchors?"
Aeliana questioned with a curious look on her face.
Right now, Nux’s Universe barely had any living beings. There were quite a few ’half beings’ that he got from devouring the worlds, but they were just that—half beings. They do not count.
Nux didn’t even have 100 Complete Beings. However, once Nux gathers all the remaining Primordial Energies, his Universe would become capable of giving birth to its own people.
Once that happens, eventually, those beings will gather together, civilization will be born. There will even be the rise and fall of dynasties,
So Aeliana was curious what role would these Time Anchors play in all this.
But...
"Who cares?"
Nux shrugged.
"What...?"
"I created what was meant to stabilize my Universe. How the beings of my Universe use my creation, I do not care.
I have no intention of involving myself with them.
I will give them complete control.
Or a Free Will, as they call it."
Nux smiled lightly, and Aeliana, who could tell what he was thinking, narrowed her eyes.
"You want them to go to wars to have monopoly over the Anchors."
"If that is what Free Will leads to, so be it.
It will betheCost of Free Will."
Nux shrugged.
"As I said, I will not interfere with my people. That would be no different than ruling over them through might. I might as well enslave them and force them to live how I want them to."
Aeliana turned silent.
She felt that this was wrong, but at the same time...
It was not...?
She felt... confused.
As he glanced at her, Nux chuckled,
"Though I do have another interesting feature."
He spoke up.

"Of course.
I have limited its sphere of influence; else there will be no point in having different Times.
One Anchor would have about a 10-kilometre-long influence."
"That’s quite small."
Astaria muttered.
"There will be a Time Anchor every 1,000,000 square kilometres."
"Still, don’t you think the sphere of influence is too small?"
"I made it that way.
I do not want the people to be too heavily reliant on the Time Anchors."
"And who will have the authority over the Time Anchors?"
Aeliana questioned with a curious look on her face.
Right now, Nux’s Universe barely had any living beings.
There were quite a few ’half beings’ that he got from devouring the worlds, but they were just that—half beings.
They do not count.
Nux didn’t even have 100 Complete Beings.
However, once Nux gathers all the remaining Primordial Energies, his Universe would become capable of giving birth to its own people.
Once that happens, eventually, those beings will gather together, civilization will be born.
There will even be the rise and fall of dynasties,
So Aeliana was curious what role would these Time Anchors play in all this.
But...
"Who cares?"
Nux shrugged.
"What...?"
"I created what was meant to stabilize my Universe.
How the beings of my Universe use my creation, I do not care.
I have no intention of involving myself with them.
I will give them complete control.
Or a Free Will, as they call it."
Nux smiled lightly, and Aeliana, who could tell what he was thinking, narrowed her eyes.
"You want them to go to wars to have monopoly over the Anchors."
"If that is what Free Will leads to, so be it.
It will betheCost of Free Will."
Nux shrugged.
"As I said, I will not interfere with my people.
That would be no different than ruling over them through might.
I might as well enslave them and force them to live how I want them to."
Aeliana turned silent.
She felt that this was wrong, but at the same time...
It was not...?
She felt... confused.
As he glanced at her, Nux chuckled,
"Though I do have another interesting feature."
He spoke up.

chapters.title: Chapter 2020: Time Anchor and Time Compass.
paragraphs: "Though I do have another interesting feature."

He spoke up, instantly gathering his wives’ interest. They stared at him, waiting for him to continue. They were literally standing at the very beginning of an entirely separate Universe, their own Universe. All of them were extremely interested in it and wanted to be a part of it.
Nux smiled at their interest. He then glanced at the Time Anchors, and a few Runes imprinted on it became brighter, as if Nux was highlighting them.
Felberta, who saw those Runes, narrowed her eyes.

When she trained with Faustina to get the Power of Genesis and inherit Aurelia’s Law of Genesis, she had studied millions of Runes, and while she still couldn’t recreate or comprehend all the Runes used to create the Time Anchor, identifying a particular set of Runes wasn’t very difficult.
"Rune of Endless Memory."
She muttered as she glanced at Nux.
Nux’s smile widened.
"These Towers will keep constant records of everything that happens under their sphere of influence for an Eternity.

These records can be accessed by every being who learns to access these Runes, allowing them to peek into history from their current time, all the way to the time when the Universe’s first True Life Forms were born."
Nux paused as he momentarily glanced at all his wives before he continued,
"I have seen memory of thousands of worlds. I have seen millions of civilizations rise and fall to the point I got bored of it.
So much so that I had started predicting how long it would take for a certain civilization to fall and for the next one to take over.
It had become a game for me, a game I had become quite good at.
Do you know how?"
Nux questioned.
The women frowned, paying attention to his words.
"History."
The women’s frown deepened and Nux’s explanation deepened.
"Almost all civilizations had the habit of burning previous civilizations’ histories and manipulating their own. Some did it to a lesser degree, while others, did quite a bit.
The knowledge they left for the next generation was… altered.
That was one of the signs. A civilization that altered history regularly usually fell quicker than others.
So the only thing I will give to the beings of my Universe is a Right to True History.
I will give them a chance to learn from their predecessors’ mistakes and… well, survive.
Again, how they will use this Gift depends on them.
I have done my part—well, at least half of it."
"Half of it?"
"I still need to create one more thing to stabilize Time."
"One more?"
The women frowned. Nux, on the other hand, extended his hands as the Time Anchor he created started trembling violently.
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzzzz
BZZZZZZ

In the end, the tremors became much stronger than before. It almost felt like the Anchor was about to break apart, but then, as if it was forcefully extracted out of the first one, another Anchor appeared in front of them.
BZZZZZZ
The process continued. More and more Anchors continued to form, constantly cloning each other until it reached the amount that satisfied Nux.
With a wave of Nux’s hand, these Anchors spread all over Umbrasol, settling in every 1,000,000 square kilometers, just as Nux had stated.
Then, Nux raised his hand and a small, elegant device formed in his palm.
It was made of smooth, silvery metal that shimmered softly. At its center was a tiny hourglass, filled with glowing sand that moved slowly, very similar to the Hourglass inside the Time Anchors.

Surrounding the hourglass were thin, spinning rings etched with shifting symbols—runes that gently changed shape with every heartbeat. The needle inside the circular ring constantly pointed at the nearest Time Anchor.
*Picture*
"What is this…?"
Felberta questioned again.
"A Time Compass."
"A Time Compass?"
"A Bridge between one’s Personal Time and Universal Time. A Time Compass can be used to switch between Personal and Universal Time more efficiently."
"I thought the switch was linked to one’s emotions."
Amaya questioned with a frown.
"It is."
Nux nodded.

"But again, emotions are too unstable. Different people have different degrees of emotions. Take two lovers for example—if one of them feels more ’love’ than the other, the two will have different Personal Times, which would create another set of problems.
The Compass solves that issue.

One can connect their Time Compass to another being, allowing them to share their Personal Time. Of course, the number of individuals one can connect to will be limited to three, and the chosen three cannot be changed, even when one of the chosen dies.
Again, I made these multipurpose as well.
A Time Compass’s needle always points at the nearest Time Anchor. It also has another, much more interesting feature—
Emotional Preservation."
The women tilted their heads, curious.
"The Time Compass allows people to Mark three special moments of their lives, allowing them to relive those moments and feel the same emotions they once did.
A mother can preserve the feeling of holding her newborn child.
A warrior can revisit the exact moment their brother fell, understanding the sorrow they once denied.
Lovers can re-experience their first kiss—not just in memory, but with the full emotional weight of that moment’s Time.
It will be my most personal and precious gift to the beings of my Universe."
"This… this is beautiful."
Evane spoke up, loving this idea. Her mind already started thinking of what three moments she would choose.
"See? I am not an emotionless monster.
I care."
Nux chuckled at her words.
"But why are there only three moments?"
Evane frowned. She had been trying to think of three moments, but she had so many beautiful moments she had spent with Nux that she couldn’t choose just three.
There should be at least a milli—no, a billion moments.
Nux, however, shook his head.
"This is supposed to be a small gift, not a curse.
I cannot let my people live in the past. The number of times they can relive these moments in a year will be limited as well.
Let’s say… once every 10,000,000 heartbeats."
"That’s so mean…"
Evane pouted.
To which, Nux just chuckled as he pulled her close to him.
"This is just for beings living here in Umbrasol. You do not have to worry about it."
He whispered into her ears as he felt her body touching his. Evane squirmed, her eyes brightened.
"Does this mean I will have no limits to the moments I store and number of times I relive them?"
She questioned excitedly.
"No, even better.
I will make sure you will never need to Mark a moment because I will always be with you, creating much more likable moments.
Why relive the past… when we can keep creating a more beautiful present?
No?"
Nux whispered again. His voice was so seductive that it resembled a demon trying to entice an innocent woman.
And the innocent woman did indeed fall for the enticement as Evane’s face turned red and,
"mm."
She nodded lightly, slowly rubbing her body with Nux’s as his hands caressed her butt and then,
Bite
Nux bit her long ears,
"Annnhh~"

chapters.title: Chapter 2021: What are you hiding?
paragraphs: "Only 60,000,000 heartbeats (about two years) have passed in total if we exclude Shadow’s Time.
I think we can call this a success, no?"
Nux questioned with a big smile on his face as he stared at his wives.
"Indeed."

The women nodded. Just like Nux, they all had big smiles on their faces. Their legs were trembling nonstop as they hovered in the air. Some had lost looks on their faces, as if they didn’t even know where they were and were just staring at an empty space ahead of them with a foolish look on their faces.
"With this, our Universe finally has the Primordial Energy of Time."
Nux announced. Once again, the women who could still hear him nodded, while the rest just stood there in silence.
Of course, Nux didn’t mind it one bit. Rather, it gave him an ego boost.
And…
He needed his wives to be in this condition for what he was about to say next. Giving the loves of his life one last look, Nux finally took his shot,
"And with this, it is time I return to the Main Universe."
He dropped the bomb, and in an instant, some of the women’s expressions changed.
Felberta stared at him and narrowed her eyes.
"You know I need to go."
Nux spoke.
Felberta was silent.
She knew it was the truth.
Nux needed to return. He needed to gather the last four Primordial Energies to complete his Universe, but…
She was also scared of losing Nux in the process.
Yes, the five thousand years away from Nux had made her paranoid.
She was… scared.
Of course, she also knew she needed to let go of this fear. Her Nux was strong, and she needed to trust him. She needed to be the reasonable one here. She couldn’t act like Amaya and hold him bac—
’Huh?’
Suddenly, Felberta’s expression changed as she realized something.
Amaya still hadn’t said anything. It was quite odd.
She turned towards her sister and very quickly realized why the woman was silent.
"Mmhhhmmmm~~ Hhhmmm~"
Amaya hummed a tune with a silly smile on her face, staring at an empty space while her legs trembled. Her juices trailed down her leg from her gown, but she didn’t seem to care.
She didn’t even seem like she was in this world to care about such mundane matters.
Yes, Amaya was currently one of the women who had lost their minds. Felberta turned back towards Nux and shook her head with a grin.
"Yo—"
"You chose her at last because of this, didn’t you?"
Eisheth questioned.
She had somewhat recovered as well and could see Amaya’s condition.
Nux smiled.
"She won’t let me leave."
He answered lightly.
"She wouldn’t.
She is too scared, so scared that she will give her all to stop you."
Eisheth spoke in a light tone.
All the women knew how much Amaya was affected by these past 5000 years without Nux. They had seen her break down multiple times. The woman had pretty much lost her mind.

Seeing her state was also when Nux realized how serious this actually was and decided not to return to the Main Universe for a while. The situation was so bad that the woman wouldn’t even let him leave the Universe even if it was just to have sex with them. They would rather have sex with him in a world where light does not exist.

It was so bad that instead of using the information he had comprehended inside the Temple of Time and creating Time right away, Nux waited for long, long years, spent time with his wives, constantly telling them he was back, and only when they calmed a little did he finally move forward.

But even then, he could sense the women still wouldn’t let him leave, so he decided to spend more time with them—this time, as an ’experiment’ to test if the Time he had created actually worked or not.

It was a perfect use of Personal Time and Universal Time. He went to his wives, connected their Personal Times, and extended it. On the Universal Level, he only spent around 100,000 heartbeats with each one of them, but in truth, they spent thousands of years together.
Time his wives would never forget, especially Amaya, who, in her desperation, laid out all her fantasies—even the ones hidden deep, deep inside her.
It was an Amaya Nux had never seen before, an Amaya he loved a lot.
And once he was done…
Amaya was left in this state.
"Fufufu~"
The Devourer smiled, her mind and body still reminiscing what just happened.
"I need her to let go of that fear."
Nux commented as he stared at his wife.
"I need her next to me if I wish to win.
I need all of you next to me, not doubting me or being scared for me,
But trusting me with your eyes closed, like you did before."
"We are just…"
Felberta didn’t know how to say anything.
"We do not know anything about the Supreme Worlds."
Thyra spoke up.
Yes, the Cat was awake from her stupor as well, and unlike Felberta, she decided to speak her mind.
"The enemies are too strong, even you know that."
Thyra spoke.
"Wasn’t that always the case?"
"But we had people protecting us before. Now we are on our own.
You are alone because we cannot help you as much. This is what affects us so much—we are too weak in front of the enemies we are facing."
Thyra then glanced at Amaya and,
"This is also the reason she is reacting so extremely. She realized how weak she was even after breaking through the Transcendent Level."
The rest of the women nodded. They felt the same.
"We cannot lose you, Nux."
Eisheth spoke up.
"We cannot."
She repeated her words, her tone much lighter than before.
"You will not. I promise.
I will not lose."
Nux answered, confident.
"There is one much more certain way to not lose."
Eisheth spoke. Everyone knew what she was implying, even Nux, but…
"I promise I will win."
Nux replied, not backing down.
The women glanced at each other, still a little worried. They tried to convince themselves and deal with their paranoia, but it was easier said than done.
Nux, who saw that, clenched his fists.
An action Felberta, who had been observing him from the start, didn’t miss.
"Nux."
She called out.
"What are you hiding?"
She questioned directly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2022: Let’s return to the Main Universe.
paragraphs: "Nux."
She called out.
"What are you hiding?"
She questioned directly.
"What are you talking about?"
Nux tilted his head in confusion, Felberta however, continued to stare at him, waiting for him to explain on his own.
Something didn’t make sense.

From the beginning, everything Nux did, he did it for his wives. Even when he had a goal, it was nothing more than a stepping stone to achieve his ultimate goal—to spend time with his wives for Eternity.
The women knew that because they had the exact same goal. Everything they did all this time, it was all done to create a safe haven for Nux and them, a haven they could spend Eternity in.
And right now…
They already had such a haven.
Sure, it had its own disadvantages, and Nux, who wanted to make everything perfect for his wives, wanted to deal with those disadvantages. This was the reason he was still fighting.
But…
To not give up even when all of them—to even play such tricks with Amaya, just so he could leave.
It went against Nux’s character.
Something didn’t make sense here.
Nux…
He was hiding something.
And with how desperate he seemed to be acting, Felberta could tell this was something important. So the first wife continued to stare at her husband, waiting for him to answer.
Under that stare, Nux couldn’t hold out for long, and after a little more hesitation, once he confirmed that Felberta had no plans on giving up unless he told her everything, he gave in instead.
"The Eternity we dreamt…
We might not have achieved it."
Nux answered, and the moment he said those words, Felberta and the other women who could still listen stared at him with frowns on their faces.
"What do you mean?"
Felberta questioned.
"It… it is just an instinctual feeling, I cannot explain it…"
"What feeling?"
Felberta narrowed her eyes.
Nux paused for a moment as he observed all his wives, then, he looked at the vast Universe he was in and,
"Our Universe is dying."
"What…?"
The women widened their eyes in disbelief. Nux, on the other hand, instantly went to calm them down,
"Again, this is just an instinctual feeling, there is a chance that I am wrong."
"But there is also a chance that you are right."
Thyra spoke up, and Nux… he nodded at her words.
"Why do you think that?"
Felberta questioned.
"Even if it is just a feeling, no matter how minuscule, there must be a reason behind it, no? What is it?"
"The very existence of our Universe makes me uncertain."
Felberta tilted her head in confusion and Nux began,
"At first, I was incompetent, I didn’t know anything. The possibility of having a separate, independent Universe inside me excited me—it made me feel strong—but…
As I grow, the more I learn, the more I realize that our Universe…
It shouldn’t exist."
The women narrowed their eyes, attentively listening to his words. Nux looked around and continued,𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
"I felt it before, but at that time, I didn’t think too much about it. But now, I am slowly realizing the truth."
"The truth?"
"The fact that our Universe, in theory, should not exist.
Usually, a Universe is formed when a Timeline branches. Every time a being from a Universe travels through Time and survives, he creates an entirely different Universe with a different ’Time’.
This is what other Universes are.
But that is not the case for our Universe. Our Universe didn’t even have a ’Time’ till now. In theory, it shouldn’t exist."
"But it does."
Eisheth spoke out loud.
"So that ’theory’ is wrong. What is there to worry about?"
"There is no ’meaning’ to our Universe, Eisheth.
We are completely out of the Loop.
All the Universes in the Multiverse have a Timeline, a Timeline that is already fixed—from the start of the Universe to its end, all the events that are supposed to play out are marked.
But…
We are an exception.
Our Universe has no predetermined Future.
It is something that should not exist, something out of the order of the Multiverse. How long do you think it will last?"
"I… do not know…?"
Eisheth tilted her head in confusion.
"I do not either."
Nux answered.
"I just… feel that if I do not complete our Universe soon, it might fall out of existence."
"But that…"
Felberta wanted to say something, but she couldn’t. She realized she couldn’t counter Nux’s words.
This feeling of his—it might even be his Universe’s way of warning him.
They couldn’t just ignore it.
"So this is the reason you wish to gather all the Primordial Energies and complete your Universe."
"That is correct."
Nux nodded.
"I wish to survive, together with all of you, and I will do everything in my power to make it happen."
"Why didn’t you tell us before?"
Thyra questioned, not liking that Nux was keeping secrets from her.
"I didn’t know how to. I still cannot explain it and I did not wish to worry you. All of you should focus on getting stronger—that is the only way you can help me."
A wide grin then appeared on Nux’s face and,
"Just imagining myself being protected by my seventeen Infinity-Level Wives as my enemies cower in fear makes me wish to live that moment right now."
The women smiled as well. Nux was right, just imagining that scene made them feel butterflies in their stomachs.
It was quite a beautiful feeling.
They all wanted to protect Nux from his enemies for once.
"Alright then,"
Suddenly, Thyra spoke up.
"Let’s leave."
She declared.
"Hmm?"
Nux tilted his head.
"Let’s return to the Main Universe."
The cat raised her voice.
"It doesn’t matter what the Theory says, it doesn’t matter if our Universe should exist or not. The only thing that does matter,
Is that none of us are going down without a fight."
Thyra then stared at Nux with her piercing blue eyes and repeated her words,
"None of us."
Nux’s smile widened, he nodded back and once again,
The Leander Family returned to the Main Universe.
And this time, they had plans of a much, much bigger scale.

chapters.title: Chapter 2023: Tell me what happened.
paragraphs: Faustina rushed into her son’s arms and hugged him as tightly as she could.
"You are back!"
"Mother."
Nux greeted with a smile on his face as he hugged her back.

He had just returned to the Main Universe and was greeted by Faelara. The woman knew his wives’ condition and waited till he was done spending time with them, and her cue to all this was Nux returning to the Main Universe.
The moment that happened, she revealed herself without wasting a moment. Clearly, she was missing her son.
"You scared me."
Faustina spoke, her voice slightly weak.

Nux was an important part of her life, not just because he practically saved her and changed her foundation from a partial, incomplete being at her world’s mercy to someone who could exist independently and aim to get stronger, much stronger than before, but also because Nux had given her something that she never truly felt before.
A child’s love.
Yes, she was the Human Progenitor, the Mother of All Humans, but…

She never once felt that love before. When her first child was born, she was busy reproducing more. As humans, who were the weakest and had the fastest reproduction, it had become hers and Caesar’s duty to populate the Union and understand the concept of reproduction.

By the time other Progenitors joined and tried reproduction themselves, her children had already grown quite a bit and had grown more attached to other Progenitors, who were there for them when their own parents weren’t.
Of course, at that time, Faustina didn’t understand what she had lost; she had never experienced a child’s love anyway, so it didn’t matter.

Even later, when the Union of Progenitors got more and more stable and their strength grew, giving them more leisure time, whenever Faustina gave birth to a child, she simply handed them over to other Progenitors to raise since she herself felt lazy.
This continued for thousands and thousands of years until…
Nux appeared.

Yes, Nux was Faustina’s first true son, a son she actually loved like a mother, and when he disappeared for 4492 years (women rounded this time to 5000, yes, girl math), Faustina lost her mind. She didn’t even dare to return to Nux’s Universe because she feared that she might collapse and become a burden to her son’s wives, who were already devastated as it was.
Even when the rest of the Progenitors tried to comfort her, it didn’t work. Her racing, uneasy heart only calmed when she hugged Nux again.
"You really really really scared me…"
Faustina repeated her words, her body trembling in her son’s embrace, a hot stream of tears rolling down her cheeks, tears she had been holding in for a long, long time now.
Nux felt his heart squeeze when he sensed his mother’s condition. He tightened his hug around her, letting her hold him for as long as she liked, an offer Faustina didn’t refuse.
The wives, who saw this scene, just smiled. Even Amaya, who had finally returned to her senses and agreed to return to the Main Universe and fight alongside her husband, was the same.
Time went by, Faustina stayed in this position for hours, until suddenly,
’Faus.’
She heard a voice in her head.
It was Caesar.
’You have been gone for a long time, have you told him yet?’
Caesar questioned.
’I… have not.’
Faustina answered, a little hesitant.
’Do it. We do not have much time.’
’Yes, just a little longer…’
Faustina answered as she kept her eyes closed and Nux close to her.
’Faus.’
A few minutes later, Caesar called again.

’He has started aging. If something happens to him, that girl will be devastated, and his heart won’t be able to take it. He is back now, you can have him for yourself later, but first, do what needs to be done.’
He spoke, his tone much more solemn than before.
Faustina was silent.
Soon, however, she glanced at Nux. Nux, who noticed her strange gaze, frowned.
"What is it?"
He questioned directly, knowing his mother wanted to say something.
"It’s…"
Faustina waited for a moment as if gathering her thoughts.
"It is about Azriel."

She spoke, and the instant she mentioned those words, Aeliana’s ears perked up. She wanted to meet her father for a long time since she was so devastated. However, after the first few times, Azriel went into closed-door cultivation because he wanted to form a new, stronger Law, and ever since then, he hadn’t met her.
"Ah, Lord Azriel."

It wasn’t just Aeliana. Nux’s attention instantly shifted when he heard his father-in-law’s name. He still remembered different variations of his father-in-law he saw back in the Temple. It was fun, but it made him miss the real one.
Also, he was curious as to how strong the man had gotten in these 5000 years. With the rate at which he was cultivating, Nux wouldn’t be surprised if he was a Transcendent already.
"How strong is he now?"
Nux questioned directly.
"No wait, first tell me what Law did he form. Is it the same one? Or is it something different this time?"
Yes, Nux was having his fangirling moment.𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮
But…
"He is a Saint and hasn’t formed his Law yet."
Faustina revealed, and, in an instant, Nux’s expression changed.
And as if she was purposefully trying to make things worse,
"And since Saints cannot live for more than 5000 years…
He only has a few decades left."
"WHAT!?"

Aeliana’s eyes widened in horror. She quickly appeared next to Faustina and unconsciously released her Aura. Faustina, who was still just a Primordial because she was solidifying her foundation, was overpowered and was about to collapse, but Nux quickly saved her with a wave of his hand, nullifying Aeliana’s pressure.
"What do you mean he only has a few decades left? Why wasn’t I informed of this?"
The Vampire raised her voice, her crimson eyes shining so threateningly that it was suffocating to even watch.
Faustina’s body trembled. Once again, Nux stepped in front of her, but this time, it didn’t calm her. In the end, Nux waved his hand, and suddenly,
Aeliana was devoured by her own shadow, returning to Nux’s Universe. Nux turned towards Vyriana and,
"Take care of her."
The Dragon nodded and disappeared as well.
Once that was done, Nux turned back to Faustina and,
"Tell me what happened."

chapters.title: Chapter 2024: Yes, yes, I missed you as well.
paragraphs: "Tell me what happened."
Nux spoke, his voice calm since he didn't wish to overwhelm Faustina, who was affected by Aeliana's gaze.
He hugged her tightly and constantly patted her back. The woman only calmed down after a few minutes, and then, after taking a deep breath, she began,
"The Anomaly was gone for thousands of years."
And that was all Nux needed to understand what happened; he, however, let Faustina continue.
"Since the Anomaly hadn't appeared for such a long time, the Universe no longer needed a Hero. According to Azriel, the Universe felt threatened."
"Threatened?"
Nux frowned.
"Of Lord Azriel?"
"Yes."
Faustina nodded.
"It seemed like the Universe didn't wish to end up like Yrniel and be dependent on Azriel. However, with the Anomaly roaming wild and destroying it from inside, it had no other choice.
It prepared and connected itself to Azriel; however, after a while, the Anomaly completely disappeared.
It was a good thing, and for the first few centuries, the Universe seemed happy; however, Azriel's progress was too quick.

Within just a few centuries, he had already reached the Semi Saint Stage, and because he was pretty much doing this for the third time, his Foundation was much, much stronger than any known being in the entire Universe.

The rate at which he was growing, reaching Infinity was only a matter of time, maybe about 2000 years; heck, Azriel even mentioned how he could reach a level beyond Infinity, a level where every being in the Universe could only bow to him,
A level where he could overpower all other Infinities with a mere gaze and… threaten the Universe itself."
"But he shouldn't be able to do that, the Universe made sure of that."
Nux frowned.
"Yes."
Faustina nodded.
"The Universe formed an interdependent relationship with Azriel so that he would not turn against it, just like Yrniel did."
Nux nodded at those words; he knew about it.
"But…"
Faustina began.
"Why be dependent on someone when there was no need to?"
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"The Anomaly was gone, the Supreme Worlds were never strong enough to threaten it because they would never be able to work together, the only threat to the Universe was…"
"The Universe's Child."
Nux completed his mother's sentence.
"Indeed."
Faustina nodded.

"So it started slowing down Azriel's progress, to a degree where even after thousands of years had passed, more than enough time for Azriel to reach Infinity Stage, he had only managed to reach the Saint Stage and is nowhere close to breaking through.
His body had also started aging, it seems that the Universe was planning on getting rid of him through natural causes by not allowing him to grow any further."
Nux's expression turned cold when he heard those words.
"That thing sure is selfish."
He commented with a smile that did not look like a smile at all.
Just thinking what would have happened if he had been a little late made him tremble in fear; now he didn't particularly care about his Father-in-law too much, but Aeliana…
He promised he would never let her get hurt again. If her father lost his life, she would have been devastated.

Nux clenched his fists, he closed his eyes and sensed Aeliana's raging emotions. The woman wanted to meet her father as soon as possible; the only reason she wasn't causing chaos all over the place was because Shadow was holding her down using her power and influence over Nux's Universe.
Yes, even Vyriana, who had become a Transcendent, was not a match for the Vampire who seemed to have lost herself.
Nux even wanted to calm her down; however, he knew nothing he said would work here. There was only one way to calm her down,
And that was exactly what he was planning to do.
'Girls, I need your help.'
He called out and in an instant, Amaya, Felberta, Astaria, and Vyriana appeared beside him, nodding at him.
They were prepared.
Nux nodded back, he glanced at Faustina and,
"I will be back soon, Mother."
He spoke as he waved his hand, and he and his wives disappeared, appearing in a nearby Middle-Level world.
"Can I go all out?"
Astaria questioned, somewhat excited.
"Sure."
Nux nodded, and the Swordswoman's grin widened.
She turned towards the rest of her sisters and,
"The four of them are mine, do not interfere."
She spoke in a solemn tone as she sensed four Transcendents in the World.
"Whatever."
Vyriana shrugged. Even though she wanted to test her strength, she would do it later and let her disciple-cum-sparring partner have a go.
Amaya and Felberta nodded as well, both of them were patient women; yes, even Amaya.
With a wide grin on her face, Astaria disappeared and appeared in front of the first Transcendent.

He looked like a human, but his body was woven from living vines, bark, moss, and crystal-like sap. His skin shimmered with green, brown, gold, or deep autumn red. His eyes glowed faintly like embers trapped inside leaves. He wore a crown of thorns on his head.
He had an intimidating Aura around him, and the moment he saw Astaria appear in front of him out of nowhere,
"Who are you?"
He questioned, alarmed.
"You will need your buddies, call them."
The woman grinned like a maniac as she grabbed her sword.
"You are too arrogant for a huma—"

The being tried to put her down; however, before he could even complete his words, Astaria moved her sword, a wave of energy rushed towards him, an energy that wouldn't even scratch the vines on his body…
Or that is what he believed.
But…
Slice
His entire arm was chopped off in an instant, the entire process was so smooth that it felt like cutting butter.
"AAAGGGGGGHHHH!!!!"
He screamed in pain; Astaria, on the other hand, just placed her sword back on the ground and,
"Last chance, call your allies."
She spoke, the wide grin on her face still hadn't disappeared.
Yes, the Swordswoman was finally strong enough to help Nux and become the nightmare she was meant to be.
The battle between her and the three Transcendents lasted an entire minute before she got bored and sliced them all.
She grabbed their severed heads and brought them to Nux. She even knelt in front of him like a warrior offering heads to her King in exchange for rewards, something that made Nux laugh out loud.
He picked her up and sealed her lips,
Then, he stepped forward and with the possible hindrance now gone, he released his pressure, prepared to devour the World.
And just as he did,
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe reacted, to which Nux just laughed.
"Yes, yes, I missed you as well."
The Anomaly was back.

It prepared and connected itself to Azriel; however, after a while, the Anomaly completely disappeared.
It was a good thing, and for the first few centuries, the Universe seemed happy; however, Azriel's progress was too quick.

Within just a few centuries, he had already reached the Semi Saint Stage, and because he was pretty much doing this for the third time, his Foundation was much, much stronger than any known being in the entire Universe.

The rate at which he was growing, reaching Infinity was only a matter of time, maybe about 2000 years; heck, Azriel even mentioned how he could reach a level beyond Infinity, a level where every being in the Universe could only bow to him,
A level where he could overpower all other Infinities with a mere gaze and… threaten the Universe itself."
"But he shouldn't be able to do that, the Universe made sure of that."
Nux frowned.
"Yes."
Faustina nodded.
"The Universe formed an interdependent relationship with Azriel so that he would not turn against it, just like Yrniel did."
Nux nodded at those words; he knew about it.
"But…"
Faustina began.
"Why be dependent on someone when there was no need to?"
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"The Anomaly was gone, the Supreme Worlds were never strong enough to threaten it because they would never be able to work together, the only threat to the Universe was…"
"The Universe's Child."
Nux completed his mother's sentence.
"Indeed."
Faustina nodded.

"So it started slowing down Azriel's progress, to a degree where even after thousands of years had passed, more than enough time for Azriel to reach Infinity Stage, he had only managed to reach the Saint Stage and is nowhere close to breaking through.
His body had also started aging, it seems that the Universe was planning on getting rid of him through natural causes by not allowing him to grow any further."
Nux's expression turned cold when he heard those words.
"That thing sure is selfish."
He commented with a smile that did not look like a smile at all.
Just thinking what would have happened if he had been a little late made him tremble in fear; now he didn't particularly care about his Father-in-law too much, but Aeliana…
He promised he would never let her get hurt again.
If her father lost his life, she would have been devastated.
Nux clenched his fists, he closed his eyes and sensed Aeliana's raging emotions.

The woman wanted to meet her father as soon as possible; the only reason she wasn't causing chaos all over the place was because Shadow was holding her down using her power and influence over Nux's Universe.
Yes, even Vyriana, who had become a Transcendent, was not a match for the Vampire who seemed to have lost herself.
Nux even wanted to calm her down; however, he knew nothing he said would work here.
There was only one way to calm her down,
And that was exactly what he was planning to do.
'Girls, I need your help.'
He called out and in an instant, Amaya, Felberta, Astaria, and Vyriana appeared beside him, nodding at him.
They were prepared.
Nux nodded back, he glanced at Faustina and,
"I will be back soon, Mother."
He spoke as he waved his hand, and he and his wives disappeared, appearing in a nearby Middle-Level world.
"Can I go all out?"
Astaria questioned, somewhat excited.
"Sure."
Nux nodded, and the Swordswoman's grin widened.
She turned towards the rest of her sisters and,
"The four of them are mine, do not interfere."
She spoke in a solemn tone as she sensed four Transcendents in the World.
"Whatever."
Vyriana shrugged.
Even though she wanted to test her strength, she would do it later and let her disciple-cum-sparring partner have a go.
Amaya and Felberta nodded as well, both of them were patient women; yes, even Amaya.
With a wide grin on her face, Astaria disappeared and appeared in front of the first Transcendent.
He looked like a human, but his body was woven from living vines, bark, moss, and crystal-like sap.
His skin shimmered with green, brown, gold, or deep autumn red.
His eyes glowed faintly like embers trapped inside leaves.
He wore a crown of thorns on his head.
He had an intimidating Aura around him, and the moment he saw Astaria appear in front of him out of nowhere,
"Who are you?"
He questioned, alarmed.
"You will need your buddies, call them."
The woman grinned like a maniac as she grabbed her sword.
"You are too arrogant for a huma—"

The being tried to put her down; however, before he could even complete his words, Astaria moved her sword, a wave of energy rushed towards him, an energy that wouldn't even scratch the vines on his body…
Or that is what he believed.
But…
Slice
His entire arm was chopped off in an instant, the entire process was so smooth that it felt like cutting butter.
"AAAGGGGGGHHHH!!!!"
He screamed in pain; Astaria, on the other hand, just placed her sword back on the ground and,
"Last chance, call your allies."
She spoke, the wide grin on her face still hadn't disappeared.
Yes, the Swordswoman was finally strong enough to help Nux and become the nightmare she was meant to be.
The battle between her and the three Transcendents lasted an entire minute before she got bored and sliced them all.
She grabbed their severed heads and brought them to Nux.
She even knelt in front of him like a warrior offering heads to her King in exchange for rewards, something that made Nux laugh out loud.
He picked her up and sealed her lips,
Then, he stepped forward and with the possible hindrance now gone, he released his pressure, prepared to devour the World.
And just as he did,
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe reacted, to which Nux just laughed.
"Yes, yes, I missed you as well."
The Anomaly was back.

chapters.title: Chapter 2025: Law of Independent Absoluteness.
paragraphs: THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE

The Universe trembled, and a certain being with long blackish-white hair, sitting at the very edge of the Universe with his eyes closed, slowly opened his crimson eyes and tilted his head in confusion.
"Hmm? Am I not dead yet?"
He questioned out loud, completely ignoring all the chaos around him.
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe trembled even further, almost as if it was affected by the man's words.
Again, the man ignored it and stared at his own arms that had wrinkles all around them.
"Ah, there are still a few years left."
The being nodded. He, who had already accepted his weak fate, closed his eyes again. He seemed like he was done with his life and was prepared to die, leaving everything behind.
He had suffered enough; it was now time to return to the two women he loved.
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
At his actions, the Universe trembled again, and suddenly, a huge meteor that was hovering around the man's body flew next to him, gently touching him.
Yes, the very Universe was trying to call him.
The man frowned, the wrinkles on his handsome face gave him a certain charm. Once again, he opened his dull, weary eyes and,
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe trembled again, almost as if trying to say something.
"Hmm?"
The being finally caught on.
"The Anomaly is back?"
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe reacted, as if nodding to those words.
"Oh…"
The being nodded.
But then,
"So what?"

He questioned out loud, and before the Universe could react again, a wry, weak smile appeared on the man's face as he stared at his arms that once had endless power coursing through them but now looked frail.
"Look at me, I failed.

In hopelessness, I killed myself before. You gave me a second chance at life and I failed you. I couldn't even break through the Divine Stage and have been stuck at the Saint Stage for thousands of years now.
The Anomaly is here?
What is a failure like me supposed to do anyway? Am I not just a disappointment who cannot even cultivate anymore?
I am a weak, broken man who is nothing more than a former shell of himself; there is nothing I can do.
I'd say you choose another Hero."
Azriel spoke as he closed his eyes in hopelessness again.
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe trembled, trying to say something again.
"What am I supposed to do even if I went there? It is useless."
Azriel shook his head again.
"Hmm? Be your eyes? And what then? The moment he realizes I am there, he will disappear. I am too weak to even be your eyes.
Again, just choose another Hero."
Azriel answered as he then smiled ever so lightly. A smile that even the Universe couldn't catch.
Nux was back; it was finally his turn to get what he wanted.
Since the Universe dared to throw him away, he would do the same.
Azriel, who was connected to the Universe all this while but couldn't cultivate, had decided to understand the very Universe itself, and by now, he had gotten quite a good understanding of it.
The Universe cannot choose another Hero.
It was bound to one, so unless Azriel dies, which itself would take a few more decades, the Second Hero cannot be chosen.
Another reason was that it wasn't exactly easy to choose a Hero.

The Universe couldn't just choose anyone at random; not only did the being need to have an absurd potential that should at least be enough for him to reach the Infinity Stage without the Universe's help, the being should also be somewhat trustworthy.
This was the reason the Infinities from the Supreme Worlds weren't chosen.
Azriel was the best and only choice.
And Azriel was going to use that to take every possible advantage he could.
In the end, the Universe forcibly moved Azriel to where the Anomaly was; Azriel, however, kept his eyes closed, not giving the Universe anything to work with.

Just like that, the Anomaly was done devouring the World and went to another. By now, Amaya, Felberta, Astaria, and Vyriana had divided the task. They all went to different worlds, killed their World Leaders, and waited for Nux to come and devour the World. After a while, Aeliana, who wanted to help her father, joined in as well. Because of that, the Anomaly's speed in devouring worlds had gotten even more absurd.
Even when the Universe constantly sent Azriel after the Anomaly, before Azriel could come to his senses, the Anomaly would disappear and devour another world.
12 Worlds were devoured.
Azriel, who was now left alone, shrugged as he closed his eyes again, almost as if he didn't care what happened.
The Universe was obviously angry; it constantly tried to converse with Azriel, but the Vampire was just too depressed to say anything.
And this didn't stop with just this.
It continued.
The next day, the Anomaly returned.
10 more worlds were devoured.
Then 11 more.
Day after day, the Anomaly continued to appear at a specific time and devour different worlds.
The Universe was losing its mind.
It was completely helpless since the Anomaly didn't stop at anything. Nux, the Anomaly, had absolutely no weaknesses; even the Universe couldn't do anything against it.
The only option it had was…
Azriel.
In the end, under the Anomaly's constant assault, even the mighty Universe had to give in.
The Universal Energy around Azriel, which he couldn't control and absorb for thousands of years, suddenly started moving on its own before it entered Azriel's body, making him stronger.
'Hmm?'
Azriel frowned, unable to believe what was happening.
Soon, however, he met another restriction,
A Law.
He had to form a Law.
The moment Azriel got the chance, he smiled lightly, then, he formed a Law.
A newer, stronger Law.
Law of Independent Absoluteness.

An advanced version of the Law of Absolute, just that this time, Azriel no longer needed to rely on the Universe or the Universal Energy to get stronger, but was very much capable of absorbing any form of energy from any source and turning it into Universal Energy.
A Law the Universe would normally never let him form, since it was simply too strong,
But in its desperation, it had no other choice.
BOOOOOOOOM
And just like that,
Azriel Ruinous broke through.
