chapters.title: Chapter 2026: The Universe is not a Child.
paragraphs: "Father!"
Aeliana quickly hugged her now, once again young Father as tightly as she could. Azriel hugged her back with a light smile on his face, constantly patting her back to calm her racing heart.
"Why didn't you say anything…?"
Aeliana, who was finally in her father's embrace again, cried.

Azriel opened his mouth but no words came out. There were too many things in his mind. Nux hadn't returned for five thousand years and honestly, Azriel had assumed the worst. His daughter was already devastated and he wasn't brave enough to share his own situation with her.
Yes, it was an extremely selfish decision, but Azriel couldn't do anything. He couldn't let his daughter suffer more than she already had.
Nux understood that feeling. This was also the reason he stayed silent; he just stared at Azriel, who, after a while, stared back at him, and the two nodded at each other.
"You sure caused a scene."
Azriel spoke up. Nux, however, stared at Aeliana who was still hugging her father and,
"I doubt you get to say that."
Azriel couldn't retort.
The two laughed a little and then,
"Thank you."
Azriel expressed his gratitude.
No matter what, the fact remained that Nux saved him.
"I guess we are even now?"
Nux smiled.
Azriel saved him once when he appeared in front of the Supreme Infinities who were trying to look when he devoured a world for the first time.
That act saved his life and now, he was even.
"I won't help you again, Father-in-Law."
"Likewise."
Azriel nodded arrogantly.

With his dependency on the Universe now over, his path ahead would be quite simpler. He was the first man who formed a Law that shouldn't exist in any way since the Universe just didn't allow its formation.
Azriel wanted to see how far it took him.
Nux wasn't any different either; he was quite curious as to how strong his Father-in-Law would be once he became a Primordial.

Yes, even now, he was looking forward to their spar, just that deep inside, he knew even if Azriel became a Primordial, the two of them could never fight simply because the Universe would then sense his presence and act.
'I will still win though.'
Nux thought inwardly as he stared at his Father-in-Law.𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮
He then chuckled and shook his head; even now, his mind was constantly thinking of ways to somehow comprehend his Father-in-Law's Law.
"I heard you formed your own Time."
While Nux was thinking all this, Azriel questioned.
"I did. Different Universes have different Time, so—"
"So your Universe needed its own Unique Time, I understand."
Azriel nodded, making Nux frown.
This… wasn't something just anyone would know…
Knowing what he was thinking, Azriel laughed lightly,
"I have closely inspected our Universe for thousands of years now. I may not know much about other Universes, but if it is about this Universe, I do know quite a bit.
How else do you think I formed my Law?"
"A Law to be completely independent of any Cultivation Bridge, huh…"
Nux muttered.
Just thinking of being able to follow any Cultivation System without any hindrances or bottlenecks at all…
It was… quite liberating.
Azriel smiled.
"So? What's next?"
The Vampire questioned.
"You already got Time, what's left?"
"Light, Darkness, Balance, Chaos."
Nux answered instantly and a wry smile appeared on Azriel's face.
"So the Energies of the Four Supreme Energies, huh…"
"Indeed. I have tried to look for them in other Worlds, from the Lowest Level to Middle-Level Worlds, but no being has formed a Law related to these Energies."
"That's not true."
Azriel shook his head.
"There were beings who formed Laws related to these energies. The Supreme Worlds just recruited those people and their families, something they accepted readily."
Since he was connected to the Universe, the amount of things he knew was quite a lot as well.
"So every single person accepted that offer?"
"Not really. Just that those who didn't were erased."
Azriel shrugged.
Nux nodded casually as well.
Azriel then stared into his son-in-law's eyes and,
"I will still say not to go against the Supreme Worlds right now, especially now more than ever."
"Hmm? What does that mean?"
Nux frowned.
"The Four Supreme Worlds have formed an alliance."
"Huh…?"
Nux blinked.
"They formed an alliance? Why?"
"To find the Universe's Child."
Azriel smiled wryly.

"For thousands of years, they have been doubting each other, but since the Universe wanted to get rid of me, it shared that the Anomaly is someone out of the Four existing Supreme Worlds and is still growing stronger.
So those people are out to hunt down the Universe's Child."
"Why would the Universe do that?"
"To get rid of me, of course.
I had turned into a deadweight, remember? Anomaly was gone, I had no more use and waiting for me to perish on my own was a pain, so it decided to use them."
"Then how are you still alive?"
"Because the Universe was hiding me."
Azriel laughed.
"Huh?"
Nux frowned; he had absolutely no clue what his Father-in-Law was talking about, and Azriel knew that.
"We cannot tell what the Universe is thinking. I have been trying to understand it for thousands of years and I have failed."
"I thought the Universe was childish."
Nux muttered, and Azriel shook his head.
"It is not childish, it's just…
Its perception is different than ours. If it was a child, then one of the Four Supreme Worlds would have taken over the entire Universe by now.
A child, no matter how strong, cannot remain in existence for trillions of years."
The Vampire spoke with a solemn look on his face.
Then, he glanced at Nux and returned to the topic,
"Anyways, what I am saying is, be careful of the Supreme Worlds; right now, they are at their strongest."
"Don't worry, I will first target Chaos."
Nux answered.
Azriel, who already knew who Nux was talking about, answered.
"It won't be easy; even the Universe cannot detect him."
Nux, however, just grinned menacingly.
"That's the fun part. I don't need to detect him. I already know where that man is."
Azriel stared at Nux for a moment, then, he nodded.
"I wish you luck."
"Thank you."
Nux's grin widened.
"I will see you soon, Father-in-Law."
He spoke as he bowed his head, then, with a wave of his hand, he disappeared and appeared in front of a Middle-Level World.
It was now time to join the War and this time, they weren't just going to join it.
They were going to flip it over and over again.
It was time for the entire Universe to know about the Leander Family.

"I thought the Universe was childish."
Nux muttered, and Azriel shook his head.
"It is not childish, it's just…
Its perception is different than ours.
If it was a child, then one of the Four Supreme Worlds would have taken over the entire Universe by now.
A child, no matter how strong, cannot remain in existence for trillions of years."
The Vampire spoke with a solemn look on his face.
Then, he glanced at Nux and returned to the topic,
"Anyways, what I am saying is, be careful of the Supreme Worlds; right now, they are at their strongest."
"Don't worry, I will first target Chaos."
Nux answered.
Azriel, who already knew who Nux was talking about, answered.
"It won't be easy; even the Universe cannot detect him."
Nux, however, just grinned menacingly.
"That's the fun part.
I don't need to detect him.
I already know where that man is."
Azriel stared at Nux for a moment, then, he nodded.
"I wish you luck."
"Thank you."
Nux's grin widened.
"I will see you soon, Father-in-Law."
He spoke as he bowed his head, then, with a wave of his hand, he disappeared and appeared in front of a Middle-Level World.
It was now time to join the War and this time, they weren't just going to join it.
They were going to flip it over and over again.
It was time for the entire Universe to know about the Leander Family.

chapters.title: Chapter 2027: Let the show begin, shall we?
paragraphs: A 3-meter-tall being who had the torso of a man and the lower body of a giant scorpion was walking back into his tent. His body was covered in dark, hard armor that shined faintly under the light. Sharp plates protected his chest and arms, and his hands ended in strong, claw-like fingers.

A thick, powerful tail curled over his back, tipped with a deadly stinger that dripped with poison. His legs were strong and bent backward like an insect's, helping him move quickly and quietly. His eyes were narrow and sharp, glowing a deep red, and small horns poked out from the sides of his head.
He had an overbearing and menacing appearance, and his character further enhanced this impression.
*Picture*
This being was a Scorvane, beings from a Middle-Level World named Saccharis, one of the direct subordinates of Khaemorr, the High-Level World led by the Princess who rose from the Chains, Sharnoth.
And this being in particular, Dulcia Von Saccharis, was the Progenitor of Scorvane, a Transcendent-Level Being, the strongest of his World.
Right now, Dulcia and his men were at War with another Middle-Level World of the enemy Faction named Gelatina. The camps were set, the men were gathered, War could start any moment now.
Dulcia was only waiting for the Queen's signal. The moment he got it, his army would invade Gelatina and destroy them.

For now, however, he was returning to his tent to get some time alone and calm his nerves. Even if he had invaded 10 Worlds for her Queen and won every battle, he was still nervous, as every Army leader should be.
It wasn't a sign of weakness, it meant that he cared, he was a good leader.
"Haaahh…"
With a deep sigh, Dulcia returned to his tent, but the moment he walked in, he froze.
A being he didn't recognize was sitting inside his tent and he...
He seemed quite comfortable.
"You are late. I have been waiting for a while, you know?"
The being smiled.
He had long black hair, purple eyes, horns, and a ridiculously handsome face.
Yes, it was Nux in his Devil Form.
"Who are you?"
Dulcia questioned with a wary look on his face. He couldn't sense his strength. What's even worse was that Saccharis's Will didn't inform him about his arrival.

Even now, it couldn't sense him. This being had a way to escape a World's senses; it was a ridiculously strong and useful ability. Dulcia could already think of ways to put this to use, for now, however, he knew he needed to deal with whoever this being was.
He clenched his claws, his tense body was prepared to act the moment it was required, but then,
"You are too tense, Dulcia, calm down.
If I wanted to hurt you, you wouldn't be standing right now."
Nux spoke with a light, calming smile on his face. His words may sound arrogant, but they weren't false.

Sure, the being in front of him was a Transcendent, but his Law wasn't a threat to him. As long as he dodged all the attacks, which itself wasn't difficult because of his mastery over space, he couldn't lose.
"…Why are you here?"
Dulcia questioned, still wary.
"Your Queen, I wish to communicate with her."
"The Queen isn't her—"
"I know that."
Nux interrupted.
"I want you to tell her that a potential ally wishes to talk to her."
Nux then threw a Call Artifact towards Dulcia and,
"Deliver this to her. Tell her she can contact me the moment she activates it."
Dulcia grabbed the Artifact and frowned.
"Why not go to her?"
He questioned directly.
He could see it, the being in front of him was strong. Since he couldn't sense his strength, he might even be a Peak Eternity-Level Being, someone even stronger than his Queen.
Why wasn't someone like him using him to contact his Queen?
Was this a trap?
But would such a strong being put enough effort to set a trap?
Or…
Was this being not as strong as he was thinking and was just putting up a fake front?
He had a way to hide his existence from the World's Will. It wouldn't be shocking if he had a way to hide his cultivation; such artifacts were rare, but they did exist.
'So he is faking it…?'
Dulcia frowned.
'Is this the reason he doesn't wish to directly meet the Queen?'
"I have my reasons."
Nux answered, oblivious to Dulcia's thoughts. Dulcia, on the other hand, continued thinking,
'Is he afraid of the Queen? But then what's the plan? Why does he wish to talk to the Queen anyways? What did he want to say?'
The more he thought, the more questions appeared in his mind.
In the end, however, he just shook his head and stopped thinking about this.
"Find someone else or go to her yourself."
He answered.
He had an entire War to worry about; he couldn't waste his time with some random man he didn't even know.
"Hmm?"
Nux frowned, a little taken aback. Soon, however, he realized the problem.𝓯𝙧𝙚𝒆𝙬𝙚𝒃𝙣𝙤𝒗𝓮𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
"Oh, I am not asking you to do this for free."
He began.
He was a good man.
Since he was here to ask for a favor, he had come with a gift.
"What do you mean?"
Dulcia narrowed his eyes.
"I have something for you."
"I do not need anythi—"
Before Dulcia could complete his words, Nux interrupted.
"You will love it, trust me. Just wait a little. It will start very soon."
"What are you even talking about?"
Dulcia's frown deepened; he was getting annoyed, he was even prepared to attack this man and end his existence, but then,
Bzzzz
Another Artifact Nux was holding started buzzing.
"It started."

Nux grinned as he infused his energy into the Artifact, and the Artifact projected a huge screen in front of both Nux and Dulcia, and the instant Dulcia saw what the screen was showing, his expression changed.
This place...
He knew what it was...
Gelatina, a World he was at War with and was about to invade.
"Let the show begin, shall we?"
Nux questioned as he glanced at a certain black-haired, crimson-eyed woman, who was walking into the enemy Army Leader's camp with a light, joyful smile on her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 2028: The Law of Eternal Drift.
paragraphs: A 2.5-meter-tall, graceful being made of soft, glowing mist was sitting on a chair.
His body had no hard edges—it flowed and shifted like smoke, but he still had a clear shape, like a monster dressed in robes of starlight.
His skin shimmered with colors like blue, purple, and silver, always moving like a slow river.
His eyes were bright and deep, like tiny galaxies spinning in the dark.
Around his head floated small rings of light, slowly turning without ever touching him.
He had long claws, and his body somewhat resembled a knight.
*Picture*
He was Praline Gelatina, the Progenitor and the Leader of the Nebuliths, a race that led the World of Gelatina.
In front of Praline stood another Nebulith, his subordinate, who was here to make a report.
"The Scorvane look like they are ready for war. Their army is prepared, and they seem to be waiting for a signal. They can attack at any moment now."
"So they are going to follow through with it, huh…"
Praline muttered with a solemn look on his face.
"They will."
The subordinate nodded.
As unusual as it sounds, an army that had constantly invaded 10 different worlds was now going to invade them.
"Hasn't their number diminished? How are they invading us so boldly?"
"According to our sources, their combined might overpowers us, but that advantage gets overwritten since we are fighting in our world. It will be a battle between equals.
There will be a lot of deaths."
The subordinate spoke up.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Praline stayed silent.
He wanted to avoid war if possible, but the enemy seemed hell-bent on sacrificing everything they had for their Queen.
A thought Praline didn't share, he had no loyalty to Aurendor, the High-Level World his world was associated with. He just participated in this foolish war because he had no other choice.
"Whatever, strengthen our defenses even further, prepare formations and defensive artifacts, and double the men on watch duty.
We need to be alert all the ti—"
"Who are yo—"
"You can't go i—"
Before Praline could complete his sentence, he heard two voices.
It was the guards guarding his tent. He stared at his subordinate, who stared back, as confused as him.
Praline stood up and tried to expand his senses to see what was going on, but then, his tent was torn open, and an extremely beautiful, black-haired woman walked in.
"Are you Praline Gelatina?"
The woman questioned.
Praline narrowed his eyes, not answering the woman's question. The woman, however, just chuckled.
"Who am I kidding? I know it is you."
She completely ignored the subordinate who stood right in front of her and stared at Praline instead.
"I will only say this once:
Surrender.
There is no need to spill any blood."
To those words, Praline grinned.
"Good for us then, don't you think?
We don't bleed."
The Nebulith Progenitor then stared at the woman in front of him and his claws elongated.
No more words were needed.
He didn't know why Gelatina couldn't sense this woman's presence, even though she was clearly from another world, but right now, it didn't matter.
It was clear that the woman was an enemy, and with how she dealt with the Primordial-Level Guards outside his tent, it wasn't wrong to assume she was a Transcendent.
Praline was the only being who could defeat her, so he stepped forward and,
BOOOOOM
He expanded his domain.
Different clashing energies swirled around, the very fabric of reality started to spin, and the ground beneath one's feet began to ripple, as if it was made of water.
The air became misty, as countless stars appeared around them.
The space itself stretched and softened, coaxing everything to slow and cease its frantic motion.
The sky rippled, and clouds of mist filled the space. The mist in the air glowed faintly with colors that changed continuously.
The Law of Eternal Drift.
A law that allowed him to drift for eternity.
In simpler words, it was a law that ensured that nothing in the universe could trap, freeze, or fully destroy him.
He could drift through matter, time, and even memories, like a cloud passing through mountains.
His power made everything around him soften, slow down, and lose its sharp edges.
A quite delicate, yet powerful law.
Especially inside his domain, where his law had become absolute.
Aeliana looked around, amused.
The battlefield vanished, replaced by vast, shifting nebulae and slow-moving cosmic tides.
The stars above twinkled lazily, and the ground was now covered in a soft layer of shining dust while Aeliana herself felt some restrictions being placed on her.
Very quickly, she started to understand these restrictions.
In this domain, nothing could move faster than a thought.
The laws of time and space bent to Praline's will, and everything within the sphere of his influence felt the drag of his Eternal Drift.
Even the strongest attacks could be dissolved into gentle currents of light and air, losing their power the moment they touched the mist.
Even Praline's existence itself seemed to have distributed all over his domain; he had become one with his domain.
'Are you seeing this?'
Aeliana questioned as she looked around.
'I am.'
Nux nodded.
'His power is quite… intriguing.'
He admitted.
'Do you want it?'
Aeliana questioned.
If yes, she could capture him alive for Nux to devour, but…

'Meh, the concept of bending time and space to his will is too foolish. It only works because he is facing weaker opponents. If he was up against someone like Faelara, who had absolute control over space, he would have lost his sense.'
Nux shook his head.
'His law just looks cool; it doesn't actually amount to anything.'
'So you don't want it?'
Aeliana questioned.
'I don't.'
And the moment those words were said, Aeliana stared back at the being in front of her and then,
Snap
She snapped, and Praline's beautiful, peaceful domain collapsed and was replaced by another, much, much more horrifying domain,
A Domain of Absolute Control.
A domain where even the Eternal Drifting… could be controlled.
"What did you say about not bleeding again?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2029: See? I told you I get good vibes from her.
paragraphs: "What did you say about not bleeding again?"
Dulcia stared at the screen in front of him with a solemn look on his face.
That…
That was his enemy.
An enemy he might have lost against, an enemy who could have stopped his winning streak because of how strong that man was…
Yet…
Here he was…
Annihilated by that woman as if he was nothing more than a bug.
"That was fast."
Nux, who was sitting right in front of the Scorvane, commented with a light smile on his face.
He then glanced at Dulcia and,
"So? How was the gift?"
"The G-Gift…?"
Dulcia stuttered, slightly confused.

Then suddenly, Nux's shadow trembled and rose up, materializing into something. At the same time, that monstrous woman, who had annihilated the strongest being in Gelatina like it was nothing, was engulfed by her shadow as well.
The woman disappeared, as if devoured by her shadow, and the shadow materializing in front of them finally solidified.
It was the same woman he was seeing on the screen.
And... she had brought Praline's severed head with her.
What's worse?
Just like this man in front of him, Saccharis's Will couldn't sense this woman either.
"He was right, he really didn't bleed."

Aeliana chuckled lightly as she observed the severed head in her arm. The thing felt like it was going to deform into mist if left alone. Aeliana was actually using her Law of Absolute Control to bind it together.
"How strange."
Nux chuckled as well.
"A being with no Core and no blood, yet a body that is so… sturdy."
"Mhm, they can be studied."
Aeliana nodded.
And Dulcia…

He just stared at this monster casually talking with the man sitting in front of him. From start to end, the woman didn't spare him even a single glance, almost as if his entire existence was of no significant importance.
Nux, who didn't wish for the poor fellow to feel left out, turned towards him and,
"Anyways, do you like the gift?"
He questioned as Aeliana threw the head towards Dulcia. He tried to catch it, however, the instant Aeliana released the head, it turned into mist and disappeared.
Praline Gelatina, the Progenitor of Nebuliths and the Leader of Gelatina, was erased out of existence just like that.
"Y-You…"
Suddenly, Dulcia realized something.
All this while, he felt that the woman in front of him was familiar, but he couldn't quite put a finger on it.
But now…
Now it finally clicked.
A few thousand years ago, he was told to investigate a certain group of mercenaries—mercenaries who had turned the battlefield into an incoherent mess.
This group of mercenaries was so strong that every time they participated in a war, the battles that had lasted for thousands of years ended within days.
They were so overpowering that no matter how powerful the enemies were, they always came out victorious. The party had never once failed to clear a mission.

The Lowest and Low-Level Worlds had turned into their stage. Things had become so ridiculous that even the Queen, who usually never cared about worlds of that level, heard about it and ordered her subordinates to search for this party.
The orders were clear.
Recruit this party or annihilate them.
Yes, Lowest and Low-Level Worlds did not matter in wars of such level, but the party was spreading too much chaos and uncertainty, which ultimately wasn't good for their Faction.
They also feared that the enemy would recruit them instead and things would become difficult at the Lower Levels.

While other subordinates didn't really care about some mercenaries who weren't even at the Transcendent Level, Dulcia was different. As someone completely loyal to his Queen, he took her orders to heart and sent his men to look for the said party.
They even sent out different missions with absurd rewards, missions that only their party could take, but no matter how much he tried,
He couldn't find them.
It was as if the entire party had disappeared.
The only thing he could find was the records of the previous wars they had participated in, and he learned everything he could about them.
Obviously, he didn't miss the mysterious black-haired, crimson-eyed Vampire who appeared every time this party was in danger and annihilated everything.
There was even a time when she defeated multiple Primordials, where their leader even had a Relic.
A black-haired, crimson-eyed woman with power over blood who could squash away Primordials like they were insects thousands of years ago…

That was his enemy.
An enemy he might have lost against, an enemy who could have stopped his winning streak because of how strong that man was…
Yet…

Annihilated by that woman as if he was nothing more than a bug.
"That was fast."

chapters.title: Chapter 2030: [We finally meet, The Princess who rose from the Chains.]
paragraphs: Chapter 2030: [We finally meet, The Princess who rose from the Chains.]
“My Queen.”
A being with greyish skin and crimson eyes called out in a low, respectful, but powerful voice.

The said being was easily one of the strongest Transcendents in Khaemorr, a being who had all the right to be arrogant and command almost any being in the world—even the other Transcendents. Right now, however, the being kept his head low. His crimson eyes showed respect so deep that it could easily be mistaken for reverence.
In front of him sat a beautiful, almost otherworldly being on a throne made of materials unknown to most of the world.
The woman was surrounded by darkness. She had long, wild greyish hair that flowed like smoke, and two massive, curved horns rose from her head, adding to her fearsome beauty.
Just like her subordinate, her eyes glowed red. They were sharp, cold, and dangerous, yet… strangely captivating.
Even when she had a serene, calm expression on her face, the presence she radiated was… intimidating—like the calm before a terrible storm.

She wore a black cloak that seemed to melt into the darkness around her, and tiny red sparks flickered near her, as if prepared to devour anyone who got too close. The space around her twisted ever so slightly, as if her presence was too strong and reality itself was struggling to contain her.
Her face had what seemed like cracks, as if her body was barely holding all her power together and was ready to burst. Honestly, it looked quite frightening.
However, despite how she looked, there was something noble in the way she carried herself—tall and proud.
She was terrifying… terrifyingly beautiful.
*Picture*
Yes, she was the Queen who rose from the Chains.
Sharnoth Nocthys.
“What is it?”
The Queen questioned, her crimson gaze falling on her subordinate.
“Dulcia Von Saccharis, the Progenitor of Scorvanes, the Leader of Saccharis, wishes to send you an artifact.
He says that a potential ally wishes to talk to you.”
“A potential ally?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
“Yes.
He says that if you wish to talk, you can activate the artifact he sends you.”
Sharnoth stayed silent, waiting for her subordinate to continue.
This matter obviously wasn’t something someone like her had to deal with—unless the ‘potential’ ally was from another High-Level World. Her subordinates should have been able to take care of it.
So if her subordinate had brought this up, Sharnoth was actually somewhat interested. Her subordinate’s next words, however, disappointed her.

“When I contacted Dulcia to know more about this potential ally, he told me that he is part of that mercenary party that rose a few thousand years ago and made a mess around the Lowest and Lower Level Worlds.”
“The one with a strange name?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“That is correct. It seems that the Vampire from that party has broken through and has become a Transcendent, quite a strong one.”
Follow new episodes on the "N0vel1st.c0m".
The subordinate nodded.
Sharnoth, however, was silent.
This time, a little disappointed.
Sure, she was interested in that mercenary party with the strange name, but that was it—she was merely curious. This didn’t mean she would personally go out of her way to discuss terms with them.
No matter how strong that Vampire was, in the end, she was just that—a Transcendent.
Actually, Sharnoth was now wondering why her subordinate even brought something like this up in the first place. He should have already activated the artifact and contacted the party.
As if he already knew what his Queen was thinking, the subordinate continued,
“I tried contacting them. However, the moment I got in contact with that being, something happened.”
Sharnoth frowned.
“He said, ‘You are not her,’ and ended the connection.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
The artifact in my hands turned into dust. It seems like it can only be used once.”
“Huh…?”
“He is looking for you, My Queen, and he refuses to talk to anyone but you.”
“A mere Transcendent wishes to talk to me?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow once again.
“Transcendent-level Vampire is his wife. We still do not know how strong that man is. He seems to have an artifact that hides his strength, and that artifact is quite strong.”
“Is that so…?”
Sharnoth nodded.
“Do you have an estimate as to how strong he is?”
She questioned. The subordinate, however, shook his head.
He was unsure.
The information he had was too limited, and this once again confused Sharnoth.
“Why did you bring this up, Shakel?”
She questioned directly.
She was getting impatient.
She didn’t have the time to deal with a Transcendent and her husband who seemed more interested in playing games than having an actual conversation.
The meta everyone followed in the universe was the same: if you wish to have a proper conversation, you reveal your origins and your strength.
If your origins are strong enough, the conversation can happen.
Yet, here he was, a member of a mere mercenary party, trying to talk to her while hiding his strength. Clearly, he was trying his luck, and Sharnoth still did not know why she was entertaining this.
If Shakel wasn’t one of her most loyal subordinates for a long time, she would have already dismissed him.
Right now, however, she decided to give Shakel the benefit of the doubt and allowed him to continue.
Shakel bowed his head and continued,
“Dulcia isn’t the only one who sent this, Your Majesty.”
“Huh…?”

“When I first contacted that man after receiving Dulcia’s message and he ended the connection, I simply decided to discard the matter because of how arrogant he seemed. It felt like he was doing all this for a show, and I didn’t wish to bother the Queen to deal with some fanatic who was interested in strange theatrics.
But then, I received more messages.
Mortifera Tenebris, the Progenitor of Ashen Veils, the High Arbiter of Oblivion,
Vespera Nocturna, the Progenitor of Twilight Spires, the Architect of Eternal Dusk,
Ignatius Pyreborn, the Progenitor of Emberflames, the Warden of the Burning Covenant,
Seraphina Obsidias, the Progenitor of Onyx Thorns, the Matriarch of the Shattered Sanctum,
And about fifteen other leaders of Middle-Level Worlds sent the same artifact—all with the same message.”
“Fifteen…?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
“Yes.

They also told me how this man’s wife annihilated their enemy’s Progenitors within a single move, and returned to them with their heads, solving wars that have been ongoing for thousands of years as a ‘gift’ to deliver this message.”
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes at those words. Her interest was once again piqued. Shakel, knowing this, continued further.
“Even if this was all theatrics, I could no longer ignore this.
Solving wars that have been going on for thousands of years within a single day—these beings clearly aren’t simple.

They definitely have a strong power over Space to teleport from one place to another. That Vampire is strong enough to completely ignore the effect of a World’s Suppression and deal with other Transcendents like they are mere bugs. They also seem to have another artifact that allows them to escape a World Will’s detection, making them nigh-perfect assassins.
They are resourceful.
Too resourceful, in fact.

If we could recruit them, we could change the entire course of the war in our favor. It will be the lead we have always been looking for, and eventually, Aurendor would have no choice but to face us directly.
It was a chance to finally get what we had been looking for all this while, so I decided to lower myself and activate another artifact, wanting to talk to that man again.
He tried to end the connection, but this time, I managed to get something out of him.
He…
He says he has a message for you.”
“A message for me?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“Yes.”
Shakel nodded.
“What is it?”
“He says he wishes to meet you alone.”
“Huh…?”
Sharnoth frowned. Shakel, on the other hand, stared at her and,
“I do not want anyone around her when we talk. Anyone. I wish to meet her alone, without her thoughts being influenced by someone.

This is what he said. He seemed quite adamant about you being alone when you talk to him. He even said that he wanted you to form a domain and alter it in a way that no being, in any form—be it body or Soul Form—other than you can survive in that doma—”
“What did you say?”
Sharnoth, who had barely shown any expression till now, suddenly reacted.
Shakel frowned.
“No one other than you should be in that domain…?”
He answered, repeating his words.
“The Soul Form—did that man use those words?”
“Yes, he did. I did not understand what it meant, but there were a lot of things that he said that didn’t make sense. The Queen does no—”
“Give me the artifact.”
Sharnoth demanded, interrupting Shakel again.
Shakel frowned. He did as he was told. His Queen’s actions, however, surprised him.
Sharnoth didn’t care. She grabbed the artifact, then she glanced at Shakel and,
“Leave.”
She ordered.
Even though he was confused, Shakel did as he was told obediently. Sharnoth, who was now left alone, suddenly spoke up.
“You too, leave.”
“Sharno—”
The Queen then activated an artifact and from the other side, she and the ‘Soul’ around her heard a voice—a voice the Soul found extremely familiar.
[We finally meet,
The Princess who rose from the Chains.]

It will be the lead we have always been looking for, and eventually, Aurendor would have no choice but to face us directly.
It was a chance to finally get what we had been looking for all this while, so I decided to lower myself and activate another artifact, wanting to talk to that man again.
He tried to end the connection, but this time, I managed to get something out of him.
He…
He says he has a message for you.”
“A message for me?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“Yes.”
Shakel nodded.
“What is it?”
“He says he wishes to meet you alone.”
“Huh…?”
Sharnoth frowned.
Shakel, on the other hand, stared at her and,
“I do not want anyone around her when we talk.
Anyone.
I wish to meet her alone, without her thoughts being influenced by someone.
This is what he said.
He seemed quite adamant about you being alone when you talk to him.
He even said that he wanted you to form a domain and alter it in a way that no being, in any form—be it body or Soul Form—other than you can survive in that doma—”
“What did you say?”
Sharnoth, who had barely shown any expression till now, suddenly reacted.
Shakel frowned.
“No one other than you should be in that domain…?”
He answered, repeating his words.
“The Soul Form—did that man use those words?”
“Yes, he did.
I did not understand what it meant, but there were a lot of things that he said that didn’t make sense.
The Queen does no—”
“Give me the artifact.”
Sharnoth demanded, interrupting Shakel again.
Shakel frowned.
He did as he was told.
His Queen’s actions, however, surprised him.
Sharnoth didn’t care.
She grabbed the artifact, then she glanced at Shakel and,
“Leave.”
She ordered.
Even though he was confused, Shakel did as he was told obediently.
Sharnoth, who was now left alone, suddenly spoke up.
“You too, leave.”
“Sharno—”
The Queen then activated an artifact and from the other side, she and the ‘Soul’ around her heard a voice—a voice the Soul found extremely familiar.
[We finally meet,
The Princess who rose from the Chains.]

chapters.title: Chapter 2031: I Declare War
paragraphs: Chapter 2031: I Declare War
[We finally meet,
The Princess who rose from the Chains.]
The moment Sharnoth activated the Artifact, she heard a calm, almost playful voice.
“Well, you have been trying to get in contact with me quite desperately. I simply decided to reward your effort.”
Sharnoth replied.
Her words were arrogant, her tone, however, seemed completely different. There was no trace of pride in her voice, it was… almost as if she was simply stating a fact.
As if she truly believed that her decision to talk to someone like Nux on her own was her ‘rewarding’ his efforts.
Nux smiled at that,
[I thank you for that.]
He remained humble.
After all, he was a humble, down-to-earth man.
[I believe that since you decided to activate the artifact, you must have agreed to my terms, correct?]
He questioned.
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes at that. Then, instead of answering Nux’s question, she asked one of her own,
“How much do you know?”
It was a question that placed a big grin on Nux’s face,
[Don’t worry, I won’t say. The Supreme Worlds will not know anything.
Snitching isn’t my style.]
“Snitching?”
Sharnoth frowned at the strange word.
Her mind, however, already started thinking, and slowly but steadily, the air around her was growing heavy.
This wasn’t good.
Even though Nux hadn’t directly answered her question, the very fact that he mentioned the Supreme Worlds and openly said he wouldn’t say anything to them told her all she needed to know.
Nux knew…
He knew about Zylarith Chaosveil, meaning that he had quite a bit of power over her.
After all, if he decided to reveal her Mentor’s existence to the Supreme Worlds and the four of them started acting on it,𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
Everything would end.
Everything she had worked for over the past tens of thousands of years—
It would all be for nought.

Sharnoth clenched her fists. Nux obviously couldn’t see that since he could only see her face and upper body through the screen, however, he could still sense that the woman didn’t believe him for even a single second.
Follow new episodes on the "N0vel1st.c0m".
Which made sense. After all, this was only their first meeting.
“Why are you here?”
Sharnoth questioned.
[Should you not start with basic introductions? Try to get to know me and stuff?]
Nux chuckled playfully but… Sharnoth was not amused.
Nux’s existence had become dangerous in her eyes. For an instant, a cruel, ruthless look shone in her eyes. Yes, she was prepared to get rid of him to remove a potential threat.
Oblivious to her thoughts, Nux just smiled. He seemed quite amused by the woman. He wanted to see how she would react and…
He was also expecting to see ‘him.’
“You did not answer my question.”
Sharnoth spoke up.
[You did not answer my question either.]
Nux shot back.
“I will be the one asking questions here.”
[You must really trust my words, don’t you?]
Nux chuckled.
[To think you would try to act bossy when your entire life can turn around if I just decide to do what I said I wouldn’t. I assumed you were the more careful type.]
“Is that a threat?”
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes.
“No, it was just a simple observation.”
Nux shook his head, dropping the topic.
[Anyways, you asked why I was here, didn’t you?
As I said through my messages before, I could be your potential ally. I am here today to turn this possibility into a reality.]
“A possible ally, huh?”
Sharnoth repeated those words.
[That is correct.]
Nux nodded confidently.
[You have already seen what I am capable of, and I do not wish to sound arrogant when I say this, but I highly doubt my alliance is an offer you would want to refuse.]
“What are your terms?”
Sharnoth questioned again.
Nux liked how she didn’t play games with every single exchange. Direct confrontation and communication was indeed the way to go.
Right now, however, Nux didn’t say anything out loud.
Rather, he stared at the woman in front of him and,
[I don’t think I should be saying it. He is still here, isn’t he?]
Sharnoth stayed silent, not denying his words.
[This is the time where you activate your Domain and kick him out so we can talk without an eternal influence.]
Nux urged.
“I do not understand. Why are you so hell-bent on keeping him away?”
Sharnoth tried to change the topic—something Nux didn’t mind.
He just played along,
[Do you not know? I am his son.
And we don’t get along.]
“His son…?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow. She turned in a random direction, as if staring at a certain being that even Nux couldn’t sense.
He, however, knew who it was.
It seemed like for some reason, only Sharnoth was able to see Zylarith.
Nux knew about this.
In his investigation before, he had found the Queen’s strange habit of talking randomly, almost as if she was accompanied by someone.
[Oh? He didn’t tell you?]
Nux questioned with a playful grin on his face.
[And here I thought he was excited to see his son after such a long time.
You disappoint me again, Father.]
Nux sighed dramatically.
Sharnoth, on the other hand, continued to stare at Zylarith and waited for him to explain.
“Do not let him manipulate you, Shar.”
Zylarith spoke up, trying to defend himself. Just like how Nux couldn’t see him, he couldn’t seem to hear him either.
Zylarith truly had turned into a ghost.
A ghost only Sharnoth could interact with.
Despite his words, however, Sharnoth continued to stare at him, waiting for an answer. Zylarith, who saw that, just sighed and gave in,
“He is my son, yes. I have been trying to recruit him, but he doesn’t listen.”
“Recruit him?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
This…
She didn’t know about this.
When did this happen?
Zylarith had been with her almost all her life. How did he even find this man when this was the first time she had seen him?
There were too many questions in her head.
The biggest one, however, was…
“Why does he sound like you are his worst enemy when all you are trying to do is recruit him on your side?
That just sounds childish.”
The woman spoke up, and yes, she was clearly aware of the fact that Nux could hear her loud and clear.
And Nux obviously did not take it lying down,
[He tried to kill my wives.]
He defended himself.
“What…?”
Sharnoth frowned.
[Exactly.]
Nux nodded.
[That is how foolish of a man he is.
He is foolish enough to believe that harming my wives will make me side with him.
I sometimes wonder how a Supreme World survived under his leadership—it almost makes me want to underestimate the other Four Supreme Worlds.]
Nux snorted.
He couldn’t see Zylarith, but knowing that his dear father could hear him was all he needed to continue the shit talk. He even wanted to have Sharnoth on his side, confronting the old soul, but then…
“So the reason you are so against him… is because he tried hurting your wives?”
[He tried to kill them.]
Nux corrected.
“But he failed, did he not?”
[That doesn’t change anything.]
Nux’s answer was instantaneous. He didn’t like how the woman was trying to downplay this.
“It does change everything.”
Sharnoth countered.
“Nothing happened, no one’s dead, it was a failed attempt. If you want, he would even apologize to you. Let bygones be bygones and start acting like an adult.
You currently seem like a stubborn child who is throwing tantrums just because he can.”
[So I should… forgive the man who tried to kill my wives?]
Nux raised his eyebrow. Sharnoth, however, nodded firmly.
“That is correct. The Universe is complicated. You cannot always get what you want. There are times when you need to back down.
There are people in this Universe who are far stronger than us. Your father is an extremely resourceful man. You need him by your side for a better future, and he needs you to carry his legacy.
Join him, and the power to have the Universe in your palms will be right on top of your hands.”
The Queen raised her voice, wanting to handle things as peacefully as possible since she wanted both of them on her side,
But then,
[Heh.]
Nux laughed.
[Who said I needed a half-dead soul to become strong? He cannot even maintain his existence without fearing the Universe’s retaliation. What could he possibly do to help me?]
Nux’s purple eyes then stared into Sharnoth’s and,
[And you, Sharnoth Nocthys,
You disappoint me.
It seems that your people’s potential for you was wrong. You weren’t as interested as they made you out to be.
You are simply a monkey who has been climbing the tree placed right in front of her, not even stopping to look around and see far taller, much higher trees.]
Soon, however, Nux’s disappointed eyes turned cold as suddenly,
[This is it.
I tried communicating peacefully but you refused to follow my terms.
Since you wish to side with my enemy,
You are now my enemy as well.
Sharnoth Nocthys,
I, Nux Leander, from the Leander Family, declare War on you and your entire Faction.]

chapters.title: Chapter 2032: The Devil was at work.
paragraphs: [Since you wish to side with my enemy,
You are now my enemy as well.
Sharnoth Nocthys,
I, Nux Leander, from the Leander Family, declare war on you and your entire faction.]
Nux spoke with a solemn look on his face. At his words, however, Sharnoth just laughed arrogantly.
"You make it sound like I was the one who approached you."
[Oh, you will.]
Nux grinned, his purple eyes stared right into Sharnoth's.
"Those are some bold words."
[You have no idea what you are up against.
And do you know what's even worse?
You are doing it for a person who would discard you the moment you are no longer useful.]
"Then I just need to make sure I will always be useful, no?"
Sharnoth chuckled, and her casual attitude was reflected by Nux almost perfectly.
[Indeed, try your best and stay useful.]
Nux then looked away, staring at a completely random place right beside Sharnoth's face and,
[And Father.]
He called out.

[You did well. I didn't think you would find such a loyal bitch who would follow your orders to her end. To burn away everything she did her entire life because of her loyalty to a person who would cast her out in minutes—
I do not know whether she is just outright foolish or… well, there is no other option,
She is foolish.]
Nux spoke, looking at Sharnoth again.
[And here I thought she wanted to avenge her dead father.]
He laughed.
And this time, Sharnoth finally reacted,
"The only fool here is you, Nux Leander."
She started.

"You came here for an alliance, despite knowing that I am together with your father. You, who does not even dare to meet me face to face, expect me to abandon the being who has helped me my entire life and choose you.
What makes you think any sane being would do that?
Or did you just naively believe everything would go your way?
Who is the foolish one here?"
The Queen questioned.
'She got you there.'
Aisha, who was hearing those words, chuckled inwardly.
'Indeed.'
Eisheth nodded as well.
'I did say it wasn't a good plan.'
Edda was having fun as well.
This was the first time Nux was losing in a battle of words, even if it was intentional.
Outside, Nux just stared at the woman in front of him and shrugged,
[I hope you do not regret your choice, Sharnoth Nocthys.]
"I will not, trust me."
Sharnoth smiled.
However, the moment the connection broke down, Sharnoth noticed something.
Shakel, one of her most trusted subordinates, had disappeared.
It wasn't just him. Three more Transcendents had disappeared, and it wasn't stopping. A foreign energy was teleporting them away.
The Queen narrowed her eyes, then, with a wave of her hand, she took over her World's Will and suddenly, all Transcendent-level beings in her world were forcefully teleported next to her.
BOOOOOOOOM
Her Aura then burst out, and in an instant, her domain expanded.
The reality changed. With a mere thought, the space around her domain was sealed, making it impossible for any being to break through her space barriers.
"Heh."
Nux, who saw what happened, laughed out loud.
The instant the woman activated her domain, she also made sure no outer being could peek inside her domain, making it impossible for him to know what was happening inside.
He did, however, witness everything that happened before this.
That woman…

She was different from Dainar and the other Progenitors of High-Level Worlds he had met. Unlike them, who constantly fought to take control over their worlds, she had complete control over her World's Will.
So much that she could even pick any being from her world using her world's influence and bring him or her next to her, just like she did right now.
If Tenebris's Progenitor were anything like her, it would have been impossible for him to extract the information he wanted from them.
Yes, Sharnoth was in a completely different league compared to those four, and this is when Tenebris's energy as a world was stronger than Khaemorr.
"No wonder they do not wish to face her head-on, she is a monster."
Nux commented out loud.
He was impressed.
Honestly, even though he had seen Sharnoth a few times in the memories of the beings he had devoured, he didn't know much about her other than her story that was told to everyone.

To every being he devoured, Sharnoth was a godly entity who couldn't be questioned, an entity that would do what she says—a fearsome entity that even the strongest beings in the Universe feared and respected.
Yes, she had that level of control over her people. Some even believed she was on the same level as the beings from Supreme Worlds—an absurd statement, but they still believed it nonetheless.
"Nux!"
Suddenly, Nux heard a shout.
He glanced at his wives and saw Vyriana waving her arm at him,
"What are you doing!? Bring others! It is my turn now!"
Behind her stood Amaya, Aeliana, and Astaria with satisfied looks on their faces. They had all captured the Transcendents Nux had abducted just now, and it was Vyriana's turn now.
Yes, the women had turned this into a game.
A game where Nux plucked out a Transcendent-level fish from the sea beneath them, and they caught them.
And right now, it was Vyriana's turn.
Just that…
"She gathered all the Transcendents around her and sealed the space inside her domain. I cannot abduct any more Transcendents."
Nux spoke as he appeared next to Vyriana.
"Huh…?"
Vyriana frowned.
"She reacted that fast?"
"She did."
"That is… quite impressive."
Aeliana seemed impressed as well.
After all, they had seen how Nux played the Eternals before—it had honestly ruined the image of an Eternal in their minds—but to think an Eternal would show such quick resistance.
"She is strong, yes.
I haven't faced her yet, but I doubt she is any weaker than the Umbrasol Progenitors."
"Umbrasol Progenitors…?"
Amaya blinked, unable to believe those words.

Khaemorr was a comparatively weaker High-Level World; it could only hold one Eternal-level being. Compared to Umbrasol, which was one of the strongest High-Level Worlds to have ever existed, Khaemorr was nothing.
The difference in the strength of their leaders should be absurd, but…
"Is she really as strong as the Umbrasol Progenitors?"
Aeliana seemed surprised as well.
"She may even be stronger, I do not know. I haven't seen her fight."
"A Progenitor of one of the Supreme Worlds chose her; she won't be weak."
Vyriana reasoned.
Nux nodded at those words.
Their new enemy definitely wasn't weak.
"So what do we do now?"
Felberta, who appeared together with the rest of the wives to join the discussion, questioned out loud.
"Wait, does her domain cover her entire world?"
Amaya questioned.
"No."
Nux shook his head.
"It only covers a very small area—the area where all the Transcendents are now gathered."
"Then what about the rest of the world?"
"I can still influence it."
Nux nodded with an evil grin on his face. He obviously knew what his wife wanted him to do.
"Let's capture the Primordials then."
Amaya spoke up. Nux's grin widened, and he nodded at those words.
The plan was simple—Nux was going to use every single advantage he had to corner Sharnoth.
He would slowly destroy everything she had built so painstakingly. He would ruin the reputation she held in her subordinates' minds.
Instead of an almighty goddess who could do whatever she wanted, Nux was going to turn her into a helpless being who was easy to bully.
He was going to ruin her lifelong work and remind her people of the day she lost her title as the Princess and was captured instead.
Yes, the Devil was at work.
And he was planning to show his worst side to the world.
The best way to do it?
Attack her people.
How long could a leader who cannot even protect her own people maintain her image?
It was a question that even a child knew the answer to.
With that in mind, Nux's space energy entered the boundaries of Khaemorr, and just as he did with the Transcendents, he started picking off one Primordial after another.
Why not pick a larger batch at the same time?
Well, he wasn't here to annihilate all her subordinates. That wouldn't do anything. He simply needed to spread fear.
He wanted Sharnoth to know what he was doing, and he wanted her to realize how helpless she was.
This was how the Devil played the King.
Sharnoth, who now sensed a Primordial gone missing, realized what Nux was trying. Slowly, she turned towards Zylarith, and the being just sighed,
"You cannot hide this forever."
"What if he goes to the Supreme Worlds?"
"Did you not hear what he said? He won't say anything.
He is prideful—let that be his downfall."
With those words, Zylarith slowly disappeared.
Sharnoth, on the other hand, waved her hand, and suddenly—
An endless amount of sinister, chaotic energy was released from her body.
It was the Power of Chaos.

"You make it sound like I was the one who approached you."
[Oh, you will.]
Nux grinned, his purple eyes stared right into Sharnoth's.
"Those are some bold words."
[You have no idea what you are up against.
And do you know what's even worse?
You are doing it for a person who would discard you the moment you are no longer useful.]
"Then I just need to make sure I will always be useful, no?"
Sharnoth chuckled, and her casual attitude was reflected by Nux almost perfectly.
[Indeed, try your best and stay useful.]
Nux then looked away, staring at a completely random place right beside Sharnoth's face and,
[And Father.]
He called out.
[You did well.
I didn't think you would find such a loyal bitch who would follow your orders to her end.
To burn away everything she did her entire life because of her loyalty to a person who would cast her out in minutes—
I do not know whether she is just outright foolish or… well, there is no other option,
She is foolish.]
Nux spoke, looking at Sharnoth again.
[And here I thought she wanted to avenge her dead father.]
He laughed.
And this time, Sharnoth finally reacted,
"The only fool here is you, Nux Leander."
She started.
"You came here for an alliance, despite knowing that I am together with your father.
You, who does not even dare to meet me face to face, expect me to abandon the being who has helped me my entire life and choose you.
What makes you think any sane being would do that?
Or did you just naively believe everything would go your way?
Who is the foolish one here?"
The Queen questioned.
'She got you there.'
Aisha, who was hearing those words, chuckled inwardly.
'Indeed.'
Eisheth nodded as well.
'I did say it wasn't a good plan.'
Edda was having fun as well.
This was the first time Nux was losing in a battle of words, even if it was intentional.
Outside, Nux just stared at the woman in front of him and shrugged,
[I hope you do not regret your choice, Sharnoth Nocthys.]
"I will not, trust me."
Sharnoth smiled.
However, the moment the connection broke down, Sharnoth noticed something.
Shakel, one of her most trusted subordinates, had disappeared.
It wasn't just him.
Three more Transcendents had disappeared, and it wasn't stopping.
A foreign energy was teleporting them away.
The Queen narrowed her eyes, then, with a wave of her hand, she took over her World's Will and suddenly, all Transcendent-level beings in her world were forcefully teleported next to her.
BOOOOOOOOM
Her Aura then burst out, and in an instant, her domain expanded.
The reality changed.
With a mere thought, the space around her domain was sealed, making it impossible for any being to break through her space barriers.
"Heh."
Nux, who saw what happened, laughed out loud.
The instant the woman activated her domain, she also made sure no outer being could peek inside her domain, making it impossible for him to know what was happening inside.
He did, however, witness everything that happened before this.
That woman…
She was different from Dainar and the other Progenitors of High-Level Worlds he had met.
Unlike them, who constantly fought to take control over their worlds, she had complete control over her World's Will.
So much that she could even pick any being from her world using her world's influence and bring him or her next to her, just like she did right now.
If Tenebris's Progenitor were anything like her, it would have been impossible for him to extract the information he wanted from them.
Yes, Sharnoth was in a completely different league compared to those four, and this is when Tenebris's energy as a world was stronger than Khaemorr.
"No wonder they do not wish to face her head-on, she is a monster."
Nux commented out loud.
He was impressed.
Honestly, even though he had seen Sharnoth a few times in the memories of the beings he had devoured, he didn't know much about her other than her story that was told to everyone.

To every being he devoured, Sharnoth was a godly entity who couldn't be questioned, an entity that would do what she says—a fearsome entity that even the strongest beings in the Universe feared and respected.
Yes, she had that level of control over her people.
Some even believed she was on the same level as the beings from Supreme Worlds—an absurd statement, but they still believed it nonetheless.
"Nux!"
Suddenly, Nux heard a shout.
He glanced at his wives and saw Vyriana waving her arm at him,
"What are you doing!?
Bring others!
It is my turn now!"
Behind her stood Amaya, Aeliana, and Astaria with satisfied looks on their faces.
They had all captured the Transcendents Nux had abducted just now, and it was Vyriana's turn now.
Yes, the women had turned this into a game.
A game where Nux plucked out a Transcendent-level fish from the sea beneath them, and they caught them.
And right now, it was Vyriana's turn.
Just that…
"She gathered all the Transcendents around her and sealed the space inside her domain.
I cannot abduct any more Transcendents."
Nux spoke as he appeared next to Vyriana.
"Huh…?"
Vyriana frowned.
"She reacted that fast?"
"She did."
"That is… quite impressive."
Aeliana seemed impressed as well.
After all, they had seen how Nux played the Eternals before—it had honestly ruined the image of an Eternal in their minds—but to think an Eternal would show such quick resistance.
"She is strong, yes.
I haven't faced her yet, but I doubt she is any weaker than the Umbrasol Progenitors."
"Umbrasol Progenitors…?"
Amaya blinked, unable to believe those words.
Khaemorr was a comparatively weaker High-Level World; it could only hold one Eternal-level being.
Compared to Umbrasol, which was one of the strongest High-Level Worlds to have ever existed, Khaemorr was nothing.
The difference in the strength of their leaders should be absurd, but…
"Is she really as strong as the Umbrasol Progenitors?"
Aeliana seemed surprised as well.
"She may even be stronger, I do not know.
I haven't seen her fight."
"A Progenitor of one of the Supreme Worlds chose her; she won't be weak."
Vyriana reasoned.
Nux nodded at those words.
Their new enemy definitely wasn't weak.
"So what do we do now?"
Felberta, who appeared together with the rest of the wives to join the discussion, questioned out loud.
"Wait, does her domain cover her entire world?"
Amaya questioned.
"No."
Nux shook his head.
"It only covers a very small area—the area where all the Transcendents are now gathered."
"Then what about the rest of the world?"
"I can still influence it."
Nux nodded with an evil grin on his face.
He obviously knew what his wife wanted him to do.
"Let's capture the Primordials then."
Amaya spoke up.
Nux's grin widened, and he nodded at those words.
The plan was simple—Nux was going to use every single advantage he had to corner Sharnoth.
He would slowly destroy everything she had built so painstakingly.
He would ruin the reputation she held in her subordinates' minds.
Instead of an almighty goddess who could do whatever she wanted, Nux was going to turn her into a helpless being who was easy to bully.
He was going to ruin her lifelong work and remind her people of the day she lost her title as the Princess and was captured instead.
Yes, the Devil was at work.
And he was planning to show his worst side to the world.
The best way to do it?
Attack her people.
How long could a leader who cannot even protect her own people maintain her image?
It was a question that even a child knew the answer to.
With that in mind, Nux's space energy entered the boundaries of Khaemorr, and just as he did with the Transcendents, he started picking off one Primordial after another.
Why not pick a larger batch at the same time?
Well, he wasn't here to annihilate all her subordinates.
That wouldn't do anything.
He simply needed to spread fear.
He wanted Sharnoth to know what he was doing, and he wanted her to realize how helpless she was.
This was how the Devil played the King.
Sharnoth, who now sensed a Primordial gone missing, realized what Nux was trying.
Slowly, she turned towards Zylarith, and the being just sighed,
"You cannot hide this forever."
"What if he goes to the Supreme Worlds?"
"Did you not hear what he said?
He won't say anything.
He is prideful—let that be his downfall."
With those words, Zylarith slowly disappeared.
Sharnoth, on the other hand, waved her hand, and suddenly—
An endless amount of sinister, chaotic energy was released from her body.
It was the Power of Chaos.

chapters.title: Chapter 2033: This… is going to be fun.
paragraphs: "Hmm?"
While Nux was slowly abducting one Primordial after the other, a frown appeared on his face, something that Felberta noticed in an instant.
"What is it?"
The Eldraeth questioned.
"The Space Laws in her world… they are being… altered…?"
Nux muttered. He himself sounded confused, unable to believe what he was sensing.
"She has the Power over Space?"
Felberta frowned.
"None of the memories I inherited indicate that."
Nux shook his head. He appeared next to Sharnoth's subordinates he had abducted. Strange markings appeared on his body as, suddenly, he started reading their memories.
It took him a minute to read and absorb all the knowledge, and once he was done, his frown deepened even further.
"I do not understand. She shouldn't have Power over Space. I saw her use an Artifact to teleport."
"Is she perhaps hiding her strength?"
"She is, yes.
None of these people have seen her go all out. Since she took down her enemies effortlessly almost all the time, even when she faced other Eternals, she never went all out.
But whatever her Power is, it is not related to Space. Whatever powers she showed had almost no relation to Space.
Also…"
Nux suddenly closed his eyes as he focused on his senses, trying to abduct another Primordial.
Locking the target wasn't difficult. However, the moment he used the Power over Space to bring that being here, his powers flickered and…
Flicker
A plant appeared in front of Nux.
"What the…"
Felberta frowned.
"Is she messing with the Space Laws?"
She questioned. She had seen Nux do something like this, but this was the first time it was happening to him.
Nux, however, shook his head as he finally realized what was going on.
"She is not affecting the Space Laws. She is affecting the very Space around her world with her energy."
"An energy that is affecting even the Space?"
Felberta blinked. There weren't many energies strong enough to affect Space.
"It's Chaos."
Nux answered.
"Chaos…?"
"I have sensed this energy before."
Nux nodded.
It was one of the energies that had always remained constant in the lifespan of hundreds of worlds that he had devoured,
An ever-growing energy,
The Primordial Energy of Chaos.
"But how does someone not from Chaosveil have Power over Chaos?"
Felberta frowned.
She knew that Zylarith was with Sharnoth, but it was common knowledge that Supreme Worlds never allowed any being to comprehend the concept related to their energies.
Every time a being comprehends such a Law, he is either recruited or killed depending on his potential and circumstances.
There has never been a case of another being using energies related to the Supreme Worlds in the history of the Universe.
So the fact that Sharnoth had the Power over Chaos…
It meant…
"My dear Father has chosen an heir."
Nux grinned.
"No wonder she didn't betray him."
Amaya commented.
"I didn't think he would go this far."
Aeliana nodded as well.
"Had he already chosen her as his successor when he came to us?"
Vyriana questioned, curious.
"He had."
Nux nodded.
"Sharnoth should be around 70,000 years old now. If she met him when she was a child, it meant that they have been together for all these years."
"Then why come to you?"
Vyriana couldn't understand.
"I had inherited their greatest invention."
Nux shrugged.
"So he was here to take the System from you?"
"That might not be the case."
Suddenly, Allura spoke up, shaking her head.
The rest of the women turned towards her and frowned. The succubus ignored them all and continued with a playful smile on her face.
"There is a chance that he prepared her as a gift for Nux."
Amaya narrowed her eyes, not liking that possibility one bit.
However, the more she thought about it…
"It is possible."
Aeliana admitted.
"But since Nux refused, he turned towards her instead."
"Or maybe she was always the backup he had been relying on. He said he had been waiting for billions of years, didn't he?
There is no way a Progenitor of a Supreme World would store all his eggs in one basket. I doubt he didn't try something else for these past billion years."
Rune spoke up.
The rest of the people turned towards the cat, and none could refute her theory.
"So she is Nux's replacement?"
Edda questioned with a big grin on her face. No one knew what was going on in that mind of hers.
"She is indeed."
Aisha nodded. She had the same grin as Edda.
The rest of the confused women just shook their heads.
"My Nux has no replacement."
Thyra snorted as she turned into a cat and jumped on Nux's shoulders. Nux smiled as he started caressing her body as affectionately as he could.
"So my father had a plan B, eh?"
He grinned.
"Aren't you the Plan B here?"
Skyla questioned innocently.
"No, she is the backup here, not me."
Nux didn't give in.
"You declared war on your replacement.
That's an interesting way to put it."
Eisheth chuckled.
Nux laughed as well.
"So? What are we going to do now?"
Amaya questioned, wanting to focus on what's more important.
"The Space in Khaemorr is too chaotic. I cannot control it anymore. I cannot even peek into that world anymore. The Chaos is limiting my senses."
Nux explained.
"The Power of Corruption is quite strong…"
Melia commented, a little taken aback.
"It is."
Nux nodded.
"What now?"
Ember questioned, repeating Amaya's question.
"Well, I did declare War."
Nux commented with a wide grin on his face.
"It is time the Universe finds out about the Leander Family."
He declared as, suddenly, 38 Transcendents appeared in front of him. With a wave of his hand, the Power of Genesis was activated, forming 38 papers.
"This is the information of 100 Lowest and Lower Level Worlds that are in Khaemorr's faction.
Destroy them all.
Keep in mind, you are not to kill the world's denizens, only kill the Leaders, and once you are done, find the largest ground there and draw this."
Nux ordered as he showed a Sigil.
A Sigil that instantly attracted the women's attention.

It had an otherworldly design. At the center, there was a glowing black hole, surrounded by swirling red and golden rings, representing Nux's Universe that seemed like it was prepared to devour more worlds.
The background was deep black, with hints of silver and violet, giving it a dangerous yet royal feel. In the middle, bold and glowing words said "Leander Family," written in a strong, noble style.
*Picture*
"Nux, what is this?"
Evane questioned, her eyes shining with excitement.
"Our painting lessons didn't go to waste, did they?"
Nux chuckled.
"You still need more work."
Evane answered with a big smile on her face.
"Then I'll be under your care."
"Yes."
Evane nodded with a bright smile on her face.
"Is this our Family Sigil?"
Melia questioned, her eyes shining with keen interest.
"No."
Nux shook his head.
"Our Sigil will have each and every one of you.
This is just something temporary."
Nux still wasn't strong enough, and he didn't wish to give his enemies any clues at all. The only reason he was even using the symbol was because he needed a banner.
A banner he could use to represent himself, add a layer of mystery around himself and… destroy his enemy through and through.
"You all can leave now."
Nux commanded as he glanced at the Transcendents.
"As you command, Lord Nux."
The Transcendents nodded and disappeared. Every single one of them had artifacts they could use to travel in space.
And while Nux could still teleport them, he decided not to.
For Transcendent Level Beings, Lowest and Lower Level Worlds were nothing. All they needed to do was appear, suppress their leaders, and be done with it. It was never supposed to be a challenge.

Honestly, if Nux wanted, he could even pass the order to destroy 1000 more worlds. After all, he had absorbed the memories of Shakel, one of Sharnoth's most loyal subordinates. He knew almost everything there was to know about the War.
If Nux wanted, none of those Lowest and Low-Level Worlds would be left. However, that would not help him achieve his purpose.
After all, his goal here wasn't destruction,
It was Isolation.
As he thought about it, a wide grin appeared on Nux's face as he tightened his hug around Thyra's cat body and started showering her with kisses.
In an instant, Rune turned into her cat form and jumped on top of him as well. She obviously wouldn't let Thyra take all the advantage alone.
The two cats fought for Nux's attention, and the moment they saw that, the rest of the women jumped in as well, not allowing the cats to get any advantage.
Nux, who saw this, chuckled and decided to return to his own Universe, where Time flew differently than the main Universe.
His moment together with his wives stretched for a long time.
'Lord Nux, I have done what you have asked of me.'
As Nux was surrounded by his wives, one of the Transcendents informed.
'Good.'
He nodded.
'Lord Nux…'
Soon, more and more of the Transcendents informed him of their success, and Nux's smile widened.
This… is going to be fun.

chapters.title: Chapter 2034: This cannot continue.
paragraphs: Chapter 2034: This cannot continue.
“Lady Sharnoth.”
In a huge meeting hall, where Sharnoth and her subordinates were holding a meeting, discussing everything that had happened this past week, a being named Varys barged in.
Varys was an Elar’zhun.

One of the most beautiful races in the Universe. Elar’zhuns have pale, marble-like skin that glowed faintly. Most of them have silver, violet, or golden eyes that are hypnotically beautiful. Varys himself had beautiful silver eyes.

Their hair resembled flowing starlight or crystal thread. They were almost 2 meters tall, their movements were graceful, and their bodies were unnervingly perfect. Even their voices were extremely melodic and oddly persuasive.
Yes, it was a race that was pretty much the embodiment of beauty and perfection. Beings that would make you submit, willingly.
Beings that seemed… incarnations of holiness.
And this is what made the Elar’zhun so dangerous.
Their features made them appear holy, pure beings that could not be corrupted, but in truth, these beings were some of the vilest in the entire Universe.
Their perfection was stolen.
Their beauty, their appearance, their skills, even their memories—they were all stolen.
These beings were called the Essence Takers.
They had the power to absorb other entities—their traits, their talent, or even their knowledge—they could absorb it all.
These beings chased perfection, and the pathway to perfection, according to their belief, could only be achieved once they absorbed every single being in the Universe.
Yes, these supposedly beautiful beings aimed to kill every other being except themselves in order to achieve perfection.
These beings were so vile that more than a few worlds had joined forces, combined their might, killed their leaders, and destroyed their worlds.
Hundreds of thousands of years later, only a few of them remained, all now serving under Sharnoth, who had recruited them.
And of course, Varys was no exception either. His appearance was nigh perfect, and his mind was cruel.
*Picture*

The moment Varys barged in, everyone in the meeting room, including Sharnoth, turned towards him. In a normal situation, Varys’s actions would have resulted in frowns and disgruntled, dissatisfied voices.
This was not the etiquette for entering the Meeting Hall.
No one was to just… barge into the Meeting Hall without any permission. It was disrespectful and arrogant—an act that might even result in execution.
However, Varys wasn’t just any random subordinate. The position he held and the matter he was supposed to handle were grave.
As he barged in, not a single being inside thought about etiquette.
Rather, they all prepared themselves for more bad news.
And Varys didn’t surprise them.
“Ten more fell.”
He spoke in a grave tone.
The entire meeting room fell silent. The council members had grave looks on their faces, even Sharnoth herself was no exception.
Varys stared at everyone and started giving the details,
“Like yesterday, there were six Lowest Level Worlds and four Low Level Worlds.
Their Leaders were assassinated three hours ago. The Worlds’ Wills altered the denizens of those worlds and only then did they find the bodies and…”
Varys hesitated for a moment before continuing,
“And the Leander Family Sigil near their dead bodies.”
Sharnoth’s face turned even grimmer when she heard those words.
Again.
This was the eighth day.
“Coward!”
Another one of the Council Members, Siara, shouted as she slammed the table.
Like Varys, she was an Elar’zhun as well. She had long crystal-like hair and golden eyes. Right now, however, her perfect face was contorted, and she had an ugly, frustrated expression on her face.
*Picture*
And she couldn’t be blamed for this either.
There was a certain way in which things in the Universe played out, and this was especially true for War.
Every time two Worlds, or two forces, fought, they went at each other. It is usually frowned upon to target the enemies’ weaker allies.
The usual flow chart of War in the Universe was simple:
When two Worlds are at War, and each of them are leaders of their respective Factions, they bring their entire Factions into the said War.
The other, weaker Worlds that are part of the Factions wage Wars against each other. The War starts with the Lowest Level Worlds and rises from there.

As the Battles intensify, Worlds from one Faction usually overpower the others. The losing worlds are destroyed or surrender and are kicked out of their Faction. The winning worlds wage War against another world or send their armies to their Faction.
This continues until one Faction is significantly weaker than the other, and the losing Faction gives in.
However, throughout this exchange, no Higher Level World or Higher Level Being is supposed to interfere in the battles between Lower Level Worlds.
A High Level World cannot just send forces to destroy enemy Low Level Worlds.
And yet…
That coward was constantly targeting Lowest and Low Level Worlds of their Faction!
In these past eight days, he had destroyed 80 such Worlds. Even though he is not going around completely wiping out those worlds, he kills all the leaders, leaving the worlds at their weakest point.
The enemy worlds that those worlds were at War with take advantage of the situation and eradicate them. It is no different from destroying those worlds, even if he is not doing it on his own.
It was cowardly.
It was shameful.
“Something needs to be done about him.
This cannot continue.”
Another being, Maeve, spoke up.
Her appearance was similar to Siara’s, however, she was not an Elar’zhun—she was different.
She was a Nocthari.

Like Elar’zhun, Nocthari was another one of the strongest races, that were once dominant but were destroyed by others because they were becoming too strong—only for Sharnoth to later find and rule over what was left of them.

Similar to the Elar’zhun, Nocthari were quite beautiful beings. They had pale, moonlight-like skin, their eyes shifted colors depending on nearby emotions. Their hair flowed like dark smoke and they were tall, lean, and graceful.

When they were at their strongest, Nocthari were known as Emotionless Architects of Domination. They saw emotion as a weakness and logic as supremacy. They did not kill out of anger—they eliminated inefficiencies with cold, calculated precision.

These beings did not feel empathy, fear, love, or guilt, and they believed that the universe must be perfected. They even went around conquering worlds to optimize life forms and erase anything illogical—even if it meant erasing entire species.
Like her people, Maeve was almost a cold beauty who could not feel emotions. She wasn’t particularly frustrated or angered by Nux’s actions; however, she could see that he needed to be stopped.
To have 80 worlds under their Faction destroyed within 8 days—it was shameful.
And while Maeve didn’t feel any shame or grief about the lost lives, she could see how this would affect their reputation.𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚
Right now, the matter was still small, since only weaker worlds were affected. However, if this continued, other worlds in their Faction would start to notice, and this would cause problems.
“And how are we supposed to stop him?”
Siara glanced at Maeve and questioned.
Maeve’s eyes turned red, reflecting Siara’s anger, and the Nocthari simply turned towards Sharnoth, ignoring Siara because she didn’t want a pointless quarrel, and continued,
“Lady Sharnoth needs to do something.
Anything.
This cannot continue.”
Maeve repeated herself and Sharnoth…
The Queen clenched her fists in frustration.
*Maeve’s Picture*
Hello everyone,

I sincerely apologize for the unexpected break in uploads over the past few days. I originally anticipated a short drop in upload rate (1 chap a day) due to my exams—for two or three days at most. However, things quickly escalated beyond anything I could have imagined.

My country began preparations for war, and living in a border state meant I was directly affected. Blackouts became frequent, and the sounds of bombardments were constant and terrifying. Writing was the last thing on my mind as I had to keep moving from place to place, trying to stay safe amidst the chaos. My parents were also away from me, living in an even dangerous area.

Thankfully, a ceasefire has now been declared. The shooting has stopped, and although blackouts are still ongoing, there is at least silence—and safety. I’m with my parents, and knowing they are safe brings me some peace.
I’m slowly getting back into the writing mindset. There will be only one chapter today, but if things continue to remain stable, I hope to return to the usual two chapters a day starting tomorrow.
Thank you so much for your patience and understanding during this difficult time. Your support means the world to me.
