chapters.title: Chapter 2035: This time, the ghosts wouldn’t escape.
paragraphs: Chapter 2035: This time, the ghosts wouldn’t escape.
“Lady Sharnoth needs to do something.
Anything.
This cannot continue.”
Maeve spoke with the same emotionless tone and Sharnoth…
She could only clench her fist in frustration.
“She is correct. This needs to stop.”
Varys nodded.

“The matter still isn’t big, but it is rising at a surprising rate. The worlds he has targeted all belong to our faction. It won’t take long for other worlds in our faction to realize what is happening, and if every single world connected to us starts falling without us being able to do anything,
our faction will fall apart.”
The Elar’zhun spoke with a grim look on his face.
“Why not go to the Supreme Worlds?”
Suddenly, Siara spoke up.𝘧𝓇ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝘣𝓃ℴ𝓋𝑒𝑙.𝑐𝘰𝑚
The rest of the Council Members turned towards her and frowned.
Most of these beings came from destroyed worlds that were once part of a Supreme World Faction. However, when their worlds were destroyed, the Supreme Worlds did not do anything to help them.
None of the people here saw the Supreme Worlds in a positive light. The very thought of seeking their help repulsed them. Siara was no exception to this,
but…
“The four of them oversee the entire Universe. Their rules, especially regarding warfare, are extremely clear.
What that coward is doing goes against the rules they value so much. If we can use them, then…
why not?”
Siara suggested, and suddenly,
“That is a plausible solution.”
Maeve nodded.

As a Nocthari, she did not feel any emotions. She was one of the only few beings in the Council who held no prejudice against the Supreme Worlds. If she could use them to get what she wanted, she did not see anything wrong with this plan.
“If we report his actions to the Supreme Worlds, they will take action.
His ability to avoid the World’s Will’s detection will also interest them.”
When the most logical being in the Council suggested it, the rest of the Council members started thinking about it as well.
It wasn’t a matter they could solve on their own; they had already tried.

The biggest problem was that the Leander Family had no home. They were wandering mercenaries. The only information that could be found about them was in the Mercenaries Hall, and even there, they were regarded as legends with more rumors than actual information regarding them.
They were like ghosts.
There was no way to track them down.
They entered worlds, assassinated their leaders, left the said worlds in a vulnerable state, and disappeared before anything could be done about them.
All they ever found were ashes—
—and the same taunting sigil, deliberately left behind like a middle finger to the faction.
The bastards were invisible.
How was… one supposed to fight such an enemy?
Letting the Supreme Worlds take on this headache was a much more preferable option.
But…
“No.”
Sharnoth shook her head.
She stared at her Council Members as her crimson eyes shined dangerously.
“Supreme Worlds will not be involved in our matters.”
She declared in a strict voice, settling the matter once and for all.
No Supreme Worlds.
Varys, Siara, and even Maeve all turned silent. None of them dared to stand against the Queen.
After all, all of them knew what would happen if they did. Even Maeve, who was incapable of feeling fear, stayed back.
Sharnoth then stared at Varys and,
“How many of the ten worlds still exist?”
“Two. The rest have lost the war against their enemies.”
“Send reinforcements to those two worlds.”
Sharnoth ordered.
“As you command, My Queen.”
“Send our men to all the worlds of our faction. Tell them to stay on guard at all times. I need an instant report the moment something happens, and make sure you contain the matter here.
No two worlds in the faction will share the information of there being Khaemorr delegations in their world.
Is that clear?”
“If we send our forces to all the worlds in our faction, it will weaken us considerably.”
Maeve spoke up.
She looked into Sharnoth’s eyes and,
“We are still at war, My Queen. We still have Aurendor to worry about.”
“If they dare to attack us, let them.
I would like to see the cowards acting brave for once.”
Sharnoth did not back down.
If anything, she would prefer if that happened.
She never wanted war.
She never wanted to involve an entire faction in this.
She simply wanted an opportunity—an opportunity to get rid of the enemies who destroyed her world, fair and square.
She would very much like a chance to take on all her enemies alone, without them hiding behind their World’s Will.
Seeing her eyes, Maeve backed down, and her doubts were eased.
She knew just how strong her Queen was. This was the entire reason she had decided to follow her in the first place.
If the enemies did actually come for them, this might actually be good for them.
“I will make arrangements then, My Queen.”
After the Nocthari backed down, Varys bowed his head, taking the responsibility.
“That will be all.”
Sharnoth spoke as she stood up from her throne.

The moment she did, the rest of the Council Members followed her and stood up as well. The Queen walked out of the meeting room, and only once she was gone did the rest of the Council Members dare to breathe.
They stared at each other, somewhat taken aback.
Honestly, while most people knew how all this could have a big effect on their faction, none of them were actually worried.
After all, the enemy wasn’t directly targeting them—they were only targeting Lowest or Low-Level Worlds. They were safe.
Even Varys wasn’t particularly worried. But even then, since his Queen had passed the order, he was going to follow.
He left the meeting hall and went to his subordinates to pass the Queen’s orders.

Khaemorr reacted according to Sharnoth’s instruction, and very quickly, their men were dispatched to different worlds with different artifacts. Artifacts that would summon the strongest Khaemorr Warriors the instant they were activated.
It was time to take down the Leander Family.
This time, the ghosts wouldn’t escape.

chapters.title: Chapter 2036: Nux’s Weakness.
paragraphs: Chapter 2036: Nux’s Weakness.
While Varys passed his Queen’s orders and made the necessary preparations, Sharnoth, who had returned to her mansion and walked into her room, suddenly paused and,
“Your son is becoming a nuisance.”
She commented.

To any normal person, it would look like she was talking to herself since there was no one around her. However, if they stared at her closely, they would realize that Sharnoth was looking in a particular direction, as if she was talking to someone.
“My relationship with him wasn’t always the best.”
The being she was talking to replied.
“I can see that.”
Sharnoth snorted.
“I do not need your confirmation on the matter, I need a solution.”
“Do you not have a solution already?”
Zylarith questioned with a slight frown on his face.
“That won’t work.”
Sharnoth shook her head.
“It is merely a desperate attempt to calm my people.
A farce.
A show to tell them that their Queen has not abandoned them, but it will not change anything. Your son is no fool.
He captured my Transcendents in our first encounter. You think he is scared of Primordial Level subordinates I send into Lowest and Low Level Worlds?”
“…I did not think he would grow to such an annoying level when I first met him.”
Zylarith admitted.
“He was barely a Protector when he was about a thousand years old.”
“That’s slow.”
Sharnoth commented.
“Indeed.”
Zylarith nodded.
“How did he become a Transcendent then?”
Sharnoth did not understand. A thousand-year-old Protector, a being with potential like that, would never be able to break through to the Transcendent Level through normal means.
“This is why I still find it hard to believe that he is Transcendent.”
“He killed or abducted my Transcendent Level subordinates, and they weren’t weak, so he isn’t either.”
Sharnoth spoke in a solemn tone.
“This is what surprises me so much.”
“Why?”
Sharnoth questioned directly.
It didn’t matter if that child was a Protector when he was a thousand years old, he is now a Transcendent and that is all that mattered.
Zylarith was never a being who dwelled in the past; Sharnoth did not understand why he was so fixated on this matter.
And Zylarith, who realized what his ‘disciple’ was thinking, decided to reveal the truth,
“I had an encounter with him about five thousand years ago.”
“And?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
“He defeated Transcendent Level mercenaries I sent after him.”
“What…?”
“Back then, I thought he had someone helping him, but…
Now that doesn’t seem to be the case.”
“But you said he was only 6–7000 years old… so 5000 years ago, he shouldn’t be more than two thousand years old…
And if he was only a Protector when he was a thousand years old then…
How did he become a Transcendent… in the next thousand years…?”
Zylarith stayed silent, and that silence answered Sharnoth’s question.
Her crimson eyes instantly turned cold and,
“He has the Law of Absolute Growth, doesn’t he?”
She questioned directly.
Again, Zylarith stayed silent, and again, his silence answered the Queen’s question.
“So he was the one…”
She muttered; her voice was so chilly that it would send shivers down any of her subordinates’ spines if they were to hear it.
Zylarith continued his silence.
He couldn’t say anything.
Sharnoth stared at him for a while. A few seconds later, however, her frosty expression flickered and,
“Zylarith Chaosveil.”
The Queen called out.
“I do not care if he is your son.
I do not care if he betrayed you.
I do not care if you have any more use for that child,
I only understand that he stands in the way of my revenge, and I need you to help me get rid of him.”
Zylarith stared at his disciple with a complicated look on his face and then,
“I want to get rid of him as well.”
He made up his mind.
All this while, he was still trying to somehow control Nux; after all, that child was his trump card.
However, a card that he couldn’t play when he wanted was not a good card.

Nux Leander was getting out of control. There were too many things about him that he could not explain. He was becoming more and more of a variable that he could not calculate, and the rate at which he was growing stronger did not make sense.
There was no pattern around him,
It was better to get rid of him.
“Give me something.”
Sharnoth demanded.
“Anything.
Any weakness.
Tell me everything about him, the world he comes from, the people he is close to. Give me something to act on.
Something he wouldn’t be able to evade.”
“He comes from a world named Yrniel.”
“Yrniel?”
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes. Soon, she took out a Call Artifact to pass down her orders, but,
“Do not bother.”
Zylarith shook his head.
Sharnoth glanced at him with a frown, and the Chaos Progenitor revealed,
“Yrniel does not exist anymore.”
“So which world is he anchored to now?”
“I… do not know.”
Zylarith shook his head.
“According to the reports I got, he has found a way to hide his Law Flow, so his Anchors cannot be found.”
“What…?”
Sharnoth’s expression changed.
Zylarith nodded,
“Even I do not understand how he did it.”
“…So what you are saying is that… he has no weaknesses?”
Sharnoth’s expression turned grim.
“No.”
Zylarith shook his head.
“Quite the contrary, he has one.
A very fatal one.”
“What is it?”
“His love for his wives.”
Sharnoth frowned at that.
“Love…?”
It was almost as if the concept was completely foreign to her.
“His love for his wives makes him do things no sane man would ever do. He foolishly considers those women to be his everything.
Capture any one of them and he will come to you himself.
You are then free to do anything you want with them.”
Zylarith grinned menacingly, and Sharnoth narrowed her eyes,
“If he loves them so foolishly, why would he ever let them go? Won’t he keep them hidden?”
“Do you not hear yourself?
He loves them foolishly, he does not hide them.
Trust me,
Capturing them wouldn’t be difficult if you follow my plan.”
“What plan?”
Sharnoth questioned, and Zylarith’s grin widened even further.

sentences.text: Chapter 2036: Nux’s Weakness.
While Varys passed his Queen’s orders and made the necessary preparations, Sharnoth, who had returned to her mansion and walked into her room, suddenly paused and,
“Your son is becoming a nuisance.”
She commented.
To any normal person, it would look like she was talking to herself since there was no one around her.
However, if they stared at her closely, they would realize that Sharnoth was looking in a particular direction, as if she was talking to someone.
“My relationship with him wasn’t always the best.”
The being she was talking to replied.
“I can see that.”
Sharnoth snorted.
“I do not need your confirmation on the matter, I need a solution.”
“Do you not have a solution already?”
Zylarith questioned with a slight frown on his face.
“That won’t work.”
Sharnoth shook her head.
“It is merely a desperate attempt to calm my people.
A farce.
A show to tell them that their Queen has not abandoned them, but it will not change anything.
Your son is no fool.
He captured my Transcendents in our first encounter.
You think he is scared of Primordial Level subordinates I send into Lowest and Low Level Worlds?”
“…I did not think he would grow to such an annoying level when I first met him.”
Zylarith admitted.
“He was barely a Protector when he was about a thousand years old.”
“That’s slow.”
Sharnoth commented.
“Indeed.”
Zylarith nodded.
“How did he become a Transcendent then?”
Sharnoth did not understand.
A thousand-year-old Protector, a being with potential like that, would never be able to break through to the Transcendent Level through normal means.
“This is why I still find it hard to believe that he is Transcendent.”
“He killed or abducted my Transcendent Level subordinates, and they weren’t weak, so he isn’t either.”
Sharnoth spoke in a solemn tone.
“This is what surprises me so much.”
“Why?”
Sharnoth questioned directly.
It didn’t matter if that child was a Protector when he was a thousand years old, he is now a Transcendent and that is all that mattered.
Zylarith was never a being who dwelled in the past; Sharnoth did not understand why he was so fixated on this matter.
And Zylarith, who realized what his ‘disciple’ was thinking, decided to reveal the truth,
“I had an encounter with him about five thousand years ago.”
“And?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
“He defeated Transcendent Level mercenaries I sent after him.”
“What…?”
“Back then, I thought he had someone helping him, but…
Now that doesn’t seem to be the case.”
“But you said he was only 6–7000 years old… so 5000 years ago, he shouldn’t be more than two thousand years old…
And if he was only a Protector when he was a thousand years old then…
How did he become a Transcendent… in the next thousand years…?”
Zylarith stayed silent, and that silence answered Sharnoth’s question.
Her crimson eyes instantly turned cold and,
“He has the Law of Absolute Growth, doesn’t he?”
She questioned directly.
Again, Zylarith stayed silent, and again, his silence answered the Queen’s question.
“So he was the one…”
She muttered; her voice was so chilly that it would send shivers down any of her subordinates’ spines if they were to hear it.
Zylarith continued his silence.
He couldn’t say anything.
Sharnoth stared at him for a while.
A few seconds later, however, her frosty expression flickered and,
“Zylarith Chaosveil.”
The Queen called out.
“I do not care if he is your son.
I do not care if he betrayed you.
I do not care if you have any more use for that child,
I only understand that he stands in the way of my revenge, and I need you to help me get rid of him.”
Zylarith stared at his disciple with a complicated look on his face and then,
“I want to get rid of him as well.”
He made up his mind.
All this while, he was still trying to somehow control Nux; after all, that child was his trump card.
However, a card that he couldn’t play when he wanted was not a good card.
Nux Leander was getting out of control.
There were too many things about him that he could not explain.
He was becoming more and more of a variable that he could not calculate, and the rate at which he was growing stronger did not make sense.
There was no pattern around him,
It was better to get rid of him.
“Give me something.”
Sharnoth demanded.
“Anything.
Any weakness.
Tell me everything about him, the world he comes from, the people he is close to.
Give me something to act on.
Something he wouldn’t be able to evade.”
“He comes from a world named Yrniel.”
“Yrniel?”
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes.
Soon, she took out a Call Artifact to pass down her orders, but,
“Do not bother.”

“Yrniel does not exist anymore.”

chapters.title: Chapter 2037: Godspark.
paragraphs: Chapter 2037: Godspark.
“Do you not hear yourself?
He loves them foolishly, he does not hide them.
Trust me,
Capturing them wouldn’t be difficult if you follow my plan.”
“What plan?”
Sharnoth questioned, and Zylarith’s grin widened even further.
“You plan on sending your subordinates to your subordinate worlds, correct?”
“Yes.”
“Discard that plan.”
“Huh?”
Sharnoth frowned.
“This is not the first time he is standing against me, girl.𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
Do you remember how your people were disappearing every minute 5,000 years ago?”
“Was that…”
Sharnoth’s expression changed.
“That was him.”
Zylarith nodded.
“I couldn’t sense his presence…”
Sharnoth finally realized it.
Soon, however, she noticed something odd,
“Wait, if you knew it was him, why didn’t you tell me?”
“I only figured it out when you told me about it. He was already long gone by then,”
Zylarith answered.
“But…”
“There was nothing we could have done. I was waiting for him to appear again; alerting you wouldn’t have made a difference.”
Sharnoth stayed silent.
Zylarith nodded at that and continued,

“What I am saying is, sending your subordinates wouldn’t make a difference. As you said, he is capable of taking care of Transcendents, he somehow has a strong grasp of the Power of Space, and he uses this power to first analyze his chances of success before making a move.

Even if you send Transcendents, if they are weaker than him, he will attack; if they are stronger, he will simply go look for another world. There are also chances he will directly attack your subordinates before they even get to the world they are meant to protect.
He is a hidden enemy, he has the advantage here.”
“This is what worries me.”
Sharnoth nodded with a grim look on her face.

In her previous encounter, she had learned just how monstrous that man was. If it weren’t for her revealing her true strength and ruining the spatial alignment of Khaemorr with Chaos, things could have become much worse than they are.
Nux’s powers were at a ridiculous level.
He was probably the trickiest Transcendent she had encountered in all her life.
“Use Portals.”
Zylarith suggested.
“Connect to your subordinate world through portals.”
“That would consume too many resources…”
Sharnoth answered. She had thought about it as well, but even this wasn’t a long-term solution. Because of how quick her growth was, one thing her Faction was lacking was money.
Or at least that is what she thought,
But…
“Don’t worry about the resources.”
Zylarith shook his head.
Then, he waved his hand, and suddenly, a storage ring appeared in front of Sharnoth.
The Queen frowned; Zylarith, on the other hand, continued,
“There are 20 million Portals in it. All you need to do is enter the worlds’ coordinates in them, and these Portals will teleport to the given coordinates and activate themselves.
That will allow you to form pathways between Khaemorr and the other worlds, giving you instant and safe access to all the worlds.”
“20 million?”
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow.
Honestly, she wasn’t exactly surprised. This wasn’t the first time her Master had done something like this. The number of resources—be it handy artifacts or even relics—he had was simply absurd.
Sharnoth had seen this man throw relics like they were waste. That was how big his treasury was.
He called it ‘System Space’.
And every time she tried to learn more about it, he just shook his head and refused to say anything.
“You have 12 more hours before he moves again; set this up.”
“It will be done.”
Sharnoth nodded.
It wasn’t like she had to set these up herself, she just needed to pass the order.
Zylarith nodded. He knew how efficient the girl was, so he didn’t say anything else and continued.
Another spherical artifact appeared in front of her, an artifact she had never seen before.

It floated in the air, humming with quiet, strange power. Its outer shell was a dark, glass-like web—semi-translucent and cracked, as if barely containing the storm within. There were runes all over its surface, constantly shifting and rewriting themselves.
At its core, what seemed like a miniature galaxy swirled. Different colors pulsed within it in an endless, almost hypnotic dance.
The moment the artifact appeared, the air around it warped subtly; it seemed like the artifact had the power to affect the very Laws of the world they were in.
Curious, Sharnoth stared at Zylarith, wanting an explanation.
“Godspark.”
And Zylarith gave her what she wanted.
“It has the power to mix one’s energy with the world’s energy.”
He explained, then looked into his disciple’s eyes and,
“Any world’s energy.”
“What…?”
Sharnoth’s expression changed.

“That child’s hold over the Power of Space is much greater than what most usually expect. He has the power to pass through the universal energy barrier and sense what is happening inside a world without having to actually be there.
With an ability like that, it doesn’t matter even if you use a Portal to send your men into those worlds; he will simply sense their existence and attack accordingly.
To avoid that, you will use Godspark.”
Sharnoth’s crimson eyes flickered with enlightenment, instantly understanding her Master’s plan.

“You will fill the Godspark with the Energy of Chaos and plant one of them in every world. The Godspark would then turn that world’s energy into Chaos energy. It would not only alter the spatial alignment of that world, even Time and other Primordial Energies will be affected as well.
It will become an entirely different place,
A battlefield where half of Nux’s tricks won’t work.”
“My subordinates will be the same. Their abilities won’t work properly either.”
Sharnoth mentioned the problem.
Zylarith, however, just grinned at that.
“It doesn’t matter.
His tricks are stronger.”
Sharnoth nodded in understanding.

With the world’s energy infested with chaos, normal abilities wouldn’t work. Most battles would turn into pure physical battles, and against a tricky opponent like Nux, who is more dependent on his abilities, physical battles would be much easier.
Sharnoth’s eyes shined, and a light, almost intractable grin appeared on her face. She finally had a way to trample the bug that had been annoying her all this while.
Just as she started thinking of her future plans after she gets rid of Nux, Zylarith spoke up,
“Now make sure you tell your men to not engage if they are up against Nux.”
“Huh…?”

chapters.title: Chapter 2038: Our priority is Nux.
paragraphs: Chapter 2038: Our priority is Nux.
“Now make sure you tell your men to not engage if they are up against Nux.”
“Huh…?”
Sharnoth’s expression changed.
Here she was, making arrangements for what to do after getting rid of Nux, but… her master wanted her men to not engage with Nux?
After everything they went through to create an environment where he would be weakened?
Was he… still worried about his son?
Sharnoth wondered for a split second. Soon, however, she shook her head.
Zylarith wasn’t the type to ‘worry’ about his son. Even if Nux was completely loyal to him, this man wouldn’t think for a second before sacrificing him if it meant he would get what he wanted.
Being worried about his son, or secretly caring for him—he was incapable of such thoughts.
Then…
Does Nux have something he wants? Is this why he is trying to protect him?
The Queen guessed.
“As I said, he is a tricky opponent. Most of your men wouldn’t be able to defeat him.”
“His tricks won’t work with the Chao—”
“It doesn’t matter.
I have underestimated him before and he surprised me. I will not make the same mistake again.
Predicting his movements is difficult. This is probably the only chance we will get.
Make it worth it.
Stick to the plan.”
Sharnoth’s face turned grim.
This was the first time she had seen her Master act like this. To think even the overly confident Progenitor of the Strongest Supreme World is being so cautious.
She couldn’t help but be more curious about Nux and what he could have possibly done for her master to react like this.
“Keep in your mind, our only target is one of his wives.”
Oblivious to her thoughts, Zylarith continued.
He then waved his hand and suddenly, around eleven projections appeared in front of Sharnoth.
“Remember these faces.”
Zylarith spoke.
“They are…”
“His wives.”
Yes, Zylarith was currently showing Nux’s wives’ pictures, and not just any wives—he was showing the weakest of them all.
“You will send two subordinates to every single world. Their strength would be similar to the leaders of those worlds. They will be Khaemorr’s support to the worlds in our Faction.

With Chaos spread all over those worlds, Nux’s perception won’t work. He and his subordinates would need to come to those worlds and fight both the World Leaders and your subordinates at the same time.

Your subordinates’ mission will be to activate the Call Artifact and summon you the instant Nux is seen. Of course, it will be great if they manage to do it—you will teleport there and capture them yourself—but most likely, Nux will get rid of them before that and they will die.
If that happens, you will drop the blame for the fallen world on the incompetent leaders who couldn’t even activate an artifact in front of the enemy.
Show your desperation to shift the blame while you do it. Show your subordinates how you are losing your composure with each passing day.
Create a pattern. Act like you are losing this battle,
But in truth, you are only waiting.
Waiting for Nux to let his guard down.”
“What then?”
Sharnoth questioned carefully.

“After he destroys a few more worlds over the next few days, he will see the pattern. He will understand that the aide you send to Lowest Level Worlds are only Sovereign Level Beings, the aide to a Low-Level World is a Primordial Level Being, and a Middle-Level World receives a Transcendent.
Once he and his wives confirm this pattern for a few days, his wives will make a move. They will come attack the worlds—and this is when you will strike.”
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes, listening intently.
“In some of the Low-Level Worlds, you will send not two, but five subordinates—two Primordials and three Transcendents.
However, even when the world is being attacked, these Transcendents will not move. They will leave the world and move to a different world.
The only time they will move is when they see one of the women I showed you.
With three Transcendents attacking them, capturing them alive will never be a problem. Once we have one of those women in our hands…”
Zylarith paused for a moment as a big, wide grin appeared on his face, and,
“Then the victory is ours.”
He announced. The Progenitor looked extremely proud of his plan.
Sharnoth, however, wasn’t very sure.
“What if those women do not appear?”
“They are desperate to prove themselves. They will appear.”
“And what if… he abandons his wives?”
“That will never happen.”
Zylarith sounded even more confident.
After all, this was a man who gave up on a certain path to success because he disrespected his wives.
He was a fool.
A fool who will fall because of his foolishness.
Sharnoth stared at Zylarith in silence.
Her eyes flickered with a slight hesitation. Soon, however, it was replaced by a determined look as she once again went through the entire plan.

“Changing a world’s energy into Energy of Chaos will harm that world. The Chaos will affect the denizens of those worlds, which in turn will cause more chaos, and the amount of Chaos Energy will only continue to increase.
It will mess up the entire world’s structure.
There is also the problem of the Supreme Worlds finding out about this.
If they find out that I am using the Energy of Chaos, it will be our end.”
She listed out the problems she could think of.
“It won’t happen.”
Zylarith shook his head.
“Those four have their own problems to worry about right now. As for the spreading Chaos, while it will make things a bit difficult for a while,
Once our mission is successful, I will give you the artifact to reverse what the Gospark did and return those worlds to their normal condition.
For now, stop thinking about this.
Our priority is Nux.
We need to stop him before he becomes a bigger threat than we can handle.”

They will leave the world and move to a different world.
The only time they will move is when they see one of the women I showed you.
With three Transcendents attacking them, capturing them alive will never be a problem.
Once we have one of those women in our hands…”
Zylarith paused for a moment as a big, wide grin appeared on his face, and,
“Then the victory is ours.”
He announced.
The Progenitor looked extremely proud of his plan.
Sharnoth, however, wasn’t very sure.
“What if those women do not appear?”
“They are desperate to prove themselves.
They will appear.”
“And what if… he abandons his wives?”
“That will never happen.”
Zylarith sounded even more confident.
After all, this was a man who gave up on a certain path to success because he disrespected his wives.
He was a fool.
A fool who will fall because of his foolishness.
Sharnoth stared at Zylarith in silence.
Her eyes flickered with a slight hesitation.
Soon, however, it was replaced by a determined look as she once again went through the entire plan.
“Changing a world’s energy into Energy of Chaos will harm that world.
The Chaos will affect the denizens of those worlds, which in turn will cause more chaos, and the amount of Chaos Energy will only continue to increase.
It will mess up the entire world’s structure.
There is also the problem of the Supreme Worlds finding out about this.
If they find out that I am using the Energy of Chaos, it will be our end.”
She listed out the problems she could think of.
“It won’t happen.”
Zylarith shook his head.
“Those four have their own problems to worry about right now.
As for the spreading Chaos, while it will make things a bit difficult for a while,
Once our mission is successful, I will give you the artifact to reverse what the Gospark did and return those worlds to their normal condition.
For now, stop thinking about this.
Our priority is Nux.
We need to stop him before he becomes a bigger threat than we can handle.”

chapters.title: Chapter 2039: Counter-Counter Attack.
paragraphs: Chapter 2039: Counter-Counter Attack.
While Zylarith and Sharnoth were busy commanding their subordinates, instructing them on how to use the artifacts they were providing and coming up with a plan to counter Nux,
The man responsible for such unrest was busy with something entirely different.

His body stirred slightly, his eyes were still closed, his body, however, could sense a familiar coldness beside him. A soft, delicate hand rested on his chest, his eyes opened on their own and he was greeted by the sight of Melia nestled in his arm, her long black hair spilling across the pillow.
She looked… serenely beautiful.
It was so ridiculously charming that on one side, Nux wanted to grab this woman and devour her, but on the other side, he wanted to continue watching her sleep.
Her breathing was calm and soft. So rhythmic that Nux felt lost in that rhythm, but suddenly, as if sensing Nux’s gaze, her eyes fluttered open.
She stared at her husband and very quickly, a slow, sleepy smile full of affection appeared on her face.
“Morning,”
She whispered in a light, sleepy voice.
“Morning,”
Nux replied, brushing a strand of hair from her face, wanting a full look and truly appreciating the beauty in front of him.
Unable to control himself, he wrapped his hands around her and pulled her close, feeling her cold body.
Melia’s smile became warmer, she too, pushed herself close to him, her fingers lightly tracing circles on his skin.
“You’re warm.”
She muttered.
“It feels good.
You did a good job as my personal heater.”
Nux chuckled at that and,
“Shouldn’t you reward me then?”
He obviously wouldn’t let go of this opportunity.
“Request what you want, I am feeling generous today.”
Melia’s reply came faster, it was almost as if she was expecting this.
“I thank you for your generosity.”
Nux’s grin widened, his canines elongated into fangs and,
Pierce
He started drinking her blood.
“Anh~”
Melia moaned ever so lightly, soon, her fangs appeared as well and,
Pierce
She bit back.

For the next few minutes, the couple’s bodies rolled over each other as they devoured each other. Only once they were satisfied did they finally stop, with Melia resting on top of Nux’s body while he continued to knead her body, holding her as if she was the most precious thing in the world.
After a minute-long silence where no party said anything,
“Are you going to do the same thing today?”
Melia opened her eyes again and looked up at him.
“Of course.”
Nux nodded, his tone casual but steady.
Melia stared at him for a moment and then,
“Do you think it’s working?”
She questioned.
“I know it is.”
Nux answered confidently as he kissed her forehead.
“It’s strange because we cannot directly see her reaction.”
Melia muttered softly.
This obviously wasn’t the first time she had experienced war. As a member of the Party ‘The one who does all the work and deserves to be rewarded’, she had participated in her fair share of them.
This, however, was the first time they were using such… cold tactics in the war.

Melia knew and understood fighting, killing, and blood, however, psychological warfare wasn’t her strongest suit. The fact that they could not see the effect of their actions made things much more difficult for her.
Yes, the Vampire was afraid…
They were up against a High-Level World, it was normal to feel intimidated.
Their enemy was stronger than them when it came to direct battle and this was worrisome.
But…
“Don’t worry.”
Nux, who understood her feelings, tightened his hug around her and assured her.

“The only being that is a threat to us is Sharnoth. It doesn’t matter if she is using Chaos to stop me from knowing what is happening in Khaemorr, she cannot protect and be present in all the worlds in her Faction at the same time.
There is nothing she can do,
Everything will go just as we expect it to.”
Yes, Nux was that confident.
And his confidence did reinforce Melia a little, she made herself more comfortable on top of him and closed her eyes.
“You know I need to leave, correct?”
Nux questioned.
It was time to attack the worlds again. He did this all at a fixed time to create a pattern, a way for the enemies to predict his actions, and while it did give his enemies a certain advantage,
It also built fear.
Especially when this matter explodes amongst the worlds in Sharnoth’s Faction.
‘It is time, who will be next?’
‘Will it be ours?’
‘What if it is us?’
‘What are we going to do?’
Such questions would keep them tense the moment the hour approached, the last-minute panic would spread even more chaos and fear.
It didn’t matter if these worlds got attacked or not, the fear they would feel would be nothing short of overwhelming.
Yes, this was Nux’s grand plan.
And for the first 3 days, he had left it to his subordinates to go and attack the selected worlds and did not interfere himself,
Later, however, things changed. Nux knew the enemy would retaliate in one way or the other, so he had taken matters into his own hands for the last five days,
And today, it finally happened.
“Huh?”
Nux, who was now standing in front of one of the target worlds, frowned as he realized something.
“The world’s infested with Chaos Energy, I cannot sense anything.”
He commented out loud.
“What are you going to do now?”
Melia questioned with a worried look on her face.
It wasn’t just this world that was infested with the Chaos Energy, all the worlds belonging to the Khaemorr Faction were the same.
The enemy had made their move and now,
The ball was in their court.
Any one of these worlds could have strong reinforcements capable of taking Nux down. Sure, the chances of them encountering such reinforcements were rare,
After all, only Sharnoth herself could actually take Nux on.
So basically, the chances of Nux being taken out were one out of millions, but Melia didn’t want to take that chance either.
After all, they had no clue what other tricks these people might have up their sleeves.
But then,
“Heh.”
Nux laughed.
“They acted much more swiftly than I expected.”
He admitted.
“But…
They did not consider my disposable pawns.”
Nux’s grin widened as he raised his hand and about fifteen Transcendents appeared around him.
“Attack.”
He ordered and without any hesitation,
Fifteen Transcendents were sent to a Lowest-Level World, ready to annihilate it through and through.
It was time for Counter-Counter Attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 2040: Why should I even keep you in my Council?
paragraphs: "Lady Sharnoth."
Varys walked into the Council Meeting. It was a sight that had become much more common in the Council, so much so that the Council Members did not even bat an eye at his entrance.
Not just the Council Members, Varys himself seemed to have gotten used to it. Heck, he had even stopped bothering with constantly reporting the fall of different worlds every single day.
Ten worlds from their Faction falling every single day had become a monotonous trend, something that Varys would rather have his subordinate report than waste time himself.
The reason he came here was something different,
Something bigger.
"Vladnir has declared neutrality."
He reported, and in an instant, the unbothered Council Members reacted.
"Vladnir...?"
Their expressions turned grim, even Sharnoth was no exception. This was even bigger than the first time a Lowest Level World had decided to abandon their faction.
Yes, with Nux constantly targeting the worlds belonging to their faction, it was only a matter of time before the word spread.

The aid Sharnoth had prepared didn’t work either. Everything she had done, from forming the portals, infesting the worlds’ energy with chaos, and sending her subordinates to different worlds, nothing had worked.
The subordinates they sent were all killed because the enemies were stronger. Even the stronger party, which consisted of Transcendents and was meant to target Nux’s wives, did not come back.
Let alone catching his wives, it seemed that those people ended up becoming a target instead, as more and more worlds with the Transcendent Level reinforcements started being attacked.

Of course, Sharnoth did try to use this opportunity and go together with the reinforcement in order to catch Nux or his wives, but every time she did it, Khaemorr was attacked instead, and she was forced to return.
Yes, even when she had used Chaos energy to prevent Nux from being able to sense anything inside Khaemorr, he knew exactly when she was gone.
Meaning there were spies working for him in Khaemorr.
Sharnoth was betrayed.
And what’s worse?
She could not find the traitor.
It was frustrating.

Not just that, since things had gotten this bad and Sharnoth’s large-scale operation of defending the worlds under her had failed so miserably, the matter regarding Nux and the Leander Family had spread like fire as well.

Almost every world under her Faction found out about them, and very quickly, panic spread. So much so that on a certain day, one of the Lowest Level Worlds declared neutrality, breaking all ties with Khaemorr.
Yes, the Lowest Level World went ahead and broke all ties with a High-Level World. It was something that had never happened in the history of the Universe.
Yet...
Now it had happened.
The matter attracted a lot of attention. The Lowest World itself gathered a lot of attention as well. Many thought it would soon be targeted and destroyed, but...
It survived.
The Leander Family did not attack because it had no connection with Khaemorr anymore. They even left a note mentioning the world’s name, ensuring they would not target them.

One would think that Khaemorr should have destroyed that world instead, but Sharnoth had a reputation to maintain as well. She couldn’t exactly destroy the world just because it left its Faction and cut all ties with them—at least not in the open.
The rest of the Powers didn’t bother. They were very much satisfied by being simple observers of this interesting game.
The Lowest Level World had ensured its survival, at least for now.
And that was all the push the others needed.
A week after that, more and more Lowest and then Low-Level Worlds started breaking ties with Khaemorr, abandoning the Faction.

It was something Sharnoth didn’t pay much attention to. It was regrettable, yes, but it wasn’t like the Lowest or Low-Level Worlds held that much importance. They were weak. They had no role in the bigger scheme of things, other than serving as cannon fodder.
Now, however, things were different.
Vladnir wasn’t a Lowest or Low-Level World,
It was a Middle-Level World.
And in the battle between High-Level Worlds and their Factions, the Middle-Level Worlds matter a lot.
If the fact that a Middle-Level World has left the Faction spreads...
More and more Middle-Level Worlds will start leaving, and while one wouldn’t make much difference, if the number continues to increase...
Then Aurendor would definitely find a way to use it to their advantage.
This... was bad.
"Why?"
Maeve questioned.
"Why did Vladnir declare neutrality? Did they give any reason?"
"They did not."
Varys shook his head.
"This isn’t a coincidence. The Leander Family started targeting Middle Level Worlds four days ago and now they have left. Even a child could tell what’s happening here."
Siara commented.
"Can you blame them? Eight Middle-Level Worlds under us have perished, and in exchange, we haven’t gotten our hands on anything.
The only time we ’succeeded’ was when Lady Sharnoth captured one of the Leander Family’s subordinates, but when we tried to read his memory, we only saw a blank.
The bastard did not remember anything. Even his cultivation had magically disappeared. It was almost as if he was abandoned by the very Universe."
Maeve then glanced at Sharnoth and,
"I have said it before, I will say it again, Your Majesty.
They need to be stopped.
If this continues, things will take a worse, far worse turn."
The Nocthari spoke with a solemn tone and this time, none of the Council Members said anything against her words.
They all realized how dire the situation was.
Even Sharnoth.
The Queen looked into Maeve’s eyes and,
"And how do you suggest I do that?"
She questioned. Her voice was full of coldness and intimidation she rarely displayed.
Maeve, however, wasn’t affected by that gaze.
"I do not know."
She merely shook her head.
"So you do not know?"
"I do not."
"That’s quite an easy answer, don’t you think?
You have been constantly telling me how I need to deal with him, yet never once did you suggest anything useful. Doesn’t that make you useless?
Why should I even keep you in my Council?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2041: Aurendor’s Actions.
paragraphs: "That’s quite an easy answer, don’t you think?
You have been constantly telling me how I need to deal with him, yet never once did you suggest anything useful. Doesn’t that make you useless?
Why should I even keep you in my Council?"

Sharnoth snapped, surprising the rest of her Council Members. None of them had seen her react like this before. Yes, there were times when the Queen had gotten angry, but never because someone counselled her.
Also, this wasn’t the first time Maeve did it. The Nocthari was always quick to call out if she didn’t like how things were playing out, and most of the time, she was correct.
Even Sharnoth herself took her words seriously and acted on them.
But...
For the Queen to react like this...
The Council Members were intimidated—well, everyone but Maeve herself. The woman was incapable of feeling such emotions, after all.
Even in this situation, she stayed logical.
"You keep me in the Council because I speak my mind, and when I do, it benefits you."𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
She answered in a straightforward manner, and she wasn’t done.

"Ever since I joined you, I rarely gave you the solution to the problem. I admit, that is not my strong suit, especially when compared to you, who has a knack for finding creative solutions to the problems we have faced before.
I have only been useful in detecting the problem before it became too big, which I did this time around as well—just that you have yet to solve this problem."
Silence.
Absolute silence fell in the Council Room.
Sharnoth glared at the Nocthari, Nocthari stared back. She could tell that her words had offended the Queen. However, she also knew the Queen wouldn’t do anything.
The Queen simply lost her calm for a moment, but she wasn’t the type to take her anger out on her subordinates.
And once again, the Nocthari was correct.
Sharnoth closed her eyes for a moment and then,
"Send our men to Vladnir, remove the Godspark, free them of the Chaotic Energy, and take the Teleportation Portal back.
From this day forth, Vladnir has nothing to do with Khaemorr."
"As you command, My Queen."
Varys nodded.
Sharnoth nodded and,
"You are dismissed."
She dismissed the meeting.
Once again, it surprised the Council Members. After all, there were still a few more matters to discuss. Maeve even glanced at Sharnoth and was about to say something but,
"You are dismissed."
The Queen repeated herself, and in an instant, the Meeting Room was emptied.
Sharnoth, now left alone, clenched her trembling fists in anger.
"Two months..."
She muttered out loud.
"It has been two months since I have been following your plan. All this time, I have been waiting patiently for your trap to work and getting my hands on one of his wives and yet...
Nothing.
I have got nothing."
The Queen spoke in a low, calm voice. Her overflowing anger, however, could still be sensed.
"Be patient, Sharnoth."
Zylarith spoke calmly.
"Patient?"
"Yes."
"A total of 614 worlds have perished, 30 worlds have left my Faction, and you want me to be patient...?"
"It is a necessary sacrifice."
Zylarith didn’t flinch.
"I told you before, that child is a tricky opponent, but be patient. He is winning, and he knows it. This is the moment he would let his guard down.
His wives have held themselves back, but this wouldn’t continue. I have met those women. They are arrogant, and they do unnecessary things to prove themselves and help him.
They will come."
The Old Soul was confident.
Sharnoth, not so much.
She still had doubts.
It was frustrating how she was completely helpless in this situation.
The only thing she could do was rely on her Master’s plan.

"They declared that they have formed an alliance with the Leander Family. The Leander Family has agreed to become their Secret Weapon that will purge theEvilfrom the Universe."
"What...?"
Sharnoth’s crimson eyes shined with endless rage and hatred.
Once again, Varys flinched.
But...
The report was long, and every single piece of information in it was important. He had to do his job.
"This has given the Leander Family a base and has spread the matter farther than it already had.
Aurendor has also decided to take in any world that hasrealized their wrongdoings and has cut ties with Khaemorrinto their Faction.

paragraphs: "Send men to Ravenhelm, Sevenruin, and Zarenal,
Wipe those traitors off the Universe’s face."
Sharnoth ordered with a cold look on her face, and Varys... his eyes widened in horror.
"...what?"

He couldn’t help but question, thinking that he was mistaken. Sharnoth may be cruel, but she had never once taken her anger out on her subordinates. Even when the Lowest and Low-Level Worlds declared neutrality, she did not do anything against them and simply abandoned those worlds as they wanted her to.
"Declaring neutrality because they felt threatened was one thing, but to act when the enemy offered them asylum—
That is a betrayal.
And Khaemorr does not forgive traitors."
Sharnoth declared, her crimson eyes shining coldly.
"...yes, My Queen."
Varys muttered as he bowed his head, ready to carry out the order given.
He didn’t particularly care about some Middle-Level Worlds but...
The problem was far above that.

Once this happens, the matter will blow up even more than it has now. Panic will surge even further. Sure, the Worlds under them won’t declare neutrality after knowing what happened to the three who did, but the unity and support they previously had will die down.
Cracks will now appear in their Faction.
Cracks wide enough for other Factions to bear their fangs. The Aurendor Faction will use this to weaken them even further.
Their fall will appear closer, and others will sense an opportunity. It wouldn’t be surprising if another High World Faction joined in the fray and allied themselves with Aurendor as well.
With two High-Level World Factions as their enemies, it will only be a matter of time that...
"Varys."
While Varys was thinking all this, Sharnoth called with a solemn look on her face.
"Yes, Your Majesty?"
Varys quickly suppressed his thoughts and tilted his head, waiting to see how he could assist the Queen.
"Maeve, what world was she assigned to? And which Portal was her world connected to?"
"A Low-Level World, Raguel, Portal ACR53."
"What about Portal ZRZ89? What world is that connected to?"
"Lowest-Level World, Dars."
"What’s special about Dars?"
Sharnoth questioned, and at that question, Varys frowned in confusion.
"Nothing in particular, it is merely a Lowest-Level World..."
Despite his confusion, he answered what came to his mind. Soon, however, as if he recalled something, he glanced at his Queen and,
"It is not of much significance since we now have Portals connected to every world in our Faction, but Dars is the world furthest away from Khaemorr.
Even with our fastest Travellers, it would take about 38 days to get there."
Just as he said those words, Sharnoth clenched her fists in anger. Her cold expression turned even colder.
As Khaemorr’s only leader, Khaemorr’s Will told her everything happening in it. With one wish, Sharnoth could tell where whoever was.
And Maeve...
Maeve went through Portal ZRZ89.
She went to Dars.
And if Sharnoth had any more doubts, suddenly, the Portal ZRZ89 lost its light.
It meant that the Portal was destroyed from the other side, making it impossible for them to access Dars.
Maeve...
She had escaped.
"Your Majesty?"
Varys called out because of Sharnoth’s long silence.
Sharnoth glanced at him in silence.

She knew she couldn’t reveal it. Maeve was one of the most influential Council Members. If it was revealed that someone like her had escaped, her people would start to panic, and more would try to escape.
"Gather all the Council Members for the Council Meeting."
Sharnoth ordered.
Varys frowned.
"You just dismissed them."
"And I am telling you to gather them again. Summon those who have gone to their assigned worlds back."
"As you command, my Queen."
Varys bowed his head as he walked out of the room.
"What happened?"
After Varys left, Zylarith, who could sense the change in Sharnoth’s expression, questioned as he floated around her.
"Maeve left."
"The Nocthari?"
Zylarith raised his eyebrow; he didn’t seem particularly surprised.
"It is just like them."
He snickered.
"Fools who do not possess emotions, of course they will be the first ones to betray their masters."

"The strongest Nocthari under me leaving my side isn’t a good sign. Nocthari does not feel fear, they do not panic, they only think with logic no matter the situation. If she left, it means that she already thinks the war is lost.
Logic is not on my side."
Sharnoth spoke with a solemn look on her face.
"And?"
Zylarith, however, just laughed.
"When you escaped Aurendor, survived, and became as strong as you are now, was logic on your side?
Would any Nocthari have supported you just after you escaped Aurendor?"
Sharnoth stared at her master in silence.
"Logic is not absolute. If it was, the Noctharis wouldn’t be a fallen race clinging to you for their revival.
Logic only forms according to what one knows, and what one knows amounts to nothing compared to millions of other different, incomprehensible factors.
Logic merely limits you.
So stop hanging onto the thoughts of a traitor. Just remember her face, and once you come out victorious,
Show her the price of betraying you."
Zylarith spoke as a cruel light shined in his eyes.
Sharnoth was momentarily taken aback. Soon, however, another question appeared in her mind,
"What should I do?"

Everything they had done so far was all for nought. With how things are progressing, in about a month, another High-Level Faction will join in. And while taking on two Eternal-Level Beings wouldn’t be difficult for her,
It would be the end for her weakened Faction.
She will be left alone and isolated from the Universe. She would lose everything she had built this far. As for her revenge...
Her enemy would have too much power by then.
It would be impossible for her to get her revenge.
At least... that was how she thought it would play out.
But,
"Get stronger."
Zylarith spoke up with a big grin on his face as suddenly, a black-purple football-sized crystal appeared in the air,
"Absorb this, get stronger, and destroy the enemy you have hated all your life."
"What is it?"
"Crystallization of all the Chaos I have gathered ever since I raised you. I intended to give it to you once I was sure it would help you break through to Infinity Stage.
But since things have come this far,
I have no other choice.
If not Infinity, then be Pseudo-Infinity instead.
We will figure out the rest later."

chapters.title: Chapter 2043: The one who escaped.
paragraphs: While Sharnoth, her World, her Faction, and everything connected to her was falling apart and was desperately trying to think of a way out,

The being responsible for it was sitting cross-legged with his eyes closed. The ground beneath him was covered with soft, purple grass. The wind brushed through his black hair, carrying a dry, strange scent.
The sky above was wide and bright, painted with three suns that shined brightly. Tall trees with purple leaves swayed gently in the breeze, their trunks glowing faintly with natural energy.

It was a beautiful land—wildflowers bloomed in strange colors, and crystal-clear lakes shimmered in the distance. Giant floating stones drifted lazily across the sky, birds with feathered tails of light soaring between them.
But something felt wrong.
Something felt... chaotic.
Yes, this world was infested with the Energy of Chaos, the energy that Nux had been trying to comprehend all this while but...
"Did it work?"
Suddenly, a beautiful blonde elf appeared behind him and sat next to him.
"I told you to be careful, did I not? Where have you been?"
Nux questioned as he rested his head on the elf’s lap.
"Nowhere, I was just looking around."
Evane chuckled, gently playing with Nux’s hair.
"I still cannot extend my senses beyond a certain limit, so don’t move. Things might take a dangerous turn when reinforcements arrive through the Portal."
"I was careful, don’t worry."
"Were you?"
Nux raised his eyebrow, and in the end, Evane decided to change the topic.
"So you still haven’t comprehended Chaos, have you?"
Nux stared at this beautiful and adorable woman in silence. He knew what she was trying to do, but he couldn’t bring himself to be angry at her. He just gave in and decided to let go,
"It is not easy."
He muttered, answering the Elf’s question instead.

He looked around and observed the thick, heavy, purple-black energy pulsing in the air. The energy looked like fog, but it didn’t move with the wind. It twisted and shifted on its own as if it were alive.
It was the Energy of Chaos that this world was infested with.
Yes, they were currently in one of the Lowest Level worlds that belonged to Khaemorr’s Faction.

Nux had already enslaved the Leaders of this world 3 weeks ago. The reinforcements sent here met the same end, and ever since that day, Nux had spent most of his time in this world, trying to comprehend the Energy of Chaos and form a Law related to it.
"It is like forming a Law related to light by staring at a light source, or a Law related to Darkness by staring at darkness.
It is not a very practical approach."
"Then why even do it?"
Evane spoke as her hand gently held Nux’s, with their fingers crossed with each other. Nux’s thumb moved on its own as he gently rubbed the back of her hand.
"It is quite interesting, this Energy of Chaos."
Nux answered.
"It is literally what its name says, Chaos.
Be it Time, Space, or anything else, it has affected it all. It has rendered all abilities useless—even expanding my senses to know what’s around me has become difficult.
It has been a while since I’ve had to just rely on my eyes to know what’s around me."
"Well, you do have what you call cameras installed all over the world, do you not?"
Evane questioned.

Yes, since he couldn’t use his senses, Nux decided to create cameras and install them all around the world to make sure nothing out of the ordinary happened. Just the Portal alone had around 20 cameras ready to alert Nux the moment anything happened in the area.
"Well, that’s more like a temporary artifact. If it is destroyed, I’ll lose the footage of that place. It is still not as good as enveloping the entire world with my senses.
Even after trying it for a month, I have only been able to expand my senses to 50 meters. It is a pathetically low number."
Nux sighed.
"It is indeed quite a unique energy."
Evane nodded.
"Even the world we are in is plunged into chaos."

"How could it not? Most abilities aren’t working. Beings with higher physical powers have come to power, but even they aren’t absolute either since Chaos made it impossible to detect enemies around. Assassinations run rampant, people cannot cultivate—it is a disaster.
There were more deaths here in the past three weeks than in the last 10 years.
What’s worse?
Because of all the chaos this is creating, the amount of Chaos Energy is increasing, strengthening these effects even further.
It’s an already strong energy with the power to strengthen itself with time.
That is what the Energy of Chaos is."
Evane nodded in silence.
Honestly, it made her nervous that the enemy possessed such strong energy, but she trusted her husband and didn’t say anything out loud.
Rather, she just tightened her hold on Nux’s arm as her other hand continued to play with his hair.
’Lord Nux.’
While Nux was enjoying the moment of peace with his wife, a subordinate called.
’What is it?’
’You should come here.’
Nux raised his eyebrow, somewhat curious.
He stood up and with Evane in his arms, he flew out of the world he was in and teleported in front of the world he was called to.

It was a Lowest Level World similar to the one he was in. Without thinking any further, he entered that world. Since this world was infested with Chaos Energy as well, he couldn’t teleport once inside.
From here, he had to move on his own.
’Where are you?’
He questioned.
’Near the tallest building.’
The Subordinate answered.

In about 15 minutes, Nux found his subordinate, who was sitting in front of 20 screens, all showing a destroyed Portal from different angles. One screen in particular, however, was showing something else,
A dark-haired woman surrounded by Nux’s subordinates, a woman Nux recognized in an instant,
"Maeve, eh?
Since she destroyed the Portal, it must mean the Nocthari escaped."
A small smile appeared on Nux’s face,
"This is fun~"
Yes, he decided to move.

Evane spoke as her hand gently held Nux’s, with their fingers crossed with each other.
Nux’s thumb moved on its own as he gently rubbed the back of her hand.
"It is quite interesting, this Energy of Chaos."
Nux answered.
"It is literally what its name says, Chaos.
Be it Time, Space, or anything else, it has affected it all.
It has rendered all abilities useless—even expanding my senses to know what’s around me has become difficult.
It has been a while since I’ve had to just rely on my eyes to know what’s around me."
"Well, you do have what you call cameras installed all over the world, do you not?"
Evane questioned.
Yes, since he couldn’t use his senses, Nux decided to create cameras and install them all around the world to make sure nothing out of the ordinary happened.
Just the Portal alone had around 20 cameras ready to alert Nux the moment anything happened in the area.
"Well, that’s more like a temporary artifact.
If it is destroyed, I’ll lose the footage of that place.
It is still not as good as enveloping the entire world with my senses.
Even after trying it for a month, I have only been able to expand my senses to 50 meters.
It is a pathetically low number."
Nux sighed.
"It is indeed quite a unique energy."
Evane nodded.
"Even the world we are in is plunged into chaos."
"How could it not?
Most abilities aren’t working.
Beings with higher physical powers have come to power, but even they aren’t absolute either since Chaos made it impossible to detect enemies around.
Assassinations run rampant, people cannot cultivate—it is a disaster.
There were more deaths here in the past three weeks than in the last 10 years.
What’s worse?
Because of all the chaos this is creating, the amount of Chaos Energy is increasing, strengthening these effects even further.
It’s an already strong energy with the power to strengthen itself with time.
That is what the Energy of Chaos is."
Evane nodded in silence.
Honestly, it made her nervous that the enemy possessed such strong energy, but she trusted her husband and didn’t say anything out loud.
Rather, she just tightened her hold on Nux’s arm as her other hand continued to play with his hair.
’Lord Nux.’
While Nux was enjoying the moment of peace with his wife, a subordinate called.
’What is it?’
’You should come here.’
Nux raised his eyebrow, somewhat curious.
He stood up and with Evane in his arms, he flew out of the world he was in and teleported in front of the world he was called to.
It was a Lowest Level World similar to the one he was in.
Without thinking any further, he entered that world.
Since this world was infested with Chaos Energy as well, he couldn’t teleport once inside.
From here, he had to move on his own.
’Where are you?’
He questioned.
’Near the tallest building.’
The Subordinate answered.
In about 15 minutes, Nux found his subordinate, who was sitting in front of 20 screens, all showing a destroyed Portal from different angles.
One screen in particular, however, was showing something else,
A dark-haired woman surrounded by Nux’s subordinates, a woman Nux recognized in an instant,
"Maeve, eh?
Since she destroyed the Portal, it must mean the Nocthari escaped."
A small smile appeared on Nux’s face,
"This is fun~"
Yes, he decided to move.

chapters.title: Chapter 2044: Surrender
paragraphs: "Are you from the Leander Family?"
Maeve questioned calmly as she stared at the Transcendent in front of her.
"Surrender."
The Transcendent spoke with an expressionless look on his face.
"You did not answer my ques—"
Before Maeve could even complete her sentence, the Transcendent rushed towards her and punched.

The Nocthari waved her hand with a calm look on her face, expecting a lethal gas to surround and devour him. The gas she summoned, however, was summoned 10 meters away from where she intended it to be.
The Transcendent got close to her and,
Bam
Maeve was sent flying.
The Transcendent didn’t give her the chance to recover either; he carried forward, prepared to hit her again.
Maeve, on the other hand, quickly understood the situation and took out her sword.
She had forgotten about it for a moment—using abilities with the Power of Chaos infesting this place was foolish.
She needed to escape.
But...
It wasn’t simple.
Maeve knew this man wouldn’t let her go.
"Tsk."
The Nocthari snorted in annoyance.
She could sense it—the man wasn’t exactly strong. If she could use her powers without any restrictions, taking him down wouldn’t have been so difficult.
However, as someone who was heavily reliant on her powers and rarely participated in close combat, she was at a disadvantage.
This, however, was only the beginning, as suddenly, four more Transcendents landed around her, surrounding her in an instant.
Maeve paused.
She was surrounded, and there was no way she would be able to deal with five Transcendents without her powers.
Instead of a victory, she needed a way out.
She looked around, her mind trying to come up with a strategy to leave this world. If she succeeded and managed to get out of Chaos Energy’s influence, allowing her to use her ability, she might win.
20 seconds.
She calculated in her head.
That was all she needed, and her mind was constantly thinking of a way to get away from these people for just 20 seconds.
’What if I get punched, use that momentum to create distance from them and run from ther—’
While Maeve was trying to come up with a battle plan, suddenly,
"I didn’t think you of all people would be resisting, Maeve Nocthar."
A voice was heard.
Maeve turned towards the voice with a frown and saw a black-haired, golden-eyed man—a being she recognized very quickly.
How could she not?
He was the reason all of this had happened in the first place.
"Nux Leander..."
She muttered.
"You know me."
Nux smiled.
Soon, however, he just shrugged,
"Then again, almost everyone in Khaemorr knows me.
Haaah...
It is not easy getting used to this fame."
The man sighed.
Maeve, however, didn’t react to his antics.
"Why are you here, Nux Leander?"
She questioned directly.
"Nothing much, I had my men surround the worlds furthest away from Khaemorr in case I find a few deserters.
I just didn’t think I would catch the strongest Nocthari out of all people.
I guess logic sometimes makes one too predictable, huh?"

Maeve stayed silent. She did not feel embarrassed because, well, she couldn’t. But she did acknowledge her error. She was so focused on escaping before Sharnoth lost her patience and the War that she completely ignored the enemy.
"Surrender.
There is no way out."
Nux spoke as he walked towards the Nocthari.
Again, Maeve stayed silent.
Surrendering was the last option; she still believed that she had a better fighting chance if she managed to somehow leave Dar’s perimeter.
But...
"You still think you can escape, huh..."
Nux paused.
This was the Nocthari’s weakness. They were simply too predictable. Maeve’s slight pause was all Nux needed to understand what she was thinking, and as if to crush whatever slight resistance she had,
Nux waved his hand and his shadow trembled. 50 more beings materialized from his shadow and...
All 50 of them were Transcendents.
Maeve was taken aback.
"Still think you can escape?"
Nux questioned with a playful look on his face.
"How did they come here? It should be impossible to use powers related to space because of the Chaos Energy."
The Nocthari questioned, and Nux just smiled at those words.
The Energy of Chaos was strong, yes, but... it was still the energy of a different Universe; it had no power over Nux’s own Universe.
Nux here wasn’t manipulating Space, he was simply summoning his subordinates using his Universe’s Power. The Energy of Chaos or any other energy held no power over it.
Of course, there was no need to reveal all this to someone else,
"I will say this one last time, Nocthari.
There is no way out.
Surrender."
Maeve stared at the Transcendents surrounding her, blocking all her escape routes, and after a second, she closed her eyes,
"Are you going to recruit me or use me as a prisoner?"
She questioned. She knew he wasn’t going to kill her, because she would already be dead if that were the case, so these two were the only things that came to her mind.
"I will recruit you."
Nux answered.
"But I will ensure your loyalty to me."
"How will you do that?"
"You do not have to worry about it.
Stay put."
Nux spoke as he extended his hand. Dense, black mist came out and surrounded the Nocthari.𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦
Yes, he was going to devour her.
Even if that allowed the Universe to make a link between him and Khaemorr, he didn’t back down—the risk was worth it.

After all, having a Nocthari completely loyal to you on your side was very useful. She could even be the Leader of all his Transcendent subordinates, allowing him to create an independent unit which he wouldn’t have to give all the directions to.
The only thing he needed was to alter her mind in a way that she saw his existence above that of logic.
’Shadow.’
He called out, ready to leave and recruit a useful subordinate,
But then—
Bzzz
A certain artifact in his storage ring buzzed.
’Oh?’
An artifact that he didn’t expect to activate any time soon.
Yes, it was Sharnoth Nocthys.

chapters.title: Chapter 2045: A way to prove my words.
paragraphs: Just as Nux was prepared to leave,
Bzzz
’Oh?’
The Call Artifact he didn’t think would activate anytime soon buzzed.
It was the Artifact he had given to Sharon Nocthys.
’This looks much more interesting.’
Shadow chuckled.
It wasn’t just her, the rest of the women gathered together as well, interested in what was going to happen.
Nux, sensing their excitement, laughed as he then picked the call and a familiar face appeared in front of him.
"It has been a while, Lady Sharnoth."
He greeted with his signature smile.
"I must admit, I didn’t think you would call this soon."
Sharnoth stared at Nux in silence.

Nux did the same. Seeing as how the only thing around her was the black-purple nebula of energy and no walls, ceiling, floor, or anything else could be seen, Nux realized that she had already activated her domain.
Just like he had requested in their first meeting.
"I take it that you are finally prepared to have a conversation now."
Nux muttered, his smile much wider than before, almost resembling a demon who had successfully tricked an innocent woman and trapped her in his schemes.
His smile made Sharnoth uncomfortable, but she didn’t show anything on her expressionless face.
"Just out of curiosity though, where is he? My ’dear’ father."
"...he escaped."
Sharnoth answered with a hesitant look on her face.
"What...?"
Nux’s expression changed.
"When I activated my domain, he escaped."
"And you want me to believe that?"
Nux narrowed his eyes.

Sharnoth was one of, if not the strongest Eternal Level Beings in this entire Universe. It was pretty much impossible to escape from her domain as long as she does not want you to. That was simply how quick her reflexes were.
Sure, that Soul Father of his was once the Progenitor of the Strongest World in this Universe. He himself was probably one of the strongest beings in existence.𝒻𝑟ℯℯ𝑤𝑒𝑏𝑛𝘰𝓋𝑒𝓁.𝒸𝑜𝘮

But right now, he was nothing more than a shadow of his former self. He was extremely weakened, so much so that just activating a bit of his remaining power was enough for the Universe to react and devour him.
Someone like Zylarith should never be able to escape Sharnoth. The woman could simply will it, and he would be powerless in her domain.
"I thought you would be much more open for an honest conversation since this is the second time you contacted me, but I guess I wa—"
"I tried to capture him, but when I did capture it, I realized that he was never with me to begin with. It was just his projection made from an artifact I had never seen before."
Sharnoth answered.
"What...?"
"I know you do not believe me, especially considering everything that has happened between us so far,
So I came up with a way,
A way to prove my words."
Nux raised his eyebrow, interested.
"Carry on."
He nodded, letting the woman continue, and after a brief pause,
The woman took out an artifact made of twisted silver, thin like old tree roots. Seven sharp blue gems stuck out from the top.
Nux frowned, and as if knowing what he was thinking, Sharnoth continued.
"This is the Crown of Chronicles, an Artifact that reads one’s memories."
Nux narrowed his eyes at those words. Sharnoth, however, just stared at him with a determined look on her face and,
"I will wear this, and within a few minutes, it will record all my memories from the time I was born. You can then have this artifact and watch my memories however you wish.
The Artifact will protect your mind from being overwhelmed by my memories. You can skip the parts you wish to skip and see what you wish to see.
With this, I will no longer have anything to hide from you. You will understand not only my position, but my state of mind.
And once you do,
You will realize that I have no intentions of betraying you as long as I get what I want."
"You want me to... read your memories?"
Nux questioned, a little taken aback.
This offer was... quite desperate.
"This is the only way I can think of that will make you trust my words."
Sharnoth answered with a straight face.
"Why the complete memory? Why not show me the time when you activated your domain and realized that my Father was a projection?"
"As I said, once you see it, you will not only understand my position but also my state of mind. You will realize what I am doing and for what I am doing it for,
You will understand what is important for me and what is not."
Sharnoth then took a small pause and,
"You will understand what I want and how desperately I want it,
And with this, you will understand how to... use me as a pawn in whatever game you are playing."
Nux blinked, unable to believe what he was hearing.
One of the strongest Eternals in the entire Universe... was reducing herself into a mere pawn...?
No matter how he thought about it, it made no sense.
"Also, I am showing you the entire thing because a small piece of memory can be fabricated."
"And your entire life cannot?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.
"I do not have the time to fabricate more than a hundred thousand years of memories."
Sharnoth answered directly, and knowing that he was not convinced,

"This is the only way I have. If you want, you can use any other artifact to read my memories, an artifact that you can trust. I would even ask you to come here and read my memories on your own like you read my subordinates’, but I understand why you would want to avoid that."
Nux turned silent.
In all honesty, this wasn’t an offer he could ignore.
Having an Eternal Level Being as a pawn...
Just thinking of the number of possibilities it opens up filled him with excitement. Without waiting any further,
"Alright then,"
He nodded.
With a wave of his hand, the Energy of Genesis was activated, and a new artifact shaped similar to the Crown of Chronicles was formed.
It was time to read the Queen’s memories.

chapters.title: Chapter 2046: The Sovereign has fallen.
paragraphs: "This is the Soul’s Crown."
Nux began, pointing at the artifact he had just created using the Power of Genesis as the base and his other racial memory-reading powers that he had devoured a long time ago.

"It is a delicate artifact that will read and record the wearer’s memories. When you wear it, keep in mind that you must not activate any form of energy. The moment you so much as move your energy, the crown will break.
Not just that, the Crown will automatically detect your age before it starts reading your memories, and if the amount of memories it stores is either higher or lower than your age, it will break."
"That is a good way of preventing any false memory implantation."
Sharnoth nodded. Not being able to use her energy and the limitation of having no extra or fewer memories than one’s age would make it almost impossible for any being to trick the artifact.
Nux just nodded.

Of course, he hadn’t reached a level where his creations would work on Eternal-Level Beings, but it wasn’t difficult to create a memory-recording artifact if the one whose memories are being read allows it.
"Remove your domain and the Chaos Energy from Khaemorr."

He instructed. Sharnoth nodded and did what she was told. Meanwhile, Nux teleported and appeared somewhere near Khaemorr. Of course, he still hid his location from Sharnoth. Even though the woman was being submissive, he still did not let his guard down.
His wives that were with him had already returned to his Universe.
In about a minute, the Chaos Energy that had mixed with Khaemorr’s Mana disappeared completely, allowing Nux to once again sense the entire world and use his Space Law to its fullest extent.
He sensed Sharnoth’s location and activated his Space Law. He teleported the Soul’s Crown right in front of her.
Sharnoth stared at the artifact in awe. The Power over Space was as strong and useful as it was before.
Slowly, Sharnoth grabbed the Crown and wore it just like she was told to.

The jewel on the Crown activated. Sharnoth closed her eyes, sensing the energy that had entered her body. She also felt that she could restrict this energy and even manipulate it because of how weak the energy was, but she very quickly realized that the energy was very deeply connected to the crown she was wearing.
The moment it was restricted or manipulated, the Crown would break.
’So that is what he meant...’
She nodded inwardly.

The artifact did its thing, recording Sharnoth’s deep-rooted memories from the time she was born. Since Nux wasn’t exactly an expert when it came to building things, the artifact wasn’t as fast as the Crown of Chronicles that Sharnoth had offered to use.

Instead of a few minutes, this artifact needed about 16 hours to record Sharnoth’s complete memory, and only once it was done did the last of the seven gems light up, signaling that everything was successful.
Sharnoth opened her eyes. To someone like her, 16 hours wasn’t a big deal. She just stared at Nux, who seemed to be cultivating while drifting in space as well.
"It is done."
She spoke.
Hearing her voice through the artifact, Nux finally opened his eyes. He nodded as he stared at the seven lit-up gems.
